 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to

(NAPS) to establishments in Andhra Pradesh during 2024-25 and 2025-26, year-wise;

Konaseema and Parvathipuram Manyam recorded low or zero enrolments under the Scheme in

THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  
 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) was launched in August 2016. 
Thescheme was extended to continue as NAPS -2 from FY 2022 -23. Under, NAPS 2.0, the

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
 
LOK SABHA

ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
 
PROMOTION OF FOLK ARTS AND CULTURAL TRADITIONS OF WESTERN ODISHA 
 
 
1262.    SMT. SANGEETA KUMARI SINGH DEO: 
         
Will the MINISTER OF CULTURE be pleased to state: 
   
(a) the details of financial assistance provided by the Government for the promotion of folk art, folk 
music, folk dance and traditional theatre in Odisha during the last five years, district-wise; 
 
(b) whether artists and cultural organisations from Balangir have received grants or financial 
assistance from the Government during the said period and, if so, the details thereof ; 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to establish dedicated programmes for the promotion of 
Sambalpuri and other folk traditions of western Odisha at the national level; and

various art forms, music, dance, theatre and literature including folk art, folk music, folk dance and

maintained. However, the financial assistance provided to the State of Odisha under various 
schemes, during the last five years is provided in Annexure-I. 
   
(c) At present, there is no such proposal to establish dedicated programmes for the promotion of 
Sambalpuri and other folk traditions of western Odisha at the national level. 
 
(d) Since, KSVY is a central sector scheme for promotion of arts and culture, no district/region wise 
data are available.  However, the Ministry of Culture has been making continuous efforts to

entries.t: Implementation of University Townships and Education-to-Employment Initiatives
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-1263 
ANSWERED ON - 27/07/2026 
 
Implementation of University Townships and Education-to-Employment Initiatives 
 
1263.    Adv. Chandra Shekhar : 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of the criteria adopted for the selection of locations and the proposed timeline  
for the development of the five "University Townships" near major industrial and logistics 
corridors; 
(b) the details of the proposed composition, mandate, functions and present status of the High-
Powered Education-to-Employment and Enterprise Standing Committee; and 
(c) the details of the action taken by the Government to integrate Artificial Intelligence (AI) 
and Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming and Comics (A VGC) into school curriculum 
frameworks, along with the mechanism proposed to assess the impact of these initiatives 
on youth employability? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (c): The Government of India has framed and approved the National Education Policy 
(NEP) 2020 to transform the education landscape into a multidisciplinary, inclusive, and 
learner-centric ecosystem. It accords high priority to enhancing access, equity, and qual ity of 
education for everyone. It promotes provision of physical infrastructure, digital tools & 
connectivity, and greater industry-academic linkages. 
 
In line with the vision of NEP 2020, it has been announced in the Union Budget 2026-27 that 
the Union Government aims to support States through challenge route, in creating 5 University 
Townships in the vicinity of major industrial and logistic corridors. Department of Higher 
Education has initiated consultation process with relevant stakeholders such as Sta te 
Governments, Academia, Industry representatives etc.  
 
To make India a global leader in services, and to optimise the potential for growth, employment 
and exports, assessing the impact of  emerging technologies, including AI, on jobs and skill 
requirements and propose measures thereof, Union Budget 2026-27 has also announced setting 

up of a High -Powered ‘Education to Employment and Enterprise ’ Standing Committee to 
recommend measures that fo cus on the Services Sector as a core driver of Viksit Bharat. 
Composition of the Committee is at Annexure.  
In line with NEP 2020, the Central Board of Secondary Education ( CBSE) has integrated 
Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Computational Thinking (CT) into the school curriculum. The 
framework introduces AI from the preparatory stage to build AI -literate learners by 2030, 
focusing on computational thinking, digital literacy, innovation, problem -solving, and 
responsible technology use.  
To ensure availability of professionals for Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming and Comics 
(A VGC) Sector, Government of India has announced in Union Budget 2026-27 to set up A VGC 
Content Creator Labs in 15,000 secondary schools and 500 colleges  by supporting  Indian 
Institute of Creative Technologies, Mumbai.

entries.t: Assessment of the Quality of Forest Cover
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1264 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
 
Assessment of the Quality of Forest Cover 
 
 1264.  SHRI VARUN CHAUDHRY: 
            SHRI JAI PRAKASH: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether there is any proposal under consideration for providing access to better satellite resolution to 
Forest Survey of India for improving the accuracy of India State of Forest Report, if so, the time frame by 
which it will be accessible, if not, the reasons therefor; 
(b) whether the Government has undertaken an independent assessment of the quality of forest cover, 
including forest density and biodiversity, in addition to the area reported in the India State of Forest 
Report, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the details of forest land diverted for non-forest purposes during the last three years, State/UT and 
sector-wise; and  
(d) whether compensatory afforestation has been carried out against all forest land diverted during the last 
five years, if so, the details of land identified, plantations raised and survival rates? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE 
CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH)  
(a) & (b) Forest Survey of India (FSI), Dehradun, an organization under the Ministry of Environment, 
Forest and Climate Change, carries out the assessment of forest and tree cover of the country biennially 
and publishes the findings in the India State of Forest Report (ISFR). The forest cover assessment is a 
wall-to-wall mapping exercise based on interpretation of multi-temporal satellite data supported by 
extensive ground truthing.  
FSI periodically adopts technological and methodological advancements for improving the accuracy and 
reliability of forest cover mapping. Over the years, these advancements have included the use of improved 
satellite data, mapping at higher scales, and refinement in image interpretation techniques, while ensuring 
consistency and comparability of the assessment over time.  
The ISFR provides an assessment of the quality of forest cover in addition to the extent of forest cover. 
The report classifies forest cover on the basis of canopy density into Very Dense Forest (canopy density 
of 70% and above), Moderately Dense Forest (canopy density of 40% to less than 70%) and Open Forest 
(canopy density of 10% to less than 40%). 
 
(c)  The details of forest land approved for diversion under the provisions of the Van (Sanrakshan Evam 
Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980 during the last three years, State/UT-wise and sector-wise, are given at 
Annexure-I and Annexure-II, respectively. 
(d)   In compliance of the conditions stipulated under the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) 
Adhiniyam, 1980, the compensatory afforestation is taken up by the concerned State/UT. As per  the 
reports received from the States/UTs, the compensatory afforestation over an area of 1,78,261.52 hectares 
has been carried out during the last five years. The survival percentage of these  plantations have been 
reported between 40% to 100%.

entries.t: Nutritional Standards under the PM POSHAN Scheme
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACY 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 1265 
ANSWERED ON- 27.07.2026 
 
Nutritional Standards under the PM POSHAN Scheme 
 
1265. Shri Abhishek Banerjee:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of States/Union Territory providing eggs under the PM POSHAN Scheme during the 
last five years, including the number of beneficiary children covered and the frequency  of egg 
supply, State/UT and year-wise; 
 
(b) whether the Government maintains data on States, districts or implementing agencies  where 
eggs have been withdrawn, reduced or replaced by vegetarian substitutes, if so, the reasons therefor 
and the number of children affected; 
 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the nutritional impact of such withdrawal or substitution, 
particularly on underweight, stunting and anaemia among children, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) whether the Government has issued guidelines to ensure that school meals are based on scientific 
nutritional standards while respecting local dietary practices and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(e) whether nutritional equivalence standards have been prescribed for substitutes provided in place 
of eggs under the PM POSHAN Scheme, if so, the details thereof? 
  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (e): Education is part of the Concurrent List of the Constitution and most of the Government 
Schools and School Boards are under the administration of the State Government  and Union 
Territory (UT) Administrations. PM POSHAN Scheme is implemented in partnership with the State 
Governments and UT Administrations. The overall responsibility for providing hot and nutritious 
meal to all children studying in Bal Vatika (just before class 1) and classes I to VIII of Government 
and Government aided schools lies with the State Governments and UT Administrations. The States 
and UTs are encouraged to decide menu suitable to the local conditions within the prescribed 
nutrition and food norms and to procure locally grown food items like millets, vegetables, 
condiments etc.  
 

Under the PM Poshan Scheme, one hot cooked meal is provided to all eligible children on all 
school working days. As per the provisions of National Food Security Act, 2013 and the Guidelines 
of the Scheme, the nutritional and food norms prescribed under the Scheme are as follows: 
 
Items For children of Primary 
classes

A) Nutritional Norms (Per child per day) 
Calorie 450 700

B) Quantum of Food Norms (Per child per day) 
Food-grains 100 gms 150 gms 
Pulses 20 gms 30 gms

Salt & condiments As per need As per need 
 
Further, there is a provision of 5% of total recurring budget as the flexi component to be used 
by the States/UTs for setting up of School Nutrition Gardens (SNGs) and provision of 
supplementary nutrition interventions in identified districts. Many States/  UTs also provide 
additional supplementary nutrition keeping in view local food habits, cultural preferences, 
availability and dietary practices.  
 
Regarding the impact of PM Poshan Scheme, NITI AAYOG has conducted the evaluation 
of the Scheme through independent third -party agency in 2025 -26. The study concluded that the 
PM POSHAN scheme  has a positive impact on  improving child nutrition and boosting learning 
outcomes.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1266 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
Development of Eco-tourism Trails in Chhattisgarh  
 
 
1266. SMT. ROOPKUMARI CHOUDHARY: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state 
 
(a) whether the Government has formulated any policy for the development of Eco-tourism Trails, if 
so, the details thereof, State/UT-wise including Chhattisgarh; 
(b) the details of Eco-tourism and biodiversity conservation projects sanctioned during the last three 
years in Barnawapara, Sitanadi and Udanti Wildlife Sanctuaries, Kanger Valley National Park, 
Indravati Tiger Reserve, Achanakmar Tiger Reserve and Guru Ghasidas-Tamor Pingla Tiger Reserve, 
along with the funds released; 
(c) whether any Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) has been issued for biodiversity conservation 
and mitigation of human-wildlife conflict in eco-tourism areas; and 
(d) the measures taken to promote tribal participation and generate local employment through eco-
tourism in Barnawapara Wildlife Sanctuary, Sitanadi Wildlife Sanctuary and Udanti Wildlife 
Sanctuary in Chhattisgarh, and whether the Government proposes to further strengthen eco-tourism 
infrastructure in these protected areas? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a)  The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has issued Guidelines for Sustainable 
Ecotourism in Forest and Wildlife Areas-2021. An indicative list of potential eco-tourism areas has 
been annexed to the Guidelines which inter-alia includes sites in Chhattisgarh. 
 
(b)  Ecotourism and biodiversity conservation is primarily the responsibility of the concerned State 
Government and Union Territory Administrations, and are undertaken in accordance with 
prescriptions of an approved Management Plan, Tiger Conservation Plan and Working Plan, as 
applicable. No specific ecotourism project has been sanctioned by the Ministry of Environment, 
Forest and Climate Change for the State of Chhattisgarh. However, financial assistance is provided 
to the State under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats 
for protection, conservation and management of wildlife and development of its habitats. The details 
of funds released to the State of Chhattisgarh under the aforesaid scheme during last three years is as 
below: 
Rs in lakhs 
2023-24 2024-25 2025-26 
409.10 443.57 266.58 
 
 

(c) and (d)  The Ministry has released species-specific guidelines on 21.03.2023 for mitigation of 
Human Wildlife conflicts involving Elephant, Gaur, Leopard, Snake, Crocodile, Rhesus Macaque, 
Wild Pig, Bear, Blue Bull and Blackbuck taking a Harmonious Coexistence Approach for addressing 
human-wildlife conflicts. The Ministry has also issued guidelines for crosscutting issues such as 
cooperation with media, occupational health and safety in human-wildlife conflict mitigation, crowd 
management and addressing health emergencies arising out of human-wildlife conflict situations. 
Moreover, Field Manual for Frontline Staff on Human-Elephant Conflict Management has been 
issued. Further, the National Tiger Conservation Authority hasissued following three SOPs to deal 
with human-animal conflict, which are available in public domain: 
 
i. To deal with emergency arising due to straying of tigers in human dominated landscapes 
ii. To deal with tiger depredation on livestock 
iii. For active management towards rehabilitation of tigers from source areas at the 
landscapelevel. 
 
The three SOPs inter alia include the issue of managing dispersing tigers, managing livestock kills so 
as to reduce conflict as well as relocating tigers from source areas to areas where density of tiger is 
low, so that conflict in rich source areas does not occur. 
 
The National Tiger Conservation Authority has also issued the Normative Standards for Tourism 
Activities and Project Tiger Guidelines, 2012. These guidelines provide for conservation of ecology; 
community participation including tribal communities thereby promoting livelihoods and ensuring 
their stake in such endeavors. 
 
As per information provided by the State Government, several measures have been taken to promote 
tribal participation and generate local employment through eco-tourism. Local youths have been 
selected as guide for tourists. Joint Forest Management Committees (JFMC) have been involved in 
trekking, bird watching, boating and running of canteen. Gypsy vehicles have been provided to JFMC 
from revolving fund for income generation of local people.

entries.t: Inclusion of Temples in PRASHAD Scheme
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TOURISM 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.+1267 
ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
INCLUSION OF TEMPLES IN PRASHAD SCHEME 
 
+1267. SHRI NARAYAN TATU RANE: 
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether any proposal to cover Kunakeshwar Temple located in 
Devgad Taluka and Shri Dev Rameshwar Temple located in Malvan 
Taluka of Sindudurg district under the Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and 
Spiritual, Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD) scheme has been 
received; 
(b) if so, the current status thereof; 
(c) if not, the details of the steps proposed to be taken by the Government 
to cover the said temples under the said scheme; and 
(d) the details of funds likely to be made available for the related 
developmental works? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM            (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (d): Ministry of Tourism under its Scheme “Pilgrimage Rejuvenation 
and Spiritual, Heritage Augmentation Drive” (PRASHAD) provides financial 
assistance to the State Governments (SGs) and Union Territory 
Administrations (UTAs) for development of tourism related infrastructure at 
identified religious and heritage sites across the country including the State 
of Maharashtra. This process is undertaken in consultation with concerned 
State Governments (SGs) and Union Territory Administrations (UTAs). 
 
Currently, no proposal is under consideration of the Ministry of 
Tourism to include Kunakeshwar Temple located in Devgad Taluka and Shri 
Dev Rameshwar Temple located in Malvan Taluka of Sindudurg district 
under the PRASHAD scheme.  
 
However, receiving proposals from the State Governments (SGs) and 
Union Territory Administrations (UTAs) for financial assistance for tourism 

projects is a continuous process. The proposals received are examined with 
reference to the prescribed guidelines and financial assistance is extended 
for such projects subject to fulfilment of the stipulated conditions and 
availability of funds.

Compliance of NGT Orders 
 
1268. SHRI SANJAY UTTAMRAO DESHMUKH: 
 
Will the Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has the details of the projects received during the last five years 
for Environmental Clearance ; 
(b) if so, the details thereof, region-wise along with their status; 
(c) whether the Government has developed any mechanism to monitor the compliance of the 
orders of the National Green Tribunal; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (b) The Government of India has issued Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) 
Notification, 2006 under the powers conferred by sub-section (1) and clause (v) of sub-section 
(2) of section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. As per the provisions laid down in 
the EIA Notification, 2006, as amended from time to time, the proposals specified in its 
Schedule are appraised by the Expert Appraisal Committee (EAC) at Central Level and State 
Expert Appraisal Committee (SEAC) at the State/UT Level, considering all the environmental 
implications associated with the project, including issues raised during the Public Consultation. 
Based on the recommendation of the EAC/SEAC, projects are further considered by the 
Ministry or State Environmental Impact Assessment Authority (SEIAA) at Central Level and 
State/UT level respectively, for approval for grant of Environmental Clearance (EC) or 
otherwise. As per the provisions stated above, ECs are granted after considering environmental 
issues and incorporating appropriate environmental safeguards, including mitigation measures 
prescribed in the Environmental Management Plan (EMP). 
 
As per the extant provisions of the EIA Notification, 2006, as amended from time to time, 
Environmental Clearance is required for project activities falling under the 38 categories 
specified in its Schedule. The state-wise details of proposals granted EC by the Ministry during 
the last five years are placed at Annexure I. 
 
(c) to (d) All directions issued by the Hon'ble Tribunal to the Ministry are followed up for next 
necessary action/compliance by the respective Divisions/Sectors and the Hon'ble Tribunal is 
constantly informed from time to time, wherever required.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1270 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27TH JULY, 2026 
 
STATUS OF EMPLOYMENT 
 
1270.      SHRI VIJAYAKUMAR ALIAS VIJAY VASANTH: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that unemployment remains 
high despite claims of job creation and if so, the details thereof 
and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(b) the details of the steps taken by the Government to generate 
sustainable employment; 
(c) whether the Government has any data on total new jobs created 
in Government and Private sectors during the last three years and 
if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(d) whether large number of vacancies in Government departments 
remain unfilled and if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons 
therefor along with the timeline to fill such vacancies; 
(e) whether the Government has assessed quality of jobs created, 
particularly contractual and gig employment and if so, the details 
thereof and if not, the reasons therefor along with the safeguards 
for job security; and 
(f) whether any study has been conducted by the Government on 
youth unemployment trends in the country and if so, the details 
thereof and if not, the reasons therefor along with the corrective 
measures initiated? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (f): Official estimates of employment and unemployment in India 
are derived from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), conducted by 
the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation since 2017 –18. 
The PLFS methodology was revamped with effect from January 2025. 
The PLFS Annual Report 2025 is the first report in the revised series to 
present labour market estimates, covering the period from January to 
December 2025. 

As per latest PLFS report 2025, the estimated Unemployment Rate 
(UR) on usual status for persons of age 15 years and above has 
decreased from 3.6% in 2022 to 3.1% in 2025 in the country. Also, the 
estimated UR for youth of age 15 -29 years has decreased from 10.9% in 
2022 to 9.9% in 2025 in the country. 
 
Further, the estimated Worker Population Ratio (WPR) indicating 
employment on usual status for persons of age 15 years and above has 
increased from 54.1% in 2022 to 57.4% in 2025 in the country. 
 
The KLEMS (K: Capital, L: Labour, E: Energy, M: Materials and S: 
Services) database published by Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) covers 27 
industries comprising of the entire Indian economy and provides 
employment estimates across 27 industries. As per the latest data, total 
estimated employment in the country has increased to 64.33 crores 
(Provisional) during 2023-24 as compared to 47.15 crores during 2014-15, 
which indicates a growth of 36.44% during the period.  
 
Further, more than 8.23 crore net subscribers have joined 
Employees’ Provident Fund Organization (EPFO) between September 
2017 and July 2025 indicating increase in employment and formalization 
of the job market. Also, more than 1.29 crore net subscribers have joined 
EPFO during the year 2024-25. 
 
Occurrence and filling up of vacant posts in various 
Ministries/Departments, is a continuous process. Ministries/ Departments 
of the Central Government have been directed, from time to time, to fill 
up vacant posts in a time bound manner. The details of vacancies and 
recruitments are maintained by the respective Ministry/ Department/PSU 
etc. under Central Government. Vacant posts are being filled up in 
mission mode by various Ministries/ Departments, their attached 
organisations and CPSUs etc.   
 
Employment generation coupled with improving employability is a 
priority of the Government. Accordingly, Government is implementing 
various employment generation schemes/ programmes in the country. 
The details of various employment generation schemes/ programmes 
being implemented by the Government may be seen at   
https://dge.gov.in/dge/schemes_programmes. 
 
The Rozgar Mela is a major initiative aimed at prioritising 
employment generation. Since its inception, more than 12.5 lakh 
recruitment letters have been issued through 19 Rozgar Melas organised 
across the country. 
 

Government is also implementing Skill India Mission (SIM) to 
deliver skill, re-skill and up-skill training through an extensive network of 
skill development centres/ schools/ colleges /institutes etc. under 
various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), 
Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship Promotion 
Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial 
Training Institutes (ITIs) in the country. The SIM aims at enabling youth 
of India to get future ready, equipped with industry relevant skills.

entries.t: Launching an e-Portal for Old EPF Accounts
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1272 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
LAUNCHING AN E-PORTAL FOR OLD EPF ACCOUNTS 
 
1272. SHRI V K SREEKANDAN: 
 
         Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)whether it is a fact that the Government is considering to launch 
an e -portal to facilitate  identification/tracking unique account 
number linking and activation of old Employees Provident  Fund 
accounts; 
(b)if so, the details thereof; 
(c)whether it is also a fact that the Government is likely to expand 
the scope of the said e-portal to include members who may not be 
able to recall or access their old number  identifications and if so, 
the details thereof; and 
(d)whether it is also true that the e -portal is expected to reduce 
manual intervention, minimize  documentation and enhance 
transparency and efficiency and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) & (b): EPFO has developed an e-portal which is a digital platform 
facilitating the members providing their Aadhaar -based 
authentication to track their inoperative accounts so as to securely 
access and transfer their old PF accounts to their active Universal 
Account Number (UAN) or get it settled. 
(c):   No such proposal is presently under consideration. 
(d):   Yes, it is expected that the portal would reduce manual 
intervention, minimize physical documentation, and enhance 
transparency and efficiency through Aadhaar -based digital 
authentication and the digital submission of Joint Declarations for 
KYC updates (s ubject to due verification). This would facilitate the 
efficient, transparent, and hassle -free settlement of old EPF 
inoperative accounts.

QUESTION 
 
1273. Shri Asaduddin Owaisi: 
 
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that, according to data from the Controller 
General of  Accounts, the Ministry spent only Rs.500 cr (~4 per cent) out of the 
Rs.11500 cr budget in the  first 8 months of the FY 2025 -26 on the Prime Minister 
Internship Scheme, when nearly 94 percent of the allocation (Rs.10,800 cr) was 
earmarked for it; 
(b) if so, the reasons for such a shortfall in the expenditure amid high rate of 
unemployment among the youth in the country; 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the reasons for the low acceptance of 
internship offers and the high dropout rate of interns, despite lakhs of applications 
being received, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the corrective measures being taken to improve the uptake, utilization of funds and 
overall effectiveness of the PMIS? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS AND MINISTRY OF 
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
                                                                                            [SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA] 
(a)&(b): The PM Internship Scheme announced in the Budget 2024 -25, is designed to 
enhance industry -relevant skills, improve job readiness, and foster professional 
exposure through structured internships in India’s top -performing companies and 
institutions to create job ready, skilled work force. The scheme is not designed  to 
provide employment.  
As an initiation to this Scheme, Ministry of Corporate Affairs launched a Pilot Project 
of the Scheme on 3 rd October, 2024, which is targeted to provide  1.25 lakh internship 
opportunities. Details of amount sanctioned and utilized for the Prime Minister

 (c): On the basis of independent evaluation and feedback survey carried out by the 
Ministry of Corporate Affairs, feedback received from various stakeholders, such as 
candidates, industry & industry associations and state governments, reasons behind 
acceptance rate of internship offers and the dropout rate of interns  in Round I & II of 
the PMIS Pilot Project are given below: 
• Internship period of 12 months was longer than that in other skilling 
programs. 
• Location is an important consideration and ideal travel distance 
indicated by candidates should be between 5-10 km. 
• Some candidates are not interested in roles offered.  
Pilot Project is a pivotal phase that has allowed for testing concepts, strategies and 
systems before a full-scale implementation.  
(d): Based on the learning during the implementation of the Round I and Round II of 
the PMIS Pilot Project, following measures have been taken: 
i. As per the r evised guidelines of the PMIS Pilot Project  issued vide O.M. dated 
12.03.2026 following key changes have been made:  
 
a. A flexible duration of internships of either 6 or 9 months based on the 
company’s requirements is provided. 
b. The monthly allowance has been enhanced from Rs. 5000 to Rs. 9000.  
c. The age requirement for youth has been relaxed from 21 –24 to 18 –25 
years. Further, candidates who have a master’s degree and students from 
final year of graduation/post-graduation are eligible to participate. 
d. Scope of companies/organisations eligible to participate has been 
expanded.  
e. Adopted a rolling internship cycle allowing continuous posting, selection, 
and onboarding. 
ii. Portal Improvement: functionality for geo -tagging internship location, moving 
vacancies and candidates between one location to another and, more visibility 
of additional benefits given by companies to the candidates. 
iii. Targeted Information, Education and Communications (IEC) activities. 
iv. Active engagement and coordination with States, UTs, Ministries and 
Departments of the Central Government and Industry Associations for 
enhancing the outreach of the scheme.

LOK SABHA 
UN-STARRED QUESTION NO. 1274 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON MONDAY, JULY 27, 2026 / SHRAVANA 5, 1948 (SAKA) 
Increasing Number of Billionaires 
✝1274. Shri Murari Lal Meena: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: - 
(a) Whether the Government is aware that there has been a significant increase in the number 
of billionaires in the country and that is among the leading nations in the world in this 
regard; 
(b) If so, the details thereof during the last five years; 
(c) Whether the Government has maintained any official or compiled data regarding the 
estimated aggregate wealth of Indian billionaires and the increase therein during the last 
five years; 
(d) If so, the details thereof; 
(e) Whether the Government has conducted any study regarding the impact of the increasing 
concentration of income and wealth on income inequality, investment, employment 
generation and inclusive economic growth; 
(f) If so, the major findings thereof; and 
(g) The policy measures and reform initiatives being taken by the Government to reduce 
income and wealth inequality, promote broad -based employment generation and foster 
inclusive economic growth? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINSITRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
 

2 
 
 
(a) and (b): There is no statutory definition of the term ‘billionaire’ either under the Income-tax Act,

entries.t: Pollution caused by KRIBHCO in Shahjahanpur
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1275 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
Pollution caused by KRIBHCO in Shahjahanpur 
 
1275. SHRI ARUN KUMAR SAGAR: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the unutilized water/waste of chemical company KRIBHCO located in Shahjahanpur 
Parliamentary Constituency of Uttar Pradesh is polluting the area, causing various diseases and 
rendering cultivable land useless; 
(b) if so, the details thereof;  
(c) whether the Government has taken/proposes to take any steps to free the said Constituency from 
pollution; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE 
CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
(a) to (d): As per the information provided by Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board (UPPCB), 
water and air polluting industries in Shahjahanpur are inspected from time to time. Action is taken 
against the polluting units found non-complying during inspection under the provisions of the 
Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 and the Air (Prevention and Control of 
Pollution) Act, 1981. 
Further, the Shahjahanpur Parliamentary Constituency of Uttar Pradesh is located within the 
Ganga River basin. Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) organizes annual inspection of 
Grossly Polluting Industries (GPIs) including Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETPs) 
operating in river Ganga main stem States having potential to discharge into river Ganga & its 
tributaries by joint teams of officials from third party technical institutes and SPCBs/PCC since 
2017. In cases of non-compliance found during inspections, appropriate actions such as issue of 
Show Cause Notice & Closure direction and imposition of Environmental Compensation are 
issued under Section 5 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. 
CPCB authorised third party technical institute, Indian Institute of Technology (BHU), Varanasi, 
inspected the industry on 23.08.2025. During the inspection, the industry was found complying 
w.r.t. notified discharge standards. 
As per the report received from Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board (UPPCB), KRIBHCO 
Fertilizers Ltd., Shahjahanpur has installed Effluent treatment plant of 200 m3/hour for treatment 
of effluent generated from industrial processes. A joint inspection of this industry was conducted 
during 04.12.2024 and 05.12.2024 by the UPPCB, the district administration and CPCB. Latest 

inspection of the unit has been done by Regional office, UPPCB, Bareilly on 19.02.2026 and in 
all above inspections it was observed that no effluent was being discharged outside the premises, 
the unit was found to be in operation in compliance of prescribed norms and there is no evidence 
to suggest that the unit's operations have caused the spread of any disease or rendered agricultural 
land unfit for use.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1277 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
DIGITAL GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL SYSTEM 
 
1277. SHRI EATALA RAJENDER: 
 
         Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)whether the Government launches digital grievance redressal 
system for gig workers in the country and if so, the details thereof; 
(b)whether the Government has developed mechanism, a firs t of its 
kind in the country  platform based Gig Workers’ Board in 
collaboration with the Department of e-Governance; and 
(c)if so, the details thereof along with present status during the last 
five years comparatively? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (c): For the first time, the definition of ‘gig workers’ and 
‘platform workers’ and provisions related to the same have been 
provided in the Code on Social Security, 2020 which has come into 
force on 21.11.2025.  
 
  The Code provides for framing of suitable social security 
schemes for gig workers and platform workers on matters relating to 
life and disability cover, accident insurance, health and maternity 
benefits, old age protection, etc. The Code provides for setting up of 
a Social Security Fund t o finance these welfare schemes.  The Code 
also has provisions to constitute a National Social Security Board for 
the purposes of the welfare of gig workers and platform workers.  
 
  The Code has provisions for setting up a toll -free centre, 
or helpline or facilitation centres for unorganized, gig, and platform 
workers by the appropriate Government. These facilities will 
disseminate information on available social security schemes, 
facilitate filing, processing and forwarding of application forms for 
registration, assist to obtain registration and facilitate the enrolment 
of the registered unorganized workers, gig workers and platform 
workers in the social security schemes.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
 
LOK SABHA  
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 1278 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
National Mission for Manuscripts 
 
 
1278. Shri Baijayant Panda: 
          Shri Murasoli S: 
 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) the current status of implementation of the National Mission for Manuscripts (NMM) across the 
country, including the details of manuscript surveys conducted and digitisation undertaken during 
the last five years and the current year; 
(b) whether the Government has conducted any evaluation or review of the Mission with regard to 
institutional capacity, regional coverage and utilisation of allocated funds; 
(c) if so, the key findings thereof; and 
(d) the details of the extent of coverage along with progress of the National Mission for Manuscripts 
in Odisha for preservation of Manuscripts from repositories in Tamil Nadu including Thanjavur 
district, particularly in the Saraswathi Mahal Library, along with the number of manuscripts 
identified, conserved and digitised, institutional partners involved and funds released thereon 
during the said period? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM  
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) Government has launched Gyan Bharatam Mission, subsuming erstwhile National Mission for 
Manuscripts (NMM), as a major initiative under the Ministry of Culture. It aims to survey, document, 
conserve, digitize and make accessible manuscripts located in academic institutions, museums, libraries, 
and private collections across India.National Manuscript Survey was launched in March, 2026 across all 
States and Union Territories of the country to identify and document manuscript holdings, repositories 
and custodians representing diverse languages and scripts.During the survey, more than 1.19 crore 
manuscripts have been reported.The total number of digitized manuscripts available across the country is 
over 8 lakh, out of which, more than 3.90 lakh manuscripts are available on Gyan Bharatam portal at 
present for public access in view mode. 

 
(b) & (c) Gyan Bharatam, is a Pan-India initiative covering cataloguing, conservation, digitization and 
publication of manuscripts identified across the country. For effective implementation, a framework of 
Cluster Centres and Independent Centres has been envisaged. These centres are provided financial 
assistance in form of grant-in-aid to undertake manuscript related activities as elaborated above. States / 
UTs have also been onboarded to act as the Nodal Coordinating Authority for the mission’s 
implementation and review within the State / UT concerned. Financial support to the States / UTs and 
their repositories is considered on case-to-case basisand in accordance with the applicableframework, 
operational requirements and availability of funds.  
(d) Under the Gyan Bharatam Mission, two centers located in Odisha namely SARASVATI, Bhadrak 
(Sanskrit Academy of Research for Advanced Society Through Vedic and Allied Tradition of India) and 
the Department of Sanskrit, Utkal University, Bhubaneswar have been onboarded. During the National 
Manuscript Survey, 78,056 manuscripts have been reported from Odisha. Further, 800 manuscripts have 
been conserved and 848 manuscripts digitized. Grant to the tune of Rs.28 Lakh has been released to 
SARASVATI, Bhadrak, Odisha in February, 2026 to carry out manuscript related activities. 
So far as Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu is concerned, out of the total 1,41,652 manuscripts reported in Tamil 
Nadu, 47,496 manuscripts have been reported from the Saraswathi Mahal Library, Thanjavur during the 
National Manuscript Survey. 
*****

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1279 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27TH JULY, 2026 
 
STATUS OF FUNCTIONAL EMPLOYMENT EXCHANGES AND MCCS 
 
1279.      SHRI APPALANAIDU KALISETTI: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the total number of Employment Exchanges/Model 
Career Centres (MCCs)  currently operational in the country, 
State/UT-wise; 
(b) the total number of job -seekers registered with Employment 
Exchanges/MCCs during each  of the last five years and current 
year, year and State/UT -wise, along with district -wise for Andhra 
Pradesh; 
(c) the details of the total sanctioned strength and actual number of 
personnel working in  Employment Exchanges/MCCs, indicating 
their designation/job in the country, State/UT and role-wise; 
(d) the total number of Government and Private vacancies notified 
through Employment  Exchanges/MCCs in the country during the 
said period, year, State/UT and sector-wise; 
(e) the details of the number of candidates placed in Government and 
Private sectors during  the last five years and current year in the 
country, sector, year and State/UT-wise; and 
(f) whether the Government has undertaken any review or impact 
assessment regarding  share of placements facilitated in Private 
sector through Employment Exchanges/MCCs and if so,  the details 
thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (f): Government is implementing National Employment Service 
through a network of Employment Exchanges. Employment is the joint 
concern of the Central and State Government. Centre formulates 
policies, standards and procedures for operating employment exchanges 
whereas administrative and financial control of Employment Exchanges 
lies with the respective State/UT Government. 
 

 
Ministry of Labour and Employment is running the National Career 
Service (NCS) Portal for transformation of the National Employment 
Service. The NCS Portal is a one -stop solution for providing career 
related services including jobs from private and government sectors, 
information on online & offline job fairs, job search & matching, career 
counselling, vocational guidance, information on skill development 
courses, skill/training programmes etc. through a digital platform 
[www.ncs.gov.in]. 
As on 15.07.2026, there are 1008 Employment Exchanges in the 
country. Further, under the NCS project, the Government has approved 
407 Model Career Centres (MCCs), which also includes 370 Employment 
Exchanges, that have been upgraded as MCCs. State/UT -wise details of 
the number of Employment Exchanges and Model Career Centres may be 
seen at https://dge.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-05/Directory_of_EEX.pdf and 
https://www.ncs.gov.in/User_Manuals/List_of_Model_Career_Centers.pdf 
respectively. 
The State/UT -wise, district -wise and year -wise details of 
jobseekers registered, and number of vacancies mobilized on NCS portal 
(including through Employment Exchange/ MCCs) across the country may 
be seen at https://www.ncs.gov.in/_layouts/15/ncsp/ViewStaticReport.aspx  
Further, notifying final hiring figures is not a mandatory 
requirement on NCS portal. However, the job hiring data is available only 
to the extent as voluntarily reported by the employers. 
 
*****

ESIC FACILITIES IN PUNJAB 
 
†1280. SHRI SUKHJINDER SINGH RANDHAWA: 
 
         Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)whether the Government is aware that the beneficiaries of the 
Employees' State Insurance  Corporation (ESIC) are facing 
difficulties in availing timely and quality healthcare services in  
various States of the country, including Punjab; 
(b) if so, the details of the complaints received along with the action 
taken thereon in Punjab, district-wise; 
(c)whether it is a fact that the beneficiaries have to depend on private 
hospitals due to the  shortage of specialist doctors, paramedical 
staff, essential medicines, modern medical equipment  and 
diagnostic facilities in several ESIC hospitals and dispensaries in 
Punjab; and 
(d) if so, the details of the steps taken by the Government to address 
the said deficiencies, upgrade the ESIC hospitals and dispensaries, 
set up new hospitals/dispensaries and fill up the  vacant posts in 
Punjab? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (d): Grievances, representations and issues raised at various 
fora are addressed expeditiously by the Employees' State Insurance 
Corporation (ESIC) in coordination with the concerned hospitals and 
dispensaries. Further, ESIC regularly follows up with the concerned 
State Governments for early settlement of pending reimbursement 
claims relating to primary and secondary medical treatment availed 
by ESI beneficiaries under emergency circumstances from medical 
institutions outside the ESI hospital and dispensary network. 
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
  Medical care in Punjab is provided through 01 ESIC 
Medical College & Hospital at Ludhiana, 01 ESIC Hospital at 
Ramdarbar, Chandigarh, 06 ESI State Run Hospitals at Mohali, 
Jalandhar, Hoshiarpur, Amritsar, Mandi Gobind Garg, Phagwara, 69 
ESI State Run Dispensaries, 03 ESIC Dispensary cum Branch Offices 
at Rajpura, Barnala & Ferozepur. To strengthen healthcare services, 
ESIC has accorded in -principle approval for setting up three new 
hospitals in Punjab at Lalru, Rajpura and Malerkotla. Apart from this, 
ESIC has also empanelled network of 139 private tertiary care 
hospitals and 9 Government Medical Colleges/Hospitals. 
Beneficiaries are referred to empanelled hospitals on a cashless 
basis wherever required services are not available in ESI 
institutions. 
  Recruitment of doctors, teaching faculty, nursing officers 
and paramedical staff in ESIC is a continuous process. Recently, 
appointment letters have been issued to 388 Insurance Medical 
Officer (IMO) Grade -II, 234 Assistant Professors, 1,577 Nursing 
Officers and 472 Nursing Officers. Further recruitment against 1,827 
paramedical posts has also been completed.

Deployment of School Teachers as BLOs 
 
1282.  Shri Sribharat Mathukumilli: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of Government school teachers deployed as Booth Level Officers (BLOs) or 
for any other duties relating to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls during 
the last three years, State/UT-wise; 
(b) whether the Government has assessed the impact of such deployment on classroom 
teaching, student learning outcomes and teacher availability in Government schools, if so, the 
details and findings thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has received any representations or complaints from teachers, 
school managements, parents or State Governments regarding disruption of academic activities 
on account of such deployment, if so, the details thereof and the action taken thereon; and 
(d) the measures taken by the Government t o minimise diversion of teachers from teaching 
duties, including deployment of alternative personnel for electoral work and the timeline for 
implementation thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (d): Education being a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution, the majority of 
schools in the country are under the administrative control of the respective State Governments 
and Union Territory Administrations. Accordingly, deployment of teachers and assignment of 
duties to them, including for electoral purposes, fall within the administrative domain of the 
concerned States/UTs. The Department of School Education & Literacy does not maintain 
State/UT-wise information regarding deployment of Governm ent school teachers as Booth 
Level Officers (BLOs) or for duties relating to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral 
rolls. 
Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in its judgment dated 06.12.2007, while 
upholding the authority of the Electi on Commission of India to requisition teachers for 
election-related duties, observed that such deployment should be undertaken in a manner that 
does not adversely affect the functioning of schools and the right of children to education. The 
Hon'ble Court further observed that, as far as practicable, duties such as revision of electoral 
rolls should be assigned during holidays, non -teaching hours or non -working days so as to 
minimise disruption to teaching-learning activities. 
 

In pursuance of the above, the Ministry of Education issued guidelines dated 13.09.2010 to all 
States and Union Territories advising that duties relating to revision of electoral rolls should, 
as far as possible, be assigned to teachers during holidays, non-teaching hours or non-working 
days. The same is reiterated to all States/UTs from time to time. 
The National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 also emphasises that teachers should be enabled 
to focus on their core academic responsibilities and should not be burdened with excessive non-
teaching work, so that they can devote adequate time to classroom instruction, lesson 
preparation, student assessment and continuous professional development. 
Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha, financial assistance is provided 
to States/UTs for strengthening academic support institutions, including the State Councils of 
Educational Research and Training (SCERTs) and District Institutes of Education and Training 
(DIETs), and for providing continuous academic support through Block Resource Centres 
(BRCs) and Cluster Resource Centres (CRCs). The Scheme also supports technology-enabled 
governance and digital school management systems to improve administrative efficiency and 
reduce avoidable administrative burden on teachers. 
Further, through P roject Approval Board (PAB) meetings, review meetings and other 
communications, the Department of School Education & Literacy regularly advises States/UTs 
to ensure timely recruitment of teachers, rational deployment and optimum utilisation of human 
resources, and to leverage digital platforms for streamlining administrative processes, thereby 
enabling teachers to devote greater time to teaching-learning activities.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1284 
ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
  
CRAFTSMEN TRAINING SCHEME 
  
1284. DR. K SUDHAKAR: 
  
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has noted Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) issues like 88 per 
cent seat underutilisation, limited access for out -of-school youth and gender disparity in 
enrolment; 
 
(b)  whether the Government has taken any steps to address inconsistent practical training 
quality, low post-training placements due to industry skill gaps and lack of career guidance, if so, 
the details thereof; 
 
(c)  whether the Government is planning to integrate remote learning, digital infrastructure and 
achieve 100 per cent capacity with inclusive measures, specially for women and remote areas; 
and 
 
(d)  if so, the details thereof, if not, the reasons therefor? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
  
(a to d):  The Directorate General of Training (DGT), under the Ministry of Skill Development 
and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), implements the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) through a 
network of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) for skilling the youth. 
 
At present, training under CTS is imparted in 170 trades through 13,856 ITIs (Government – 3,328 
and Private – 10,528) across the country. 
 
The enrolment in ITIs has increased from 9.51 lakh in the academic session 2014 -15 to 14.70 
lakh in the academic session 2025-26. During the same period, seat utilization has improved from 
54% in the academic session 2014-15 to 64% in the academic session 2025-26. 
 
To ensure better utilization of training infrastructure and resources, DGT undertakes periodic 
rationalization of training units with no admissions. Accordingly, in January 2025, 21,069 units 
comprising 4.49 lakh seats in ITIs across the country, with no admissions during the academic 
sessions 2018 -19 to 2023 -24, were de -affiliated. Further, in May 2026, 4,292 units with an 
aggregate seating capacity of about 90,256 seats, wi th no admissions during the academic 
sessions 2022-23 to 2025-26, were also de-affiliated. 
 
The trade curriculum under CTS is updated periodically in consultation with industry, academia 
and State/UT Governments to incorporate emerging technologies, modern tools, equipment and 
machinery. The CTS curriculum also provides for On -the-Job Training (OJT), enabling trainees 
to gain practical exposure in industry settings and bridge the gap between classroom learning 
and workplace requirements. 

Further, DGT has developed the Bharat Skills portal, which provides digital learning resources, 
including e-books, videos, question banks and other e-learning content, to supplement classroom 
training and improve access to quality learning material for trainees and instructors under CTS. 
 
To promote greater participation of women in vocational training, 30% of the seats in Industrial 
Training Institutes (ITIs) are reserved for women. Further, the enrolment of women trainees under 
CTS has increased from 87,819 in the academic session 2014 -15 to 2,20,814 in the academic 
session 2025-26, reflecting the increasing participation of women in vocational training. 
 
Further, DGT undertakes various outreach and awareness initiatives to improve seat utilization 
under CTS and promote awareness among youth, parents and local communities about skilling 
opportunities and employment prospects under the ITI ecosystem.

entries.t: Pension Scheme for Landless Agricultural Labourers
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1286 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
PENSION SCHEME FOR LANDLESS AGRICULTURAL LABOURERS 
 
†1286. SHRI VIJAY BAGHEL: 
 
         Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)whether any pension scheme is implemented for landless 
agriculture labourers by the Government; 
(b)if so, the details thereof; 
(c)the details of the total number of landless agriculture labourers in 
the State of Chhattisgarh at present; 
(d)whether there is any provision to provide minimum wages to 
agriculture labourers by the Government; 
(e)if so, the details thereof; and 
(f)if not, whether the Government proposes to implement the same? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (f): The Government runs Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan -
Dhan (PM -SYM), a pension scheme for providing social security to 
unorganised workers  including landless agriculture labourer. 
  The PM-SYM scheme was launched in February, 2019 in 
order to provide old age protection to the workers of the unorganised 
sector such as const ruction workers, home -based workers, street 
vendors, domestic workers and other similar categories. This is a 
voluntary and contributory pension scheme. Under the scheme, a 
monthly assured pension of Rs. 3000/ - is provided to unorganised 
workers after attaining the age of 60 years, and the spouse is eligible 
for 50% of the pension as family pension. Workers in the age group of 
18–40 years whose monthly income is Rs. 15,000/ - or less and who 
are not members of EPFO/ESIC/NPS (Government funded) and are not 
income tax payers are eligible to join the scheme. The monthly 
contribution by the beneficiary ranges from Rs. 55/ - to Rs. 200/ - 
depending upon the entry age of the beneficiary. Under the  scheme,  
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
an equal matching contribution is paid by the Central Government. 
Enrolment in the scheme is done through the Common Service 
Centres (CSCs), which have a network of about 4 lakh centres across 
the country. Eligible unorganised workers can also self -enrol b y 
visiting the portal www.maandhan.in. 
   The number of Agricultural labourers registered on 
eShram portal (on a self -declared basis) in the state of Chhattisgarh 
is approximately 61 lakh as on 22.07.2026. 
 
  Under the provisions of the Code on Wages, 2019, both the 
Central Government and the State Governments are empowered to 
fix, review and revise minimum rates of wages for employees 
employed in scheduled employments under their respective 
jurisdictions. Ac cordingly, the appropriate Government fixes the 
minimum rates of wages for agricultural labourers falling within its 
jurisdiction.

 ANSWERED ON MONDAY, JULY 27, 2026/ SHRAVANA 5, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
Credit- Deposit Ratio of Banks in Uttar Pradesh 
 
† 1288. SHRI ARUN GOVIL: 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the current credit -deposit ratio of banks in Uttar Pradesh along with the year -wise credit-
deposit ratio during the last ten years, year-wise; 
(b) the details of the action plan of the Government to improve the credit -deposit ratio in those 
districts of Uttar Pradesh where credit-deposit ratio is low along with the district-wise details 
thereof; 
(c) whether it is a fact that no bank in the cou ntry has established its Head Office in Uttar 
Pradesh, the largest State in the country whereas the Head Office of the bank plays a 
significant role in improving the Credit-Deposit Ratio; 
(d) if so, whether the Government has any plan to set up the Head Office  of any bank in Uttar 
Pradesh and if so, the details thereof; 
(e) the number of villages selected under the Sansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY) in Meerut 
Lok Sabha Parliamentary Constituency that have bank branches; and 
(f) the plan of the Government to open bank branches in the above selected villages having no 
branches? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a): The current Credit - Deposit (CD) ratio of Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs) in Uttar 
Pradesh stands at 52.01% as of 31.3.2026. F urther, the CD ratio of SCBs in Uttar Pradesh 
during the last ten years, year-wise is at Annexure-I.  
(b): The CD ratio of SCBs in Uttar Pradesh, district - wise as on 31.3.2026 is at Annexure -II.  
The State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC), Uttar Pradesh has informed that banks in Uttar 
Pradesh, undertake various initiatives from time to time, to improve credit deployment, 
especially in low CD ratio districts. These initiatives include, inter alia, targeted credit expansion, 
strengthening district- level monitoring, credit outreach and awareness, support to Self Help 
Groups (SHGs), Micro- Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and One District One Product 
(ODOP) Clusters, process improvements and digital enablement for loan processing and 
coordination with various member lending institutions. 

Further, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has advised the banks to ensure that wide disparity in the 
ratios between States/ Regions is avoided in order to minimise regional imbalance in credit 
deployment and banks may review t he performance of their branches in such areas and take 
necessary steps to augment the credit flow. The Lead Bank of the district may discuss the issue 
of low CD ratio in all its aspects with the banks and also in the District Consultative Committee 
(DCC) forum. Special Sub-Committees (SSCs) of the DCC should draw up Monitorable Action 
Plans to increase the CD ratio in the districts having CD ratio of less than 40% and to report the 
progress on the implementation of the plan to DCC on a quarterly basis and through them to 
the convenor of the State Level. 
(c) and (d):  The Head Office of Utkarsh Small Finance Bank is located in Varanasi, Uttar 
Pradesh, while the Head Offices of Uttar Pradesh Gramin Bank and the Uttar Pradesh State 
Co-operative Bank are located in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. The credit planning and monitoring 
activities in a State are carried out through RBI’s Lead Bank Scheme, irrespective of the location 
of the bank’s Head Office.  
(e) and (f): Ministry of Rural Development has informed that unde r the Sansad Adarsh Gram 
Yojana (SAGY), a total of 10 Gram Panchayats had been selected in Meerut District. Further, 
as per the Jan Dhan Darshak (JDD) app, as on 30.6.2026, all inhabited villages i.e. 98,047 in 
the State of Uttar Pradesh are covered by a b anking outlet (Bank Branch, Business 
Correspondent, or India Post Payments Bank Centre) within a 5km radius.

PRESERVATION AND PROMOTION OF TRIBAL CULTURAL HERITAGE 
 
1289. DR. KIRSAN NAMDEO: 
 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any survey or documentation of the tribal 
cultural heritage, archaeological sites, traditional art forms, folk music, dance, festivals 
and indigenous knowledge systems in the Gadchiroli-ChimurLokSabha Constituency 
under any scheme; 
(b) the details of funds sanctioned, projects approved and cultural institutions supported in 
the said Constituency during the last five years and the current year, year-wise; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to establish a Tribal Cultural Resource Centre, 
museum or interpretation centre for preserving and promoting the cultural heritage of the 
tribal communities of the said region; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof along with the proposed timeline and if not, the reasons 
therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM  
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) The Government of India has set up South Central Zone Cultural Centre (SCZCC), 
Nagpur and West Zone Cultural Centre (WZCC), Udaipur to protect, promote and preserve 
folk/ tribal culture including folk dance & music, traditional art forms etc. of their member 
States which include Maharashtra (Gadchiroli-ChimurLokSabha Constituency). These ZCCs 
organize various cultural activities and programmes on regular basis in their member States 
including the State of Maharashtra.  
 
 SCZCC has promoted the tribal folk dances 'Lingo' and 'Rela' of Gadchiroli by 
providing performance platforms through various programmes organized by them. SCZCC 
has also facilitated the participation of tribal artists from the region in regional and national 
cultural events to preserve and disseminate their traditional art forms, music, dance and 
indigenous cultural practices.  
 
 Besides, SangeetNatakAkademi (an autonomous organization under Ministry of 
Culture) engaged fifty (50) artists belonging to Gond Tribe from the Gadchiroli-
ChimurLokSabha Constituency to participate in the cultural performances during the 
Republic Day Parade, 2026. 
 
 Further, WZCC has documented the traditional cultural practices/ art forms of 
Maharashtra, namely Gondhal in 2020, Dhangiri Gaza in 2024 and PaithaniSaree in 2025 as 
part of its efforts to preserve and promote the cultural heritage of the State.

entries.t: Construction of Hostels in Navodaya Vidyalayas
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1290 
ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
Construction of Hostels in Navodaya Vidyalayas 
 
1290. Shri Rambhual Nishad: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of construction of hostels in Navodaya  Vidyalayas started in the 
country during the last three years, State/UT -wise and year -wise especially district -
wise in Uttar Pradesh;  
 
(b) the status of construction of hostel in  Navodaya Vidyalaya at Sultanpur district of 
Uttar Pradesh as on date;  
 
(c) whether the construction of the said hostel at Sultanpur has been completed, if 
so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons for delay; and  
 
(d) the time by which the said construction is likely to be completed? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (d): The construction of permanent NavodayaVidyalaya (NV) building including 
hostels is a continuous process, which depends upon identification of suitable land, 
completion of lease formalities in favour of NavodayaVidyalayaSamiti (NVS) by the 
sponsoring authorities, submission of drawings/estimates by construct ion agency, 
availability of funds and requisite approvals, etc. as well as consecutive growth of the 
Vidyalaya. 
 
NVs are constructed in three phases, i.e. Phase -A, Phase -B and Phase -B 
(balance) as per growth of the students and efficient use of infrastructures. Under 
Phase A - School Building, Kitchen Dining, partial dormitories & partial staff quarters 
are constructed. Under Phase  B - partial dormitories & staff quarters and in Phase  B 
(balance) - left over dormitories are constructed as per act ual requirement basis. As 
per information received  from NVS, in Uttar Pradesh, hostel/ dormitories(beds) had 
been constructed in the year  2023-24 in NVs in Kanshiramnagar (192 beds), Hapur 
(384 beds), Shamli (192 beds), Badaun (192 beds) and Sultanpur (288  beds) 
districts. During the year 2025 -26, construction of hostel/ dormitories(beds) has been 
started in NVs in GB Nagar (24 beds) and Sitapur-I (48 beds). Further, State/UT-wise 
details of NVs  including in the State of Uttar Pradesh  where construction of 
hostels/dormitories (beds) have been started/completed during the last three years in 
the country are at Annexed.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1291 
TO BE ANSWERED ON: 27.07.2026 
 
NDC Targets 
 
1291.  SHRI MALAIYARASAN D: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) the progress made by Government towards achieving Nationally Determined Contributions 
(NDCs) under the Paris Agreement, including the targets relating to reduction in emissions 
intensity of GDP, expansion of non-fossil fuel-based electricity capacity and creation of 
additional carbon sink through forests and tree cover; 
(b) whether the Government has conducted any assessment of the progress made by various 
sectors, including power, transport, industry, agriculture and waste management, towards 
achieving the NDC targets and, if so, the details thereof including Kallakurichi constituency of 
Tamil Nadu; 
(c) the details of the measures taken by the Government during the last three years to accelerate 
climate mitigation and adaptation, particularly in climate-vulnerable States and coastal regions; 
and 
(d) the details of the monitoring and reporting mechanism adopted by the Government to track 
progress towards the NDC targets and India's long-term goal of achieving net-zero emissions 
by 2070? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI V ARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d)   India’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) comprises of three quantitative 
targets namely the reduction of overall emission intensity of our GDP, enhancing share of non-
fossil fuel-based energy resources in installed electric power capacity and creation of additional 
carbon sink.  
 
India has achieved a reduction of 37.38% in the emissions intensity of its GDP in 2022 from 
the 2005 level, against the NDC goal of reducing emissions intensity by 45% by 2030.  The 
share of cumulative installed electric power capacity from non-fossil fuel-based sources 
crossed 50% in June 2025, thereby achieving the NDC goal five years ahead the committed 
timeline. As of 30th June 2026, non-fossil fuel-based energy resources accounted for 54.18% 
of the country’s total installed electric power capacity.  India has created an additional carbon 
sink of 2.44 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent during 2005 to 2022, against the NDC goal of 
creating an additional carbon sink of 2.5–3.0 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent by 2030 through 
additional forest and tree cover.  The NDC targets for the year 2035 have been enhanced, with 
quantitative targets to reduce the emissions intensity of GDP by 47% from the 2005 level, 
achieve 60% cumulative installed electricity capacity from non-fossil fuel-based energy 

 
 
resources, and create carbon sink of 3.5 to 4.0 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent through forest 
and tree 4cover as compared to the baseline year of 2005. The NDC also includes five 
qualitative targets aimed at promoting sustainable lifestyles, adoption of climate friendly and 
cleaner path and enhancing adaptation capacity, etc. aligned with the goal of Viksit Bharat 
@2047. 
 
Our goal is to achieve the NDC targets at the national level, in line with the provisions of the 
Paris Agreement which calls for nationally determined contributions and national level 
reporting from the signatory Parties. 
 
The Government of India stands committed to implement its climate commitments through a 
whole-of-government approach. The National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) 
comprises of nine national missions in specific areas of agriculture, energy efficiency, green 
India, Himalayan eco-system, human health, solar energy, strategic knowledge on climate 
change, sustainable habitat, and water.  Six of its nine missions focus on adaptation for 
enhancing climate resilience of vulnerable communities. All these missions are 
institutionalized and implemented by their respective Nodal Ministries/Departments through 
various schemes and programs across many sectors.  
 
Several measures have been taken to accelerate climate mitigation and adaptation under these 
schemes and programs.  The focus is to promote renewable energy, electric mobility, 
sustainable transport and habitats; climate resilient agriculture; water conservation; enhance 
energy efficiency; forest and tree cover; restore ecosystems; reduce disaster risks, etc.   
 
Some of the flagship initiatives are National Green Hydrogen Mission; PM Surya Ghar: Muft 
Bijli Yojana; Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM); 
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) for clean energy technologies, including high-efficiency 
solar PV modules and Advanced Chemistry Cell batteries; initiatives related to Carbon Capture, 
Utilisation and Storage (CCUS) and Nuclear Energy Mission; and launch of hydrogen powered 
train which is step forward towards future ready and low-carbon sustainable transport.   For 
coastal regions, measures include, inter-al

Sanction of Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas in uncovered Districts of Telangana 
 
1292. Shri Kunduru Raghuveer: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has received proposals from the Government of 
Telangana for the establishment of 16 Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas (JNVs) in the 
uncovered districts of the said State; 
 
(b) if so , the details of the proposals received and the present status of their 
examination, district-wise; 
 
(c) the reasons for the delay, if any, in according approval to these proposals and the 
timeline fixed for their disposal; and 
 
(d) whether the Government proposes to sanction these 16 JNVs at the earliest, 
considering the objective of ensuring equitable access to quality residential 
education in educationally underserved districts of Telangana if so, the details 
thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (d): The Navodaya Vidyalaya Scheme envisages for opening of one Navodaya 
Vidyalaya (NV) in each district of the country. Opening of new NVs is a  continuous 
process which depends on the willingness of the concerned State Government/UT 
administration to make available requisite suitable land, free of cost, for construction 
of the permanent building and making available required temporary building, f ree of 
rent, to run the Vidyalaya till the permanent building is constructed. Sanction and 
opening of new NVs depends on approval by the competent authority as per extant 
procedures. At present, 16 NVs have been sanctioned in 16 districts of Telangana, 
out of which 15 NVs are functional.  District-wise list of sanctioned NVs in Telangana
