Impact of Geopolitical Developments in West Asia. 
 
 
1369. Shri Utkarsh Verma Madhur: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the fiscal and macroeconomic implications 
of recent geopolitical developments in West Asia on India's crude oil import bill, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the estimated impact of different international crude oil price scenarios on India's crude oil import bill, 
current account balance and fiscal position; 
(c) whether the Government has reviewed the likely impact of prolonged volatility in global crude oil 
prices on inflation, fuel subsidies and the growth projections for the current financial year, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(d) the sectors identified as most vulnerable to energy price volatility and the broad assessment of its impact 
on production and logistics costs; and 
(e) the contingency measures proposed by the Union Government to safeguard macroeconomic stability, 
contain inflationary pressures and minimise the impact of disruptions in the global energy market on the 
Indian economy? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a)-(c): The recent geopolitical developments in West Asia has adversely affected the countries globally, 
with major implications for crude -oil-importing emerging economies. According to the Reserve Bank of 
India's Financial Stability Report (June 2026), the recent geopolitical developments in West Asia led to an 
increase in international crude oil prices which has widened the crude oil import bill for India, with 
implications for current account deficit, similar to the experience during previous oil price shocks. 
However, the average Indian crude oil basket prices have eased significantly from USD 114.5 per barrel 
in April 2026 to USD 77.6 per barrel in July 2026 (up to 22nd July). The decline in crude oil prices, together 
with sustained growth in services exports and remittance receipts, is expected to support the external sector 
and mitigate pressures on the current account. Further, the recent measures announced by the Government 
and the Reserve Bank of India are expected to bolster capital inflows and he lp meet India's external 
financing requirements. 

While global uncertainties remain elevated, the high -frequency indicators for the first quarter of 2026 -27 
point to sustained momentum in economic activity and domestic demand. Also the average Consumer 
Price Index (CPI) inflation has remained moderate at 3.9 per cent during April-June 2026, reflecting price 
stability. Consistent with these trends, the Reserve Bank of India has projected real GDP growth at 6.6 per 
cent and Consumer Price Index  (CPI) inflation at 5.1 per cent for 2026 -27. RBI has further noted that 
global commodity price movements and prolonged supply chain disruptions pose challenges to the growth 
and inflation outlook. 
On the fiscal fron t, the Government has adopted a  balanced fiscal strategy  to ensure macroeconomic 
stability and resilience amidst the evolving situation. The Government continues to assess the implications 
of crude oil price volatility on the fiscal position, including fuel subsidies and revenue collections, and has 
undertaken appropriate fiscal measures, including calibrated revisions in the Special Additional Excise 
Duty on petrol and diesel and customs duties on select imports, to preserve fiscal space. The availability 
of fiscal buffers, including the Economic Stabilisation Fund, provides additional flexibility to respond to 
external shocks while maintaining the fiscal consolidation path. 
(d) The energy price volatility in the recent months has implications on the prices of petrochemical 
feedstock and intermediate products and related downstream sectors including plastics, packaging, textiles, 
pharmaceuticals, chemicals, automotive components and other manufacturing industries. According to the 
data published by the Department for Promotion of Indu stry and Internal Trade (DPII T), the increase in 
global energy prices has exerted some upward pressure on domestic producer prices, with Wholesale Price 
Index inflation increasing from 4.0 per cent in March 2026 to 9.9 per cent in June 2026. However, industrial 
activity has remained r esilient during the period. Growth in the Index of Industrial Production improved 
from 3.0 per cent in March 2026 to 5.1 per cent in May 2026, while the growth in the Nine Core Industries 
also strengthened from 2.9 per cent in March 2026 to 5.0 per cent in  June 2026, reflecting continued 
momentum in industrial activity despite higher input and logistics costs. 
(e) The Government has undertaken a range of measures to ensure availability of critical industrial 
inputs including energy, ease input cost pres

having a growing population and a large number of transferable Central 
Government employees, does not have a Kendriya Vidyal aya, causing 
hardship to the children of such employees, if so, the details thereof;

Project-specific proposals are examined under the statutory provisions of the Ancient

entries.t: Vocational Courses in Government Colleges in Muzaffarnagar
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 1372 
ANSWERED ON - 27/07/2026 
 
Vocational Courses in Government Colleges in Muzaffarnagar 
 
† 1372.    Shri Harendra Singh Malik : 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Government is considering to introduce vocational professional courses in 
Government colleges in Muzaffarnagar, keeping in view the district's major industries, 
namely sugar, steel and paper; 
(b) whether there is any proposal to link the proposed Centre of Invention, Innovation, 
Incubation and Training (CIIIT) at Muzaffarnagar with the Indian Institutes of Technology 
(IITs) for promoting high-end research, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether any specific guidelines have been issued under the National Education Policy 
(NEP), 2020 to provide internships for meritorious students from rural areas of 
Muzaffarnagar in local steel plants and sugar mills, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether the Government is considering any proposal for the establishment of a new Central 
University or a multidisciplinary research institution in Muzaffarnagar district and if so, the 
details thereof? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (d): Government of India launched National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 with an aim 
to provide holistic development of students. NEP 2020 envisages integration of pra ctical 
exposure and skill courses with regular programs. NEP 2020 also emphasizes the importance 
of industry-academic connect to enhance employability of students/youth.  
 
To achieve the objectives of NEP 2020 and to create a robust ecosystem of industry exposure 
in Higher Education Institutions (HEIs), University Grants Commission (UGC) has issued 
Apprenticeship Embedded Degree Programme (AEDP) Guidelines. Further, to ensure general 
exposure of industry to technical education students, AICTE has made inter nship mandatory 
component of model curriculum/programmes approved by AICTE.  
 
The UGC had approved 04 Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs) in Muzaffarnagar District 
Uttar Pradesh to offer skill -based programmes under the National Skills Qualification 
Framework (NSQF) during the academic year 2020–21. Under the National Apprenticeship 
Training Scheme (NATS)  of Ministry of Education , 02 colleges in Muzaffarnagar district, 
namely Shri Ram College and Sanatan Dharam College, have started AEDP courses and have 
signed Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with the Board of Apprenticeship Training 

(BoAT) (Northern Region), Kanpur, for providing     training to students. Further, a total of 7 
establishments / industries of Muzaffarnagar are registered with the BoAT (Northern Region), 
Kanpur for providing apprenticeship training to graduates under NATS.  
 
Government of India has also  established several premier Centrally Funded Institutions in 
Uttar Pradesh to provide high quality and multidisciplinary education to students such as Indian 
Institute Technology (IIT) Kanpur, Motilal Nehru National Institute of Technology (MNNIT) 
Allahabad, Banaras Hindu University, Aligarh Muslim University  etc. Government of India 
also provides financial support to State Governments under Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha 
Abhiyan (RUSA) / Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM-USHA) for specific State 
Government universities and colleges  to improve quality by ensuring their conformity to 
prescribed norms and standards. Under PM -USHA, a total of 6 units under the Multi -
Disciplinary Education and Research Universities (MERU) component have been approved in 
the State of Uttar Pradesh.  
 
Government of India has approved 204 Units in the State of Uttar Pradesh under various phases 
of the PM -USHA scheme including Rs 5 crore for Vijay Singh Pathik Government 
Mahavidyalaya, Kairana, in Muzaffarnagar district  to strengthen colleges component of PM -
USHA.  
 
As per information provided by Government of Uttar Pradesh, “Maa Shakumbhari University, 
Saharanpur”, a State Public University, alongwith its affiliated colleges, provides internship 
opportunities to students. Further there is no proposal to link Centre of Invention, Innovation, 
Incubation and Training (CIIIT), Muzaffarnagar with IIT.

(a) whether widespread closure and merger of thousands of primary and secondary 
Government schools in the country in recent years has adversely affected the 
implementation of RTE Act, 2009 which guarante es free and compulsory education for 
children aged 6-14 in neighbourhood schools; 
(b) if so, the details thereof;

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1376 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
ESTABLISHMENT OF AN ESI HOSPITAL AT TANDUR 
 
1376. SHRI KONDA VISHWESHWAR REDDY: 
 
         Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)whether the Government has received any proposal or 
representation from the State  Government of Telangana, public 
representatives, the Employees' State Insurance Corporation  
(ESIC), workers' organizations, industry associations or any other 
stakeholder for the  establishment of an Employees' State 
Insurance (ESI) Hospital at Tandur in Vikarabad district of  
Telangana; 
(b)if so, the details thereof and the action taken by the Government 
thereon; 
(c)whether the Government is aware that Tandur is a major cement 
manufacturing hub with several large cement industries, including 
Cement Corporation of India, employing a large number of workers 
covered under the ESI Scheme to facilitate insured worke rs and 
their families; and 
(d)whether the Government proposes to establish an ESI Hospital at 
Tandur and if so, the  details and timeline thereof and if not, the 
reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (d): A representation dated 03.10.2015 was received from the 
then Hon’ble Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha), Shri Konda 
Vishweshwar Reddy, regarding provision of ESI medical facilities for 
factory employees at Tandur, now in Vikarabad district, Telangana.  
  ESIC Headquarters accorded in-principle approval in 2018 
for establishment of a 2 -doctor ESI Dispensary at Tandur. However, 
as the Government of Telangana could not operationalise the 
dispensary, the in -principle approval has since been withdrawn on 
20.02.2026. The Insured Persons and their dep endants are presently 
availing primary medical care through ESIS Dispensary, Sadasivapeta 
and ESIC DCBO, Sadasivapeta.

NEW-AGE SKILLS UNDER PMKVY 
  
†1377. SHRI GYANESHWAR PATIL: 
            SHRI BHUMARE SANDIPANRAO ASARAM: 
  
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state: 
  
(a)    the number of beneficiaries trained under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana  
(PMKVY) during the last five years across the country particularly in Madhya Pradesh and 
Maharashtra; 
 
(b)   the details of funds allocated and utilized for implementation of PMKVY in the said States 
during the last three years and the current year; 
 
(c)   whether the Government is planning to expand the scope of PMKVY to Cover new -age 
skills like digital literacy, artificial intelligence, robotics or green technologies there under; and 
 
(d)  if so, the details thereof along with the steps being taken by the Government to promote 
the participation of women, Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes and other marginalized 
communities in PMKVY, State-wise including the said State? 
  
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) Under PMKVY, a  total of 36,44,663 candidates have been trained across the country 
during the last five financial years and the current financial year, including 3,93,767 in Madhya 
Pradesh and 1,75,389 in Maharashtra as on 30th June 2026. 
  
(b)  PMKVY4.0 is a demand driven scheme and there is no provision of fund allocation in the 
scheme to the States/UT. The details of funds utilized for implementation of PMKVY in the States 
of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra during the last three years and the current year is given 
below:  
 
State 2023-24 2024-25 2025-26 2026-27* 
Madhya Pradesh 43.17 205.84 26.98 3.67 
Maharashtra 32.09 44.44 6.05 1.01 
* Up to 30th June 2026. Amount in ₹ crore. 
  
(c)       Under PMKVY 4.0, training has been standardized through the National Skills 
Qualification Framework (NSQF), aligning courses with industry needs and national priorities. 
Under the Scheme, training have been aligned to the requirements of new -age and futuristic job 
roles such as AI, Robotics, Internet of Things (IoT ), Semiconductor, Drone technology, Solar, 3D 
Printing, etc. as per changing requirement and marked demand. To meet emerging technology 
demands, 600+ new -age and futuristic courses have been introduced.  As on 30 th June 

2026, around 5.44 lakh candidates have been trained in  new-age and futuristic job roles under 
PMKVY 4.0 across the country. 
  
(d)       PMKVY is a demand driven scheme accessible to every section of society including 
Women, Scheduled Castes (SCs)/ Scheduled Tribes (STs) and other marginalized communities. 
The Scheme does not envisage separate State -wise interventions, instead, it provides an 
inclusive framework applicable nationwide. To promote equitable access to skill development 
opportunities, the Scheme has a provision of Special Projects which are targeted towards 
ensuring coverage of under -represented social groups - SC/ ST/ Women/ PwDs and geographic 
areas such as Aspirational Districts, Tribal districts, etc. Special attention has been given to 
women, tribal communities, and other marginalized groups in rural areas to promote their 
participation in the skill development programs.  
  
In order to improve inclusivity by ensuring that SC, ST, women, and other marginalized 
communities can undertake skill training and eventually access gainful wage and self -
employment, boarding & lodging and transportation facilities are provided as per Common 
Norms. For non-residential training, conveyance/transportation costs are covered for women and 
PwDs. Additionally, ₹5,000 is provided for assistive devices, aids, and appliances for PwD  
candidates. All candidates are also covered under one -year accidental insurance for additional 
social protection.

1378.      DR. ALOK KUMAR SUMAN: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of employment generated under various Government 
initiatives during the last three years and the current year, year -
wise; 
(b) the measures taken by the Government to strengthen social 
security coverage for workers in the organised and unorganised 
sectors; 
(c) the details of the progress made by the Government in 
implementation of the e -Shram portal and other related welfare 
schemes in the country, State/UT-wise including Bihar; 
(d) whether the Government proposes to introduce additional 
employment-linked incentive measures in the country and if so, 
the details thereof; and 
(e) the steps taken by the Government to improve job opportunities 
for youth across the country? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (e): Official estimates of employment and unemployment in India 
are derived from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), conducted by 
the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation since 2017 –18. 
The PLFS methodology was revamped with effect from January 2025. 
The PLFS Annual Report 2025 is the first report in the revised series to 
present labour market estimates, covering the period from January to 
December 2025. 
 
As per latest PLFS report 2025, the estimated Worker Population 
Ratio (WPR) indicating employment on usual status for persons of age  15 
years and above has increased from 54.1% in 2022 to 57.4% in 2025; the 
estimated Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) on usual status for 
persons of age 15 years and above has increased from 56.1% in 2022 to 
59.3% in 2025 and the estimated Unemployment Rate (UR) has 
decreased from 3.6% in 2022 to 3.1% in 2025 in the country. 
 

The Ministry of Labour and Employment launched eShram portal 
(eshram.gov.in) which is a One -Stop-Solution for unorganized workers to 
have access to various social security schemes, Ministry of Labour and 
Employment launched the eShram – “One-Stop-Solution” on 21st October 
2024. eShram– “One-Stop-Solution” entails integration of different social  
security/ welfare schemes at single portal i.e., eShram. This enables 
unorganized workers registered on eShram to access social security 
schemes and see benefits availed by them so far, through eShram.So far, 
fifteen (15) schemes of different Central Ministries/ Departments have 
already been integrated/ mapped with the eShram to extend benefits and 
access to social security, health insurance and accidental claim to 
eShram cardholders. 
 
The Labour Codes were enacted to meet need for comprehensive 
labour reforms that formalize employment, simplify compliance through 
digital integration, strengthen social Security and ensure workplace 
safety and equality. The Codes will provide universal minimum wages 
and social security benefits for workers. 
 
The Labour Codes also have several enabling provisions which will 
promote formalisation and employment generation including social 
security and welfare of the workers. Such provisions include, 
formalization of employment through mandatory issue of appointment 
letter, universalisation of social security by extending coverage to 
organised, unorganised, gig and platform workers to strengthen their 
protection against employment -related vulnerabilities and enabling 
greater adaptability to new forms of work like gig & platform work and 
technology-driven employment models. 
 
Employment generation coupled with improving employability is a 
priority of the Government. Accordingly, Government is implementing 
various employment generation schemes/ programmes in the country. 
The details of various employment generation schemes/ programmes 
being implemented by the Government may be seen at   
https://dge.gov.in/dge/schemes_programmes. 
 
The Rozgar Mela is a major initiative aimed at prioritising 
employment generation. Since its inception, more than 12.5 lakh 
recruitment letters have been issued through 19 Rozgar Melas organised 
across the country. 
 

Government is also implementing Skill India Mission (SIM) to deliver 
skill, re-skill and up -skill training through an extensive network of skill 
development centres/ schools/ colleges /institutes etc. under various 
schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan

(NAPS) and Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training 
Institutes (ITIs) in the country. The SIM aims at enabling youth of India 
to get future ready, equipped with industry relevant skills.

1379. Shri Parimal Suklabaidya:

National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 in Assam particularly with regard to foundational literacy 
and numeracy, multidisciplinar y education and the use of mother tongue/local languages in the 
foundational stage, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of schools selected under the PM SHRI Scheme and the number of Eklavya 
Model Residential Schools sanctioned and operational in Assam, district-wise along with the steps 
taken to strengthen infrastructure, teacher training and vocational education;  
(c) the present status of digital education initiatives, including DIKSHA, SWAYAM and other 
online learning platforms in Assam, indicat ing teacher enrolment, student participation, internet 
connectivity, and availability of digital devices in rural, tea garden, tribal and flood-affected areas; 
and  
(d) the details of Central funds allocated, released and utilized for NEP implementation in  
Assam during the last three years, along with the major achievements, challenges and the roadmap 
for ensuring equitable and quality education across the State?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a): The Central Government continuously reviews the performance of the States. Accordingly, 
it may be informed that after the announcement of National Education Policy 2020 (NEP 2020), a 
number of transformative changes have taken place in school education for its  implementation. 
Several initiatives have been taken and the centrally sponsored schemes namely, Samagra Shiksha, 
PM Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI), Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM POSHAN) 

and Understanding Lifelong Learning for All in Society (ULLAS) have been aligned with the 
objectives and vision of NEP 2020. 
 NEP 2020 gives the highest priority to achieving universal Foundational Literacy and 
Numeracy (FLN) for all children by Grade 2  and accordingly, the Department launched National 
Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy (NIPUN Bharat Mission) 
under the aegis of the NEP and aligned with centrally sponsored scheme of Samagra Shiksha for 
early learning across States and Union Territories. 
  Implemented across the country, a range of interventions have been undertaken  under the 
Mission. These include nationwide implementation of Vidya Pravesh, a three -month school -
readiness module for all Grade 1 students; large -scale teacher and school head training through 
NISHTHA (National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement) ; FLN 
focusing on activity-based and child-centric pedagogy; provision of play-based and digital learning 
resources such as DIKSHA (Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing) ; Jaadui Pitara - a 
collection of Learning Teaching Material (LTM)  & e-Jaadui Pitara for children in the 3–8 age 
group; Primers developed in 121 Local Languages for foundational literacy and numeracy in 
mother tongue and teaching learning material for students.  
 Further, guidelines on co-location of Anganwadi Centres with primary schools, released on 
3rd September 2025, ensure convergence between school education and Anganwadis, supporting 
smoother transition from pre-school to Grade 1. 
 NEP 2020 stresses up on providing multidisciplinary and a holistic education across the 
sciences, social sciences, arts, humanities, and sports for a multidisciplinary world in order to 
ensure the unity and integrity of all knowledge.

for active implementation of NEP:

Axom.

 Notification of the age of admission as six years for class I. 
 Development of six months certification course on ECCE for the Anganwadi workers/pre-

 Alignment of medium of instructions across all four stages of education as per NEP 2020.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
DEPARTMENT FOR PROMOTION OF INDUSTRY AND INTERNAL TRADE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1381. 
      TO BE ANSWERED ON TUESDAY, THE 28TH JULY, 2026. 
 
EASE OF DOING BUSINESS IN SONIPAT 
 
1381.  SHRI SATPAL BRAHAMCHARI: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  whether the Government has reviewed the services being provided to 
industries, MSMEs  and startups under the Ease of Doing Business in the 
Sonipat Lok Sabha Constituency of Haryana; 
 
(b)  if so, the details of the major shortcomings identified in the review such as 
issues related to  company registration, statutory clearances, compliance 
procedures, digital services and investment facilitation; 
 
(c)  whether the Government has received complaints or suggestions to enhance 
the Ease of  Doing Business from the Sonipat Lok Sabha Constituency, if so, 
the details thereof; and 
 
(d)  the steps taken or proposed to be taken by the Government to rectify these 
shortcomings, simplify procedures, attract investment and provide more 
effective facilities to local entrepreneurs and MSMEs? 
 
ANSWER

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a): The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) 
undertakes periodic assessment of the Ease of Doing Business (EoDB ) 
ecosystem across States and Union Territories through initiatives such as the 
Business Reforms Action Plan (BRAP), assessment of State Single Window 
Systems and other regulatory reform initiatives. BRAP 2024 assessed 
implementation of 434 reforms coverin g areas such as business entry, 
investment facilitation, labour regulation, utility permits, startups, services 
sector, inspections and online service delivery through a government -to-
Business feedback mechanism. Haryana was assessed under this framework. 
However, DPIIT does not undertake EoDB assessments at the constituency 
level. 
(b): As per BRAP 2024, Haryana demonstrated substantial implementation of the 
reform agenda. From a total of 434 reforms, 342 were assessed for 

implementation. Out of 342 applicable reforms, 89.5% were reported as 
implemented, 2.9% were eliminated through Government Process Re -
engineering, 7.0% as not applicable due to judicial orders, and only 0.6% were 
reported as not implemented. Haryana was ca tegorised as an “Aspirer” State 
in BRAP 2024, including in the area of Regulatory Compliance Burden. The 
State also recorded relatively stronger performance in specific Ease of Doing 
Business areas such as Business Entry, Land Administration and the sector -
specific area of Health. 
(c): DPIIT regularly receives feedback and suggestions from businesses, investors, 
MSMEs, startups and other stakeholders through consultations, workshops and 
feedback-based assessments such as BRAP. The BRAP 2024 feedback 
exercise in Haryana covered 5,848 users across various reform areas. 
Suggestions received from users included simplification of documentation 
requirements, improvement in portal speed and reliability, introduction of 
integrated dashboards for applications and pay ments, enhancement of user 
interface and user experience, enabling easier document uploads, improving 
transparency in processing of applications, and ensuring seamless payment 
and refund mechanisms. However, such record and feedback constituency -
wise is not maintained. 
(d): The Government has undertaken several measures to improve Ease of Doing 
Business and strengthen the regulatory ecosystem across the country, 
including Haryana, such as: - 
i. Implementation of the Business Reforms Action Plan (BRAP) to promo te 
business-friendly regulatory reforms across States and Union Territories. 
ii. Assessment and strengthening of State Single Window Systems through 
a detailed reform framework and guidebook to improve investor facilitation 
and online service delivery. 
iii. Development of the District Business Reforms Action Plan (District BRAP) 
to improve regulatory governance, investor facilitation, public service 
delivery and entrepreneurship promotion at the district level. 
iv. Implementation of the Reducing Compliance Burden  (RCB) initiative 
through simplification, rationalisation, digitisation and decriminalisation of 
regulatory compliances. More than 47,865 compliances have been 
reduced across the country. 
v. Encouraging States and UTs to ensure complete end -to-end online 
delivery of services, improve portal reliability and usability, strengthen 
grievance redressal mechanisms, simplify documentation requirements, 
introduce transparent renewal mechanisms, and enhance awareness 
regarding digital service offerings. 
vi. Continuous stakeholder consultations and sharing of best practices with 
States and UTs to improve regulatory efficiency, transparency and

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF STEEL

FOR ANSWER ON 28.07.2026  
 
 
 
CHALLENGES FACED BY THE STEEL SECTOR 
 
 
 
1382.   DR. T SUMATHY ALIAS THAMIZHACHI THANGAPANDIAN: 
 
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the challenges faced by the steel sector in 
increasing production while reducing carbon and pollutant emissions and if so, the 
details thereof; 
 
(b) the manner in which the Government is aligning the steel sector’s production 
growth strategy with decarbonisation measures, including energy efficiency, green 
steel, hydrogen-based technologies and cleaner production processes and the 
outcomes achieved so far; 
 
(c) the details of steps being taken to ensure compliance with the European Union’s 
Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism including preparedness of domestic steel 
producers, reporting mechanisms and support provided during the last five years; and 
 
(d) the manner in which the Ministry is coordinating with other concerned Ministries to 
mitigate adverse trade and competitiveness effects arising from carbon-related border 
measures? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE          (SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
(a)&(b): Ministry of Steel released a report titled "Greening the Steel Sector in 
India: Roadmap and Action Plan" on the basis of the recommendations of the 14 Task 
Forces constituted by this Ministry for this purpose which provides the details of 
challenges being faced by the steel sector for green transition, roadmap for green steel 
and sustainability, towards net-zero target by 2070. The report is available on Ministry 
of Steel's website. 
(c)&(d): The Government has undertaken the following initiatives for green 
transition of the steel sector: 
(i) Ministry of Steel released the Taxonomy for Green Steel for defining and 
categorizing the low emission steel. Green Steel Taxonomy provides a framework for 
production of green steel, creation of market for green steel and seeking financial 
support. During Financial Year 2025-26, 90 steel units have been awarded green steel 
certification under the notified Green Steel Taxonomy Framework, accounting for a 
total green steel production of 12.4 million tonnes.   
Contd…..2/- 

: 2 : 
 
(ii) Four pilot projects have been awarded for implementation of pilot projects for 
use of hydrogen in steel sector under National Green Hydrogen Mission launched by 
Ministry of New & Renewable Energy.  
(iii) National Solar Mission launched by Ministry of New and Renewable Energy in 
January, 2010 promotes the use of solar energy and also helps to reduce the emission 
of steel industry. 
(iv) Ministry of Power has notified Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) on 
28.06.2023 for regulating Indian Carbon Market across various industrial sectors, 
which is also applicable to steel plants. 
  Ministry of Steel works in close coordination with the Ministries/Departments 
concerned to address the trade effects arising from carbon-related border measures.

entries.t: Implementation and Impact of PMKSY in Tamil Nadu
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA  
 UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1384 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 28TH JULY, 2026 
 
IMPLEMENTATION AND IMPACT OF PMKSY IN TAMIL NADU 
 
1384.  SHRI MANI A: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण 
मंğी be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the implementation and impact of the 
Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY)-(Per Drop More Crop) in 
Dharmapuri district, Tamil Nadu, considering the district's recurring water scarcity 
and dependence on horticulture and if so, the details thereof;  
(b) whether the existing coverage of drip and sprinkler irrigation systems in 
Dharmapuri is adequate to meet the irrigation needs of small and marginal farmers 
cultivating mango, millets, vegetables and other crops and if so, the details thereof;  
(c) whether the Government proposes to expand access to micro irrigation 
through simplified procedures, enhanced awareness campaigns, technical 
assistance and timely subsidy support for farmers in Dharmapuri district and if so, 
the details thereof; and  
(d) the measures being taken to promote water use efficiency, improve irrigation 
coverage, enhance crop productivity and strengthen climate-resilient agriculture in 
Dharmapuri district under PMKSY? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) : The Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) of Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) was 
implemented in the Country including Tamil Nadu from the year 2015-16 to 2021-22 
as a component of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY). From the year 
2022-23, the scheme is being implemented under the Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi 
Vikas Yojana (PMRKVY).  
  

 
 As informed by the State of Tamil Nadu, Micro Irrigation systems is being 
promoted in the State through PDMC and large number of farmers are adopting it.   
Adoption of Micro Irrigation systems has enabled farmers to cultivate more area, get 
more yield when compared to conventional method of irrigation. Consequently, the 
livelihood and economic well-being of the farming community have improved.  
 
(b) :  The State has informed that about 80% of the financial allocation is allocated to 
Small/Marginal farmers under PDMC scheme. In Dharmapuri district, majority of the 
farmers come under Small/Marginal category. With the adoption of micro irrigation 
systems, farmers are able to undertake cultivation throughout the year, ensuring 
sustainable agricultural production. In Tamil Nadu, Small and Marginal Farmers are 
provided with 100% subsidy for the installation of micro irrigation systems through the 
PDMC scheme and State's additional share thereby reducing the financial burden on 
Small and Marginal Farmers. Further, the 5% GST applicable on micro irrigation 
components is also borne by the State from its additional share. In Dharmapuri district, 
since inception of the scheme in 2015-16, 94982 ha area has been covered under 
Micro Irrigation.  
 
(c) : The State Government has taken initiatives to expand access to Micro Irrigation 
through the simplified procedures i.e. right from registration of beneficiaries to final 
fund release are carried out through portal to ensure transparency, timely 
implementation, and efficient monitoring. In addition, farmers are regularly updated of 
the status of their applications through the portal, enabling them to track the progress 
of their application. The awareness is created among the farmers about PDMC 
scheme through extension officials during their field visits, Mass contact Programmes, 
Farmer’s Grievance Day, various other meetings held at village, block and district level 
and through social media tools like Instagram, Twitter and Whatsapp. Extension 
officials also provide technical assistance for maintenance of Micro Irrigation systems, 
acid treatment etc.    
 
(d):   As informed by the State, priority is accorded to Dharmapuri district in the 
allocation of funds considering its recurring water scarcity and the predominance of 
horticultural crops. Efforts are being taken to bring more area under Micro irrigation in 
the district in order to promote effective usage of available ground water and orient 
farmers towards climate-resilient agriculture. 
 
 
*****

MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
DEPARTMENT FOR PROMOTION OF INDUSTRY AND INTERNAL TRADE

1387.  DR. ANAND KUMAR: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  whether the Government has taken any special diplomatic, commercial or 
economic initiatives to attract investments from multinational companies of 
Europe and Japan in the  aspirational districts of the country, if so, the details 
thereof; 
 
(b)  whether any institutional coordination mechanism has been developed, in 
collaboration with district Panchayats and other local bodies, for the effective 
implementation of such investment proposals, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c)  the concrete strategy made by the Government to generate employment 
generation, promote skill development, export promotion and reduce the 
regional disparities through such investments; and 
 
(d)  the details of the Foreign Direct Investment received in the aspirational districts 
during the last three years, country-wise and sector-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (d): NITI Aayog launched the Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) in 
January 2018, wherein, 117 districts were identified as Aspirational Districts. 
ADP monitors the progress of these Districts based on the delta ranking 
method, which rewards Districts for their quarterly progress in the 49 Key 
Performance Indicators (KPIs)  across sectors such as health & nutrition, 
education, agriculture & water resources, financial inclusion & skill development 
and basic infrastructure. The broad strategy of ADP rests on 3 Cs – 
Convergence (between Central and State Schemes), Collaboration  (between 
Centre, State, District Administration, Development Partners and Citizens) and 
Competition (between Districts). The projects under ADP Phase I (Year 2018 
to 2022) and ADP Phase II (Year 2022 to 2024, further extended to FY 2025 & 
2026) have been funded by Official Development Assistance (ODA) from  
Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) which is an incorporated  
administrative institution under the Government of Japan. 

An investment decision is made by a company based on multiple factors 
including the risk to the capital deployed as well as the returns from the 
investment. The investment promotion eﬀorts project the potential that the 
country oﬀers for the investors including facts about the infrastructure, 
incentives, compliances, etc. to facilitate decision making by the investor. The 
country-wise and sector -wise details of FDI Equity Inflows Reported in 
Aspirational Districts from Financial Year 2023 -24 to 2025 -26 are placed as 
Annexure.

(a) whether the Government is implementing any policy relating to the 
Medical Certification of  Cause of Death (MCCD) in the country, if so, the

1389. DR. BACHHAV SHOBHA DINESH: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether the Government is aware of cases where State-level Fertilizer Control 
Laboratories and Central testing facilities such as the National Test House have given 
contradictory findings on the same fertilizer sample, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b)  the procedure and prescribed timeline under the Fertilizer Control Order, 1985, for third-

(c)  whether any data is maintained on cases where an initial "non-standard" finding was 
later overturned on re-verification during the last three years and if so, the number of such

(d)  the steps being taken by the Government to reduce delays in re-verification, particularly

MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) to (c):   As per existing provision of Fertilizer Control Order (FCO), 1985 which was 
amended on 13-12-2024, out of the three samples collected by the Fertiliser Inspectors, 
one sample is given to the dealer or importer or manufacturer or pool handling agency or 
marketer as the case may be and the second sample is sent to the in-charge of the 
laboratory and the third sample is kept in the custody of designated authority appointed by

 Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान

(a) whether farmers in various states of the country are raising key demands

(b) whether any concrete decision has been taken by the Government on the 
demands of the farmers including the legal guarantee of MSP and if so, the timeline 
fixed for implementing the same and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether is it not the fact that if MSP comes under as Guarantee, it would help 
farmers for increasing their earning from the crops output as well as avoid 
exploitation by the middle man as big stockiest; 
(d) whether farmers are under constant distress due to the rising cost of cultivation, 
decline in income and economic insecurity; and 
(e) if so, the policy steps being taken by the Government towards a permanent 
solution for providing a legal guarantee of MSP for the crops of the farmers and if

ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛमंũी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
 (a) to (e): Time to time, suggestions/representations from farmers’ organizations and 
other stakeholders are received regarding the Minimum Support Price (MSP). 
 
Every year, Government fixes Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for 22 
mandated agricultural crops for the country as a whole, based on the 
recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP), after 
considering the views of the State Governments and Central Ministries/Departments 
concerned.  
  

While recommending MSPs, CACP considers important factors like cost of 
production, overall demand-supply conditions, domestic and international prices, 
inter-crop price parity, terms of trade between agricultural and non-agricultural 
sectors, the likely effect on the rest of the economy, besides ensuring rational 
utilization of land, water and other production resources. Before recommending 
MSP, CACP also consults stakeholders (including Central and State Governments, 
procurement agencies, industry associations, farmers' representatives, research 
institutions etc.) and inputs received are also utilized for finalizing the 
recommendations by the Commission. 
The Union Budget for 2018-19 had announced the pre-determined principle to 
keep MSPs at levels of at least one and half times of the cost of production. 
Accordingly, Government had increased MSPs for all mandated Kharif, Rabi and 
other commercial crops with a minimum return of 50 percent over all India weighted 
average cost of production from year 2018-19 onwards. 
Government offers to procure agricultural crops through designated 
procurement agencies and farmers have the option to sell their produce to the 
government agencies or in the open market whichever is advantageous to them.  
Out of the total production, only marketable surplus is available for 
procurement by Government agencies when market price of these produce fall 
below the MSP. Government procures cereals and coarse cereals through Food 
Corporation of India (FCI) and other designated State Agencies to provide price 
support to the farmers. Procurement of pulses, oilseeds and copra is done under 
Price Support Scheme under umbrella scheme of Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay 
Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA), on the request of the concerned State 
Government as per the guidelines as and when market price of these produce fall 
below the MSP. Procurement agencies under PM-AASHA Scheme are National 
Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd (NAFED) and National 
Co-operative Consumers' Federation of India Ltd. (NCCF). Cotton and Jute are also 
procured by Government at MSP through Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) and Jute 
Corporation of India (JCI), respectively. 
 
Increased MSP has benefited farmers of the country which are evident from 
data of procurement and MSP amount paid to the farmers. The details of

authorised bodies in addressing the deficiencies found in the applications and 
assists them to comple te the application. The GI Registry also provides 
handhold support to the applicant throughout the process. For more assistance, 
applicants can contact the GI Registry at e -mail: gir -ipo@nic.in or 044 -

Availability of Bharat Taxi in Purvanchal Areas of UP 
1392.  Shri Rajeev Rai: 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the facility of Bharat Taxi is available in the State of Uttar Pradesh especially in 
Purvanchal, if so, the details thereof;  
(b) the details of the total expenditure incurred by the Government on the development, 
promotion, maintenance and operation of Bharat Taxi, along with the source of funding; and  
(c) whether the Government has assessed the performance of the Bharat Taxi platform since its 
launch, including complaints received, customer satisfaction, fare competitiveness etc. and 
compared its performance with private taxi aggregators and if so, the deta ils and the 
corrective measures taken thereon?  
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
(सहकारिता मंत्री) (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) Bharat Taxi is a cooperative -led digital App mobility platform operated by Sahakar Taxi 
Cooperative Limited (STCL), a multistate cooperative society, registered under the MSCS Act 2002. 
Bharat Taxi is providing its services in the cities of Delhi-NCR, Gujarat and Maharashtra. At present, 
it has not been officially launched in Uttar Pradesh especially in Purvanchal . 
(b) The Government has not incurred any expenditure on the development, promotion, maintenance, 
or operation of Bharat Taxi. Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL ) funds the development  
promotion, maintenance and operation  of Bharat Taxi through its own capital.  
(c) The performance of the Bharat Taxi Application is reviewed periodically by Sahakar Taxi 
Cooperative Limited (STCL). The review covers key operational and service -related parameters, 

Page 2 of 2 
 
including customer experience, grievances received, fare competitiveness, platform performance, 
and the effectiveness of technology systems. The Application is also benchmarked against prevailing 
practices in the taxi aggregation sector to identify areas for improvement. 
Based on the findings of such reviews and feedback received from users, appropriate corrective 
measures are undertaken, wherever required. These include strengthening the technology platform, 
addressing software-related issues, enhancing platform features, reviewing fare-related aspects, and 
improving service delivery. Regular technical and operational monitoring is also carried out to 
support the reliable and efficient functioning of the platform.

1393.  SHRI ARUN GOVIL: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  whether Meerut in Uttar Pradesh is a world -class hub for the manufacturing of 
sports goods, gym/fitness equipment and sports wear; 
 
(b)  the percentage of exports to the USA out of the total exports originating from 
Meerut; 
 
(c)  the extent to which the exports of this industry have been affected due to the 
US-Iran war; 
 
(d)  the details of the assistance/facilities proposed to be provided by the 
Government to this industry affected by the US-Iran war; and 
 
(e)  whether the Government proposes to provide assistance/facilities to the sports 
goods manufacturing industry in preparation for the proposed 2030 
Commonwealth Games, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a): Industries is a State subject. Both the Central Government and the State 
Governments implement various policies and programmes to create  an 
enabling eco-system for the development of the industrial sector in the 
country. Meerut is a recognised centre  for the manufacturing of sports goods, 
gym/fitness equipment, and sports wear in the country. 
(b): Based on the Sports Goods and Toys Export Promotion Council (SGEPC)’s 
membership records during the Financial Year 2025 -26, the total exports of 
Sports Goods originating from Meerut was ₹ 557.84 Crore and  the exports 
from Meerut to USA was ₹ 98.40 crore which accounts for approximately 
17.64%. 
(c): No significant or quantified impact on Meerut's sports goods exports has  been 
officially reported. The US-Iran conflict primarily disrupted shipping through the 
Strait of Hormuz and Meerut's exports are directed mainly to the USA and 
Europe - disruption to this specific industry has been minimal. However, the 

eﬀect has been widely indirect, via marginally higher fr eight and war risk 
insurance costs on international shipping. 
(d): No dedicated sector specific assistance package/facilities have been 
announced for the sports goods industry in relation to the US -Iran war 
specifically. However as a broad based response, a "Resilience & Logistics 
Intervention for Export Facilitation (RELIEF)" package was announced by 
Ministry of Commerce & Industry on 19th March 2026, covering elevated freight 
costs and war risk insurance premiums. 
Further, under Export Promotion Policy 20 25-30 Uttar Pradesh, Exporters are 
eligible to avail assistance which includes: 
 Gateway Port Freight Assistance: Inland freight reimbursement at 30% 
of total charges; annual cap raised from ₹20 lakh to ₹40 lakh per exporter; 
per-container caps doubled (20 ft: ₹20,000; 40 ft: ₹40,000). 
 Air Freight Rationalisation Assistance: Minimum 30% of freight 
charges or ₹50/kg, up to ₹40 lakh per exporter. 
 Reimbursement of 30% of the ECGC premium, subject to a maximum 
of ₹15 lakh per MSME exporter. 
 
These measures are intended to mitigate the impact of increased logistics, 
freight and insurance costs and support the continuity of exports. 
(e): Presently there is no exclusive  assistance/facilities to the sports goods 
manufacturing industry for the proposed 2030 Commonwea lth Games. 
However, sports goods manufacturers in Meerut continue to be supported 
through the Uttar Pradesh Export Promotion Policy 2025–30 and other MSME 
support initiatives of the State Government. Further, Meerut has been 
identified as a flagship district for Sports goods under One District One Product 
(ODOP) which is an initiative by the Department for Promotion of Industry and 
Internal Trade (DPIIT) with the aim of selecting, branding, and promoting at 
least one product from each district of the countr y to enable holistic growth 
across all regions. 
Several steps have been undertaken to promote and enhance the visibility  of 
products identified under the ODOP initiative. These steps include; facilitating 
participation in domestic and international exhibit ions, capacity building 
initiatives in collaboration with various agencies; e -commerce on -boarding 
drives for Government e-Marketplace (GeM)- ODOP Bazaar which showcases 
and stocks India’s best ODOP products. For promoting ODOP at international 
level, engagement with Indian Missions abroad, virtual buyer sellers meet and 
participation in international exhibitions have been undertaken.

Traditional Fisheries 
1396. Dr. M P Abdussamad Samadani:  
Will the Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware that overcapacity and unregulated expansion of the 
mechanised trawler fleet have severely degraded the inshore benthic environment along India's 
continental shelf; 
(b) the concrete steps taken to strictly enforce the 5 -nautical-mile prohibition zone for mechanised 
trawlers to safeguard traditional fishers; and 
(c) whether the Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) will conduct comprehensive 
at-sea benthic surveys, rather than relying solely on landing data, to assess true ecosystem health? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (ICAR -CMFRI) has assessed that the 
trawl-based landings have shown no palpable decline in fish landings during 2021-2025. As per the 
Marine Fish Stock Status of India (2022) publication of the ICAR-CMFRI, the marine fish stocks 
of the Indian waters are in good health , and 91.1% of the 135 fish stocks evaluated in different 
regions of the Indian EEZ were found sustainable.   
(b) ‘Fisheries’ is a state subject, and each Coastal State has its Marine Fishing Regulation Act 
(MFRA) for governance of fishing activities within the territorial waters up to 12 nautical miles 
from the baseline, including zoning of fishing areas for traditional and mechanised fishing vessels, 
mesh‑size and gear regulations, seasonal fishing bans, minimum legal-size limits for fish capture, 
prohibition of destructive fishing practices such as paired/bull trawling and use of artificial/LED 
lights, and prevention of juvenile fishing. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India is 
implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), under which activities such 
as installation of Turtle Excluder Devices (TEDs) in trawl nets for protecting the sea turtles, sea 
ranching, and ins tallation of artificial reefs in coastal waters towards enhancing fish stocks are 
undertaken for safeguarding the livelihood interests of traditional fishers. PMMSY also promotes 
acquisition of deep-sea fishing vessels, open-sea cage culture, and mariculture, including seaweed 
farming to divert fishing pressure away from the inshore coastal waters. 
 
(c) The ICAR-CMFRI has informed that it conducts long -term monitoring of marine fisheries 
and ecosystems using a statistically validated, FAO -recommended stratified multistage random 
sampling design. The ICAR -CMFRI generates high-quality time-series data on fi sh landings and 
fishing effort from over 1,300 landing centres along India's 11,000 km coastline to assess fish stock 
status and infer ecosystem changes. Further, Institute also informed that it implements national 
programmes on marine biodiversity, benthic ecosystem health, trophic interactions, and the impacts 
of bottom trawling.

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  कृͪष एवं ͩकसान

(a) The eligibility criteria and approval process for sanctioning subsidies under National 
Horticulture Board (NHB) Schemes;  
(b) Whether the Government proposes to review the existing approval mechanism to 
ensure transparency and avoid any perceived conflict of interest in the grant of such 
subsidies;  
(c) Whether any serving Union Minister, Member of Parliament, or their immediate 
family members have received subsidy under schemes of the National Horticulture

ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी   (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) : Financial assistance under the National Horticulture Board (NHB) Schemes is 
provided in the form of credit-linked back-ended capital investment subsidy to eligible 
farmers and entrepreneurs for development of commercial horticulture, protected 
cultivation, post-harvest management and cold chain infrastructure. The schemes are 
open to all eligible applicants, including individuals, partnerships, companies, 
cooperatives and other eligible legal entities, subject to fulfillment of the prescribed 
eligibility conditions. The project land should be owned by the applicant or held on lease 
for a minimum period of ten years, duly reflected in the revenue records. The 
applications are processed through a transparent multi-tier mechanism. 
  

 The financing bank first sanctions the term loan and appraises the project. 
Thereafter, NHB scrutinizes the application through the Project Examination 
Committee (PEC) before issuing the Grant of Clearance (GoC). After completion of the 
project, a joint inspection is carried out by NHB, the financing bank and the State 
Government. The subsidy claim is thereafter considered by the Inter-Ministerial Project 
Approval Committee (PAC), comprising representatives of the Ministry of Agriculture & 
Farmers Welfare, ICAR, APEDA, Directorate of Marketing & Inspection (DMI), NITI 
Aayog and the Ministry of Food Processing Industries, before approval. The subsidy is 
released only to the financing bank and is adjusted against the beneficiary’s loan after 
successful completion of the prescribed lock-in period, in accordance with the Scheme 
Guidelines. 
(b):  The National Horticulture Board (NHB) processes all applications for financial 
assistance under its Schemes through a transparent mechanism in accordance with 
the prescribed Scheme Guidelines. All eligible applicants are treated equally and 
applications are considered solely on the basis of the eligibility criteria and compliance 
with the provisions of the Scheme. 
To further enhance transparency, efficiency and ease of doing business, the 
application processing system has been progressively digitized. The earlier hybrid 
system involving submission of both online and physical documents has been replaced 
with a completely online process. Further, the mandatory pre-inspection of certain 
categories of projects has been dispensed with and technology-enabled verification 
has been introduced. Applicants upload the geo-coordinates of the project site through 
the NHB mobile application, which are verified by NHB using GIS/Google Maps and 
other digital tools, thereby reducing physical interface while ensuring authenticity of 
project location. 
In addition, based on the experience gained during implementation, NHB 
periodically reviews the Scheme Guidelines to strengthen safeguards against multiple 
benefit of subsidy through different legal entities or capacities, prescribe suitable 
exclusions wherever considered necessary, and address any potential conflict of 
interest. 
  

(c): The details of serving Union Ministers, Members of Parliament and their immediate 
family members, who have received financial assistance under the Schemes of the 
National Horticulture Board during the last five years, are as under: 
Shri LUMBA RAM (MP, Sirohi, Rajasthan) in 2025 and Sh. BHAGIRATH 
CHOUDHARY, MoS.MoA and FW (MP, Ajmer, Rajasthan) in 2026.  
Shri Bhagirath Choudhary, has communicated that he has refunded the subsidy 
to the bank concerned under the scheme. The concerned bank  has been 
directed to return the subsidy amount to NHB. 
(d): The existing NHB Scheme Guidelines do not contain any specific provision 
regarding conflict of interest or recusal in respect of applications submitted by public 
functionaries or their family members.

incurred, employment generated, increase in fish production and progress achieved in exports 
under the first phase of the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) during the last 
five years, State-wise:

the first phase of PMMSY, if so, the details thereof,

proposed new initiatives relating to inland fisheries, aquaculture, shrimp farming, cold chain,

incentive package for providing Fish Farmer Producer Organisations (FFPOs) with financial

THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d) : The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, 
Government of India with effect from the Financial Year 2020-21 is implementing the Pradhan 
Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)  for holistic development of fisheries and 
aquaculture sector in the country. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India during 
the last six years has approved fisheries development projects of 34 States/U nion Territories 
and other implementing agencies amounting to Rs.21,461 crore with Central share of Rs.9,571

implementing agencies under PMMSY. State-wise details of the projects approved, central 
share and funds released during the last six years are furnished at Annexure-I.

augmentation of fish production, enhancement of fisheries exports and creating of livelihood 
and employment opportunities. The fish production in the country has increased from 141.64 
lakh tonne (2019 -20) to an all time record of 197. 75 lakh tonne (2024 -25), creation of direct 
and indirect employment opportunities to 58 lakh persons in fisheries and aquaculture related 
activities, increase of fisheries export from Rs.46,663 crore (2019 -20) to Rs.73,890  crore 
(2025-26). The National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog, Government of India 
has evaluated the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana  along with other Centrally 
Sponsored Schemes and the evaluation study while underlining the impact created by PMMSY 
in the fisheries sector has recommended its continuation. The PMMSY has been continued till 
September, 2026 in its existing form . During the current financial year (2026-27), a Central 
budget of Rs.2500 crore has been allocated for this scheme.  
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) implemented by the Department of 
Fisheries, Government of India inter-alia provides financial assistance for setting up of Fish 
Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPOs) to economically empowe r the fishers, fish farmers 
and enhance their bargaining power. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India during 
the last five years (FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26) has approved projects worth of Rs.544.86 crore 
for formation of 2195 FFPOs  in the country  with support in the form of incubation cost, 
management cost and equity grant.

including Panchayat-city connectivity. 
  
However, Ministry of Rural Development has informed that Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana

 UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 1407 
ANSWERED ON 28.07.2026 
 
  DIGITAL CONNECTIVITY INITIATIVES  
  
1407. SHRI MANICKAM TAGORE B:  
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to State:   
(a)  whether digital connectivity initiatives have been extended to Panchayats, if so, the 
details thereof and effectiveness in bridging rural-urban digital divide; 
  
(b)  whether coordination between Central and State agencies is adequate for connectivity 
projects, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons for delays and inefficiencies in 
implementation; 
  
(c)  whether public transport services have been expanded to link rural Panchayats with 
cities, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons for limited accessibility for rural 
populations; 
  
(d)  whether private sector participation has been encouraged in rural connectivity projects, if 
so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons for underutilization of private investment 
opportunities; and 
  
(e)  whether the Government has identified connectivity-deficient Panchayats, if so, the 
details thereof and the targeted measures proposed to address regional disparities in 
infrastructure development? 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)  
  
(a) & (b)  The Ministry of Panchayati Raj has undertaken various digital governance 
initiatives under the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP) to strengthen the functioning of 
Panchayati Raj Institutions. The Ministry has developed digital applications such as 
eGramSwaraj, AuditOnline and mActionSoft to facilitate planning, financial management, 
accounting, audit, monitoring of works and service delivery by Panchayats. The Ministry also 
continuously upgrades these applications and integrates them with other Government digital 
platforms to improve efficiency, transparency and accountability in Panchayat governance. 
The Ministry works in coordination with the respective State Governments and other 
Ministries/Departments, wherever required, for the implementation and integration of digital 
governance initiatives.  

2 
 
In addition, as per the information furnished by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), 
the BharatNet project is being implemented in a phased manner to create a broadband network 
connecting all Gram Panchayats (GPs) across the country. The BharatNet infrastructure is made 
available to Telecom Service Providers (TSPs) and Internet Service Providers (ISPs) for 
extending broadband services to Gram Panchayats, rural areas, Government institutions, schools 
and other users. As of June 2026, out of 2,63,447 Gram Panchayats/ Traditional Local Bodies 
(TLBs) planned to be connected under BharatNet, 2,21,780 Gram Panchayats have been 
connected for the provision of high-speed broadband services. 
Further, the Amended BharatNet Programme (ABP) was approved by the Union Cabinet on 
04.08.2023 for upgradation of the existing BharatNet Phase-I and Phase-II network, creation of 
network in the remaining Gram Panchayats, and operation and maintenance of the network for a 
period of ten years.  
(c) to (e)  The development and operation of public transport services, including connectivity 
between rural areas and urban centres, as well as the promotion of private sector participation in 
connectivity infrastructure, are primarily the responsibility of the respective State Governments 
and the concerned Ministries/Departments. The Ministry of Panchayati Raj does not implement 
any scheme specifically for expansion of public transport services or connectivity infrastructure 
linking rural Panchayats with cities. Accordingly, information regarding the expansion of such 
services, private sector participation in such projects, and identification of connectivity-deficient 
Panchayats is not maintained by this Ministry.

(a):  The Ministry of Textiles launched National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM) in the

(Promotion and Market Development) of NTTM, a total of 47 National/International conferences

(c) & (d):  The National Technical Textiles Mission is focused on promoting indigenous 
development and commercialisation of value -added Technical Textiles products, including 
critical segments such as agro -textiles, geo -textiles, medical textiles, industrial textiles,  
protective textiles, and sportech, among others. The Mission also undertakes creation of 
awareness among stakeholders, user Ministries/Departments, and the general public regarding 
the applications and benefits of Technical Textiles through workshops, con ferences, exhibitions, 
and skill development programmes. Further, use of Technical Textiles items has also been 
recommended for mandatory adoption in specified applications by various end -user 
Ministries/Departments/State Governments, wherever feasible, to  create sustained domestic 
demand. 
 
  The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Textiles, which covers Technical 
Textiles as one of its focus segments, has been introduced to enable the textile sector to achieve 
scale and competitiveness at a global  level. The Scheme is designed to address India's structural 
gaps in the Man -Made Fibre (MMF) and Technical Textiles value chain, and to encourage 
investment in high value -added segments, thereby enhancing production capacity, technology 
adoption, and expo rt competitiveness of the sector.  
 
  These measures, taken together, are expected to give a significant impetus to the growth of 
the domestic Technical Textiles industry and to enhance its share in global trade.

क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛमंũी    (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) : The Government is implementing various schemes to address infrastructure gaps and 
to strengthen post-harvest infrastructure across the country. Agriculture Infrastructure 
Fund (AIF) facilitates medium- to long-term debt financing for creation of post-harvest 
management infrastructure and viable farming assets, including warehouses, cold stores, 
pack houses, sorting and grading units, assaying units, primary processing centres, 
ripening chambers, logistics facilities etc. The Scheme provides 3% interest subvention 
and credit guarantee support on loans up to ₹2 crore for eligible borrowers, subject to a 
maximum lending rate of 9% per annum. The Mission for Integrated Development of 
Horticulture (MIDH) promotes, holistic growth of the horticulture sector covering fruits, 
vegetables, root and tuber crops, mushrooms, spices, flowers, aromatic & medicinal 
plants, coconut, cashew, cocoa. The Scheme envisages support for creation of post-
harvest management (PHM) and marketing for better price realization of produce. The 
Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) scheme supports creation and upgradation of 
scientific storage capacity and other agricultural marketing infrastructure through loan cum 
back-ended capital subsidy. These interventions strengthen the post-harvest value chain 
and help reduce post-harvest losses including in horticulture-producing regions.  

 
 
(b) : Under AIF, since July 2020 till date, total 1,184 projects with a loan amount of Rs. 
598.90 crore have been sanctioned in Himachal Pradesh. The district-wise details of 
projects sanctioned, loan amount, loan disbursed is at Annexure-I.  
(c) : The State wise details of the infrastructure created under AIF including storage, cold 
chains, pack houses and grading units, is placed at Annexure-II. 
(d) & (e) : AIF is implemented uniformly across the country, including hilly and Himalayan 
States, to facilitate access to institutional credit for farmers, including small and marginal 
farmers, through eligible entities such as Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Primary 
Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), Self Help Groups (SHGs), Marketing Cooperatives 
Societies. An online single-window of AIF Portal has been developed for application 
submission, approval and monitoring of projects under AIF. 
 (f) : Under the AIF scheme, outreach activities are undertaken through State 
Governments, Central Programme Management Unit (CPMU), State Programme 
Management Units (SPMUs), Banks, NABARD, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), 
Cooperatives, Self Help Groups (SHGs) etc. to inform and educate farmers about the 
benefits and provisions of the scheme by way of workshops, webinars, Krishi Melas, 
exhibitions, FPO interactions etc. As part of the outreach, handholding support for project 
identification, preparation of Detailed Project Report, bank linkage and portal-based 
application is also provided to prospective beneficiaries.

NATIONAL ELECTRIC VEHICLES POLICY 
 
†1412. SHRI CHANDAN CHAUHAN:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that several States have implemented different policies and 
incentives to promote Electric Vehicles (EVs);  
 
(b) whether the Government is proposing to formulate a comprehensive National Electric 
Vehicle Policy or National Framework to ensure uniformity in standards, charging infrastructure, 
battery recycling, safety standards, and incentives across the country;  
 
(c) whether the Government has sought consultation with State Governments, industry, and 
research institutions in this regard;  
 
(d) whether there is a provision to promote indigenous manufacturing of EVs, batteries, and other 
key components, and private investment under the proposed policy/framework; and  
 
(e) the details of steps being taken by the Government for the deve lopment of a balanced and 
coordinated EV eco-system across the country? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a): Yes.  
 
(b): No National Electric Vehicle Policy or National Framework is under consideration in the 
Ministry of Heavy Industries. 
 
(c) & (d): Question does not arise in view of part (b). 
 
(e): The Schemes being implemented by the Government for the development of a  balanced and 
coordinated EV eco-system across the country are as under: 
 
(i) Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles in India 
(FAME India) Scheme Phase -II: The Government implemented this scheme for a period of 
five years from 01.04.2019 to 31.03.2024 with a total budgetary support of ₹11,500 crore. T he 
scheme provided demand incentive for e -2Ws, e-3Ws, e-4Ws and grant for e-buses and setting 
up of EV public charging stations (EV PCS). FAME-II has supported the sale of approximately 
16.72 lakh electric vehicles, including e -2Ws, e-3Ws, and e -4Ws. In ad dition, 5,197 electric 
buses (e-buses) have been deployed under the Scheme as on 30.06.2026. Further, an amount of 
₹912.50 crore was allocated under the Scheme for the establishment of EVPCS across the 
country. 
 
 
 
 
 

-2- 
 
(ii) Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component 
Industry in India (PLI-Auto): The Government notified this scheme for Automobile and Auto 
Component Industry in India, on 23.09.2021, for enhancing India's manufacturing capabilitie s 
for Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) products, including EVs, with a budgetary outlay 
of ₹25,938 crore.  
 
(iii) Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for National Programme on Advanced  
Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage :  The Government on 09.06.202 1 notified the PLI  
Scheme for manufacturing of ACC in the country with a budgetary outlay of ₹18,100 crore. The 
scheme aims to establish a competitive domestic manufacturing ecosystem for 50 GWh of ACC 
batteries. 
 
(iv) PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovativ e Vehicle Enhancement (PM EDRIVE) 
Scheme: This scheme with an outlay of ₹10,900 crore has been notified on 29.09.2024. This 
scheme supports incentivization of approximately 28.30 lakh electric vehicles (EVs) including 
e-2W, e -3W, e -Trucks, e -buses and e -Ambulances. Further, grant for EV public charging 
stations (EV PCS) and upgradation of testing agencies is also available under this scheme. An 
allocation of ₹4,391 crore has been made under the scheme for deployment of 14,028 e -buses 
out of which 13,800 e -buses have been allocated in seven cities having four million plus 
population viz. Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Pune and Surat. Further, 
200 e-buses have been approved for Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir. ₹2,000 crore has 
been allocated for deployment of EV Public Charging Station on pan India basis.   
 
(v) PM e-Bus Sewa-Payment Security Mechanism (PSM) Scheme: This Scheme notified 
on 28.10.2024, has an outlay of ₹3,435.33 crore and aims to support deployment of more than 
38,000 electric bu ses. The objective of this scheme is to provide payment security to e -bus 
operators in case of default by Public Transport Authorities (PTAs). 
 
(vi) Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electric Passenger Cars in India 
(SPMEPCI) was notified on 15th March, 2024 to promote the manufacturing of electric cars in

क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
  

(a):  Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, 
Ministry of Jal Shakti is implementing Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme 
(PMKSY-AIBP) and Har khet Ko Pani Components of PMKSY which focuses on major, 
medium and minor irrigation projects. Three major and medium irrigation projects are 
benefiting the Parbhani and Yavatmal Parliamentary Constituencies under the 
Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme and Central Assistance amounting to Rs. 
601.92 crore has been released for these projects with an irrigation potential of 37.62 
thousand hectares created, so far. Further, 14 minor irrigation projects in Yavatmal 
district and 18 minor irrigation projects in Washim district have been included under 
the Special Package for Maharashtra. Central Assistance of Rs. 22.52 crore and Rs. 
39.60 crore has been released with creation of an irrigation potential of 5,403 hectares 
and 4,192 hectares in Yavatmal and Washim districts respectively. 
 
(b):  The Government is implementing yield-based Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima 
Yojana (PMFBY) and weather index-based Restructured Weather Based Crop 
Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) to provide financial support to farmers against crop 
losses due to natural calamities and adverse weather events. PMFBY is voluntary for 
States/UTs and farmers. To make claim settlement simple, transparent and time-
bound, the Government has developed the National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP) for 
online enrolment, subsidy management and direct transfer of claims into farmers' bank 
accounts. The Digiclaim Module integrated with PFMS has been operationalised from 
Kharif 2022 for transparent claim processing. Further, from Kharif 2024, a penalty of 
12% is auto-calculated on delayed payment by Insurance Companies. From Kharif 
2025, a 12% penalty is also levied on delayed release of State share of subsidy in 
addition to opening of ESCROW account for advance deposit of premium share by 
States has been made mandatory. The Government has also leveraged technology 
through CCE-Agri App, YES-TECH, integration of land records with NCIP and 
mandatory use of Crop Loss Assessment App (CLAP) for faster and transparent claim 
settlement. 
  

(c):  Government is promoting organic farming in all States/UTs including 
Maharashtra through Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Paramparagat Krishi Vikas 
Yojana (PKVY) since 2015-16. The scheme provides end-to-end support covering 
production, processing, certification and marketing, with preference to small and 
marginal farmers through formation of organic clusters including training on all aspects 
of organic farming. Under PKVY, financial assistance of Rs.31,500 per hectare for 
three years, including Direct Benefit Transfer of Rs.15,000 per hectare for on-farm/off-
farm organic inputs are provided to beneficiary farmers. In Maharashtra, since 
inception of the scheme, Central assistance of Rs.165.56 crore has been released 
and 69,852 hectare has been covered benefitting 91,259 farmers. District wise details 
are not maintained centrally.   
 
(d) & (e): The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India 
is implementing Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) scheme 
in the Country including Maharashtra. The scheme is implemented by the States/UTs 
as per their Annual Acton Plan (AAP). Under PDMC Scheme, financial assistance is 
provided to farmers for installation of micro irrigation systems @ 55% and 45% of the 
unit cost to small & marginal farmers

Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:

(b)  whether it is true that  maintenance data is updated on the e-

(c)  whether the Government will revise the standards to increase
