MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1699    
(TO BE ANSWERED ON 29.07.2026) 
 
LIVE EVENTS DEVELOPMENT CELL 
1699. SMT. D K ARUNA: 
SHRI KRIPANATH MALLAH: 
SHRI DILESHWAR KAMAIT: 
SHRI ASHOK KUMAR RAWAT: 
Will the Minister of INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING be pleased 
to state: 
(a) the progress made by the Live Events Development Cell (LEDC) 
since its constitution including the key outcomes of its four meetings 
held so far; 
(b) the number of States/Union Territories that have adopted the 
Model Executive Order, 2026; 
(c) the number of event -related permissions processed through the 
Single-Window Clearance System on the India Cine Hub (ICH) portal; 
and 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to position India as a global 
hub for live events by 2030 including infrastructure and ease-of-doing-
business measures for event organisers? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING  
AND PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
(DR. L. MURUGAN) 
(a) to (d): The Government has identified the live events sector as 
an important driver of economic growth, employment generation, 
tourism and cultural promotion.  

To facilitate the sustainable growth of the sector and position India 
as a global hub for live events by 2030, the Live Events Development 
Cell (LEDC) was constituted in July 2025. It is chaired by the 
Secretary (Ministry of Information and Broadcasting), with 
representatives of Central Ministries and Departments, State 
Governments, industry associations and other stakeholders. 
Four meetings of the LEDC have been held,  on 26.08.2025, 
16.10.2025, 04.02.2026 and 30.04.2026, and has initiated several 
measures to strengthen infrastructure, simplify regulatory 
processes, promote ease of doing business and develop a robust 
ecosystem for the live events sector.  
The major outcomes are as under: 
• An Execution Framework setting out a comprehensive strategy 
for the growth of the sector has been prepared and circulated to 
all stakeholders. 
• An online system for live event permissions has been developed 
and made operational on the India Cine Hub (ICH) portal. It 
provides a single digital workflow covering application, 
coordination, approvals, payments and inspections, with time -
bound processin g, real -time tracking, escalation of delays, 
integrated digital payments and digital audit trails.  
• 29 States/UTs have designated their Nodal Officers for Live Event 
permissions on the ICH portal.  
• The "Model Executive Order for Streamlining Licensing and 
Permissions for Live Events in India, 2026" has been prepared by 
LEDC and circulated to all States and Union Territories on 
13.03.2026. At present, 3 States/Union Territory have 
implemented it in their State.  
• The Archaeological Survey of India has framed a Standard 
Operating Procedure for organising live events at protected 
monuments and has shared a list of 224 heritage sites for the 
purpose.  

• A concept note on a Greenfield Venue Development Policy has 
been prepared and circulated to State Governments, sports 
authorities and industry stakeholders. 
• A Skilling Committee has been constituted. The Indian Institute 
of Mass Communication, in collaboration with the Media and 
Entertainment Skills Council and the Event and Entertainment 
Management Association, has undertaken preparatory work 
relating to certificate and short-term courses in live events and 
elective modules in its existing programmes. 
• The LEDC has identified issues relating to visa and FRRO 
facilitation for visiting artists and crews, use of sports and 
heritage venues, streamlining of music licensing, permissions for 
events beyond 10 p.m., taxation and access to finance, and has 
shared these with the concerned Ministries and Departments for 
their consideration. 
• Upon recommendation of LEDC, Reserve Bank of India has 
dispensed with the requirement of furnishing a Bank Guarantee 
for advance remittances of USD 500,000 and above for the import 
of services under the Foreign Exchange Management 
Regulations, 2026, notified on 15th January 2026. The regulations 
shall come into force from 01.10.2026.

Will the Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:

implementation under PM -VIKAS Scheme and the erstwhile Seekho aur Kamao scheme in 
Maharashtra have been received by the Government and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the funds released, project implementing agencies empanelled, beneficiaries trained in

(c)  Yes, The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy has integrated principles of sustainable and 
social equitable energy transition into its policy guidelines and scheme frameworks.  
 
Renewable energy projects are implemented in compliance with applicable environmental regulations 
and sustainability considerations. These measures aim to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, enhance 
energy security, diversify the energy mix, and support India's commitments towards achieving net-zero 
emissions by 2070 and its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) target of achieving 500 GW 
electricity capacity from non-fossil fuel based sources.  
 
PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana is democratizing solar energy access by providing Central Financial 
Assistance (CFA) to residential households for installation of rooftop solar (RTS) systems to empower 
them to generate their own electricity. Under this Sc heme, all residential households in the country, 
having a grid -connected electricity connection with the local DISCOM, can avail the benefits for 
installation of RTS systems by applying on the National Portal of the scheme.  To facilitate adoption 
of RTS system for economically weaker sections under the Scheme, facility of collateral-free loan from 
nationalized banks at a concessional interest rate of repo -rate plus 50 bps, i.e., 5.75% per annum for 
the present, with a tenure of 10 years, has also been prov ided.  Further, the Ministry has included 
RESCO/Utility-Led Aggregation (ULA) Models under the Scheme to enable DISCOMs/State 

Governments/State Designated entities to support RTS development, primarily for low -income 
households/ families.   
 
PM-Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM -KUSUM) is empowering farmers through 
installing standalone solar pumps, solarization of existing grid connected agricultural pumps including 
feeder level solarization and setting up of solar power plants u pto 2 MW on their barren/uncultivable 
land.   
 
The Ministry has also been implementing New Solar Power Scheme (for Tribal and Particularly 
Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTG) Habitations/Villages) under PM Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha 
Abhiyan (PM JANMAN) and Dharti Aabha Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA JG UA), for the 
electrification of un -electrified households in PVTG and tribal habitations/villages, solarization of 
Multi-Purpose Centres (MPCs) in PVTG areas, and solarization of public institutions in identified tribal 
habitations/villages, through off -grid solar systems; where grid connectivity is not techno -
economically feasible.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF MINES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1704 
ANSWERED ON 29.07.2026 
  
INCENTIVE SCHEME FOR QUICKER OPERATIONALISATION OF MINES 
  
1704. SHRI V K SREEKANDAN: 
  
Will the Minister of MINES be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether it is a fact that the Government has instituted an incentive scheme with an 
outlay of Rs.5,000 crore for financial year 2026-27 and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether it is also true that the aim of the scheme is for quicker operationalisation 
of mines, readiness in placing mines for auction, governance and integration with the 
government's central monitoring portal and if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) whether the scheme also aims to incentivise States towards ensuring that mines 
are placed faster for auctions and if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR COAL AND MINES 
(SHRI SATISH CHANDRA DUBEY) 
  
(a) to (c): Yes, an incentive scheme with an outlay of ₹5,000 crore has been 
incorporated under Part -V (Mining Sector Reforms) of the Scheme for Special 
Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) for financial year 2026 –27. The 
Scheme comprises of three components viz. Component-I (Implementation of Mining 
Reforms), Component-II (Mine Operationalization) and Component -III (State Mining 
Readiness Index-based Reforms).  
The incentive scheme aims to facilitate and expedite faster mine operationalizati on 
and improve overall governance of the mining sector by incentivizing States/ UTs (with 
legislature) to undertake reform measures including, inter-alia, State’s integration with 
Unified Mining Portal of Ministry of Mines for mine operationalization; cons titution of 
pre-auction committee to resolve land scheduling issues for faster identification and 
preparation of mineral blocks for auction; publication of annual auction calendar for 
major minerals to facilitate more active & transparent auction by the States; successful 
auctioning of major mineral blocks with pre-embedded clearances; operationalization 
of auctioned major mineral blocks as per prescribed target; and adoption of 
technology-based measures to prevent/ 
 detect grade misclassification of mineral ore.

 Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:- 
 
(a) the present installed nuclear power generation capacity in the country, plant-wise along    
with its percentage contribution to the total electricity generation;  
(b) the details of nuclear power projects under construction and those approved during the  
last five years indicating their present status and expected dates of commissioning;  
(c) whether the Government has fixed any target for expanding nuclear power capacity by   
      2030 and 2047 and if so, the details thereof;  
(d) the measures taken to promote indigenous nuclear technology, ensure fuel security and  
enhance public safety at nuclear power plants; and  
(e) the steps taken to encourage private sector participation in the nuclear power sector in  
accordance with the existing legal framework?

AND PRIME MINISTER’S OFFICE (DR. JITENDRA SINGH)

under NPCIL beyond 2032 which will comprise of indigenous Pressurised Heavy Water 
Reactors (PHWRs) and Light Water Reactors (LWRs ). Additionally, the Government has 
approved the pre -project activities of 2 x 500 MW FBR 1 & 2, to be built  with the same

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS  
DEPARTMENT OF TELECOMMUNICATIONS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1708 
 ANSWERED ON 29TH JULY, 2026 
 
SANCHAR SAATHI INITIATIVE FOR TELECOM SECURITY AND CONSUMER 
PROTECTION 
 
1708.  SHRI PRADEEP KUMAR SINGH: 
SHRI BALABHADRA MAJHI: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the progress made under the Sanchar Saathi initiative during the last one year including the 
number of lost or stolen mobile devices traced, blocked, recovered and the action taken against 
fraudulent mobile connections including details for the Nabarangpur Lok Sabha Constituency of 
Odisha; 
 
(b)  the measures taken to protect telecom consumers from cyber frauds, spoofed calls, spam 
communications and misuse of mobile connections through technology enabled solutions including 
their implementation in the Nabarangpur Lok Sabha Constituency; 
 
(c)  the major digital services made available through the Sanchar Saathi portal and mobile 
application for the convenience of citizens along with their utilisation in the Nabarangpur Lok Sabha 
Constituency; and 
 
(d) the steps taken to further strengthen telecom security, consumer awareness and digital trust 
through this initiative, including the special measures taken for the Nabarangpur Lok Sabha 
Constituency? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS AND RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. PEMMASANI CHANDRA SEKHAR) 
 
(a) The progress made under the Sanchar Saathi initiative of Department of Telecommunications 
(DoT) during July 2025 to June 2026 is as under:  
 
i. Number of lost or stolen mobile devices blocked, traced & recovered are 20.59 lakhs, 
11.11 lakhs & 6.99 lakhs respectively.   
ii. Based on 6.4 lakh reports of suspected fraud communication shared by citizens on 
Sanchar Saathi, 35.48 lakh mobile connections have been disconnected.  
   Lok Sabha constituency wise data is not maintained.  
 
(b) DoT has taken measures to protect telecom consumers from cyber frauds, spoofed calls and 
misuse of mobile connections through technology enabled solutions which have been implemented 
throughout the country including Nabarangpur Lok Sabha Constituency. These measures, inter-alia, 
include :  

2 
 
i. Sanchar Saathi initiative of DoT enables citizens to report the suspected fraud 
communications. DoT uses this crowd-sourced data to carry out analysis and to zero 
down on misuse of telecom resources.  
ii. DoT has developed Financial Fraud Risk Indicator. This is a risk-based metric that 
categorises a suspicious mobile number according to its probability of being associated 
with medium, high or very high risk of financial fraud.  
iii. DoT has developed international incoming spoofed calls prevention system which is a 
system to identify and block incoming international spoofed calls displaying Indian 
mobile numbers. 
 
 In addition, Telecom Regulatory Authority of India has implemented Distributed Ledger 
Technology based system under the Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference 
Regulations for curbing spam. 
 
(c) Sanchar Saathi web portal and mobile App of DoT are available to citizens across India 
including Nabarangpur Lok Sabha Constituency. Key digital services of Sanchar Saathi include 
facilitating citizens to: 
 
i. report suspected fraud communications, 
ii. know mobile connections in their name & report connections which are not required or 
not taken by them, 
iii. report lost/ stolen mobile handsets, and  
iv. check genuineness of mobile handset. 
  
(d) DoT is actively promoting telecom safety, consumer awareness and digital trust through 
widespread multilingual awareness campaigns including explainer videos & infographics on social 
media platforms, SMS campaigns, student volunteers through Sanchar Mitra scheme. These 
initiatives are being taken on pan-India basis.

Will the Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:

(d) the measures taken by the Government to enhance  market access and business 
opportunities for artisans belonging to minority communities through such initiatives 
particularly in Tamil Nadu; and 
(e) whether the Government propose to organise such outreach programmes in other States 
and Union Territories as well and if so, the details thereof?

THE MINISTER OF MINORITY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU) 
 
(a)  Under the PM VIKAS scheme, Ministry has been organising 'Lok Samvardhan Parv', 
bringing together minority artisans from across India and assist them to scale up their 
operations and businesses. The platform offers artisans a unique opportunity to showcase 
their indigenous arts, crafts, and rich cultural heritage. The event has been designed not only 
to promote the traditions of minority communities but also to foster an innovative and 
entrepreneurial environment for artisans.  
(b)  So far, the Ministry has organised 06 Lok Samvardhan Parvs, as under: 
i. July, 2024 at Dilli Haat, INA, New Delhi 
ii. January, 2025 at Baba Kharak Singh Marg, New Delhi 
iii. April, 2025 at Convocation Ground, Kashmir University, Srinagar, Jammu & Kashmir 
iv. June, 2025 at Gandhi Darshan, Raj Ghat, New Delhi 
v. August-September 2025, Marine Drive Exhibition Area, Kochi, Kerala

across the country to exhibit and market their products. To enhance their skills in areas like 
marketing, export & online business, design, taxation and sales etc., workshops we re 
conducted by the Ministry, with support from the Export Promotion Council for Handicrafts 
(EPCH), ensuring a holistic approach to empowering their talent and augmentation in their 
incomes.  
The benefits of Lok Samvardhan Parv are available to eligible participants from all 
States and Union Territories, including Tamil Nadu, thereby facilitating market access and 
business opportunities for artisans and traditional craftsmen. 
(e) The Ministry has issued a framework for organising Lok Samvardhan Parv in States and 
Union Territories under the PM VIKAS Scheme. Organisation of such events at other 
locations is considered from time to time, subject to receipt of proposals from eligible 
implementing agencies, availability of funds and fulfilment of the prescribed guidelines.

entries.t: Low-interest, long-term Loans/Financial Grants under RDI Scheme
entries.head:
Page 1 of 2 
 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY 
DEPARTMENT OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1712 
ANSWERED ON 29/07/2026 
  
LOW-INTEREST, LONG-TERM LOANS/FINANCIAL GRANTS UNDER 
RDI SCHEME 
  
1712. SHRI YADUVEER WADIYAR: 
 Will the Minister of SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state:  
(a) the details of total quantum of capital actually disbursed in the 
form of low -interest long -term loans or financia l grants under the 
newly implemented Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) 
Scheme since its launch; 
(b) the details of distinct vetting mechanisms and risk-assessment 
frameworks utilized by the Government to evaluate deep -tech and 
biotechnology startup proposals and to ensure  that high-risk, high-
reward innovations are not filtered out by traditional risk -averse 
commercial lending criteria; and 
(c)  the details of specific execution roadmap established to 
distribute these commercial innovation fu nds equitably to tier-2 and 
tier-3 regional entrepreneurship hubs  instead of allowing capital 
consolidation in mature metropolitan startup corridors? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE 
MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY AND EARTH SCIENCES 
(DR. JITENDRA SINGH) 
 
(a) The Union Cabinet approved the ₹1 lakh crore Research, 
Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme on 1 July 2025 with a total 
outlay of ₹1 lakh crore over six years to incentivise private sector 
participation in research and development. The Scheme was formally 
launched by the Hon'ble Prime Minister on 3 November 2025. 
Since the launch of the Scheme, financial assistance of ₹1,000 crore 
each has been sanctioned to two Focused Research Organisations 
(FROs), namely the Technology Devel opment Board (TDB) and the 
Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), 
aggregating to ₹2,000 crore. Of this, ₹500 crore has been disbursed 
to TDB in March 2026 for onward financing of eligible technology 
entities.  

Page 2 of 2 
 
TDB has, so far, approved  22 projects with a total project cost of 
₹4,744 crore, involving RDI Fund support of ₹2,192 crore. BIRAC has 
shortlisted 8 projects involving ₹390.35 crore for support under the 
RDI Scheme.  
The RDI Scheme does not provide financial grants. Financial 
assistance under the Scheme is extended primarily through long -
term, low -interest loans, equity and equity -linked instruments, in 
accordance with the approved Scheme framework. 
  
(b) The Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme has 
adopted a specialized evaluation and risk -assessment framework 
that is distinct from conventional commercial lending practices. 
Applications are evaluated by an empowered Investment Committee 
comprising senior domain experts, technologists and investment 
professionals, in accordance with the criteria prescribed in the 
Scheme's Implementation Guidelines.  
The assessment considers factors such as the degree of 
technological innovation, Technology Readi ness Level (TRL), 
commercialisation potential, market opportunity, capability of the 
management team, project implementation plan and expected 
strategic impact, rather than relying solely on conventional lending 
parameters such as collateral or risk -averse commercial lending 
criteria. The Scheme is specifically designed to support high -risk, 
high-impact and transformative innovations. Accordingly, it focuses 
on technologies with the potential for significant technological 
advancement and commercialisation, rather than routine research 
and development or incremental improvements. 
 
(c) The Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme does 
not earmark funds for specific States, cities or regions. It is a pan -
India initiative designed to provide equitable a ccess to financing for 
eligible technology entities across the country, including those 
located in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, through a transparent, merit-based 
evaluation process. 
Participation under the Scheme has been invited from all regions of 
the country and is not restricted to established metropolitan startup 
hubs. The Scheme is implemented through multiple Second -Level 
Fund Managers (SLFMs), with eligible proposals being evaluated on 
the basis of the criteria prescribed in the Implementation Guidelines, 
without any regional preference. This approach is intended to ensure 
broad-based access to financing for meritorious technology -driven 
innovations across the country.  
*****

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

ROLE OF STATES IN IMPLEMENTATION OF DIGITAL INDIA PROGRAMME 
 
1713. SHRI MALAIYARASAN D: 
 
Will the Minister of ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased 
to state: 
 
(a) the status of implementation of Digital India Programme across States including 
Kallakurichi Lok Sabha Constituency of Tamil Nadu; 
(b) the details of funds allocated, released and utilised under the Programme during the last 
five years; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to expand broadband connectivity, Common Service 
Centres and digital literacy initiatives in rural and remote areas; 
(d) the details of steps taken by the Government to ensure data privacy, cybersecurity and 
protection of citizens' digital rights under the Programme; 
(e) whether independent evaluation of impact on employment generation, governance 
efficiency and digital inclusion has been conducted; 
(f) the role of States in monitoring and implementation at ground level including Tamil Nadu; 
and 
(g) whether any timelines have been fixed for next phase of Digital India expansion and if so, 
its key measurable outcomes thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (g):   In line with Hon’ble Prime Minister's vision to democratise technology and 
empower citizens, the Government of India had launched the Digital India programme in July, 
2015. At its core, the programme promotes three interconnected goals: strengthening digit al 
infrastructure, delivering government services digitally, and empowering citizens through 
digital literacy and employment. 
 
The Government has implemented several initiatives and policy measures to improve digital 
access and e-governance across the country including rural areas of Tamil Nadu.  Details of 
some of the key initiatives are as follows: 
 
Digital Connectivity and Digital Infrastructure: Digital India has contributed to the rapid 
expansion of internet access, through initiatives such as BharatNet, which aims to provide 
high-speed internet to rural and remote areas. As a result, there has been a substantial increase 
in internet accessibility and usage across the country, and internet penetration in India has 
grown in the last decade. 
 
● Telecom, Internet & Broadband Penetration: Total telephone connections in India 
grew from 93.3 crores in March 2014 to 116.69+ cr in March 2022 to 133+ crores in 

March, 2026. In Tamil Nadu, the total number of telephone subscribers has crossed 
8.41 crore. 
● Internet subscribers jumped from 25.15 crore in March 2014 to 82.48 cr in March 
2022 to 109.27 crore in March, 2026. In Tamil Nadu, the total number of internet 
subscribers has crossed 6.90 crore. 
● BharatNet - Linking Villages to the Internet: As of June 2026, about 2.21 lakh Gram 
Panchayats (GPs) have been made service ready under BharatNet project in the 
country including 1,1118 GPs in Tamil Nadu. 
● Under the Government-funded 4G Saturation Project and other mobile connectivity 
projects, till June 2026, 257 mobile towers have been commissioned in Tamil Nadu. 
● As on 30.06.2026, total of Rs. 1886 crores have been disbursed under various ongoing 
projects of Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN) in Tamil Nadu. 
● Aadhaar: Aadhaar created a trusted biometric identity platform for secure and instant 
digital authentication. Aadhaar enrolments increased from 0.42 crore in 2010 -11 to 
over 144+ crore by June 2026. In Tamil Nadu, over 8.18 crore Aadhaar have been 
generated. 
● Unified Payments Interface (UPI): UPI has empowered millions of individuals and 
small businesses in rural and remote areas to make fast, secure and low -cost digital 
payments, significantly advancing financial inclusion. 
o  UPI serves more than 55.49 crore individuals, 6.5 crore merchants, and connects 
731 banks on one platform, making it the world’s largest digital payment system. 
o  UPI powers 85% of India’s digital payments and nearly 50% of global real -time 
digital payments. 
● DigiLocker provides citizens with anytime access to authentic digital documents 
issued by original issuers. The platform has over 71.66 crore registered users, with 
more than 936.03 crore documents issued by 2,822 onboarded issuers. More than 2.18 
cr Aadhaar enabled registrations have taken place in the state of Tamil Nadu to avail 
DigiLocker services. 
● Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance (UMANG) provides citizens 
with a single mobile platform to access government services. The platform offers 
2,575 services for individuals, including 17 services integrated by the Government of 
Tamil Nadu. 
● eSign (e-Hastakshar): e-Sign is an online electronic signature service, which can be 
integrated with service delivery applications via an Application Programming 
Interface (API) to facilitate an e-Sign user to digitally sign a document. e-Sig

entries.t: Monitoring Illegal Sand Mining in Uttar Pradesh
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF MINES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1718 
ANSWERED ON 29.07.2026 
 
MONITORING ILLEGAL SAND MINING IN UTTAR PRADESH 
  
1718. SHRI PUSHPENDRA SAROJ:  
          SHRI ANAND BHADAURIA:  
 
Will the Minister of MINES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of the action taken by the Union Government pursuant to the directions 
of the National Green Tribunal to strengthen monitoring of illegal sand mining in the 
State of Uttar Pradesh;  
(b) the number of districts in Uttar Pradesh whose District Survey Reports have been 
reviewed by the Government for compliance with the Sustainable Sand Mining 
Management Guidelines and Enforcement & Monitoring Guidelines for Sand Mining 
along with the deficiencies identified;  
(c) the status of implementation of the Mining Surveillance System, satellite -based 
monitoring and other digital tools for detection of illegal mining in the said State along 
with the assistance provided by the Government therefor; and  
(d) the advisories, guidelines or directions issued by the Union Government to the 
State Government of Uttar Pradesh during the last two years to improve monitoring, 
transparency and enforcement against illegal sand mining? 
   
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR COAL AND MINES 
(SHRI SATISH CHANDRA DUBEY) 
  
(a) & (d) : Ordinary sand is a minor mineral, and under Section 15 of the Mines & 
Minerals (Development & Regulation) (MMDR) Act, 1957, State Governments have 
the power to make rules for regulating the grant of minor mineral concessions. 
Furthermore, under Section 23 C of the MMDR Act, 1957, State Governments have 
the power to frame rules to prevent illegal mining, transportation, and storage of 
minerals. Hence, these matters fall under the purview of State Governments. The 
Ministry of Mines has not issued any advisori es, guidelines, or directions to the 
Government of Uttar Pradesh in the last two years to improve monitoring, 
transparency, and enforcement against illegal sand mining. 
  

(b): Preparation, updating, and approval of District Survey Reports (DSRs) are the 
responsibilities of the respective State and district authorities. As per the State 
Government of Uttar Pradesh (UP), a District Survey Report has been prepared for all 
areas, assessing the amount of available minerals in the district, and this report has 
been uploaded to the district's NIC website for public convenience. 
  
(c): The Mining Surveillance System (MSS) is a satellite -based platform designed to 
facilitate State Governments in identifying possible illegal mining of major minerals. It 
analyzes satellite imagery within 500 meters of lease boundaries to identify anomalies, 
which are flagged as "triggers" and are forwarded to the State Governments for field 
verification. A total of 10 triggers have been generated through MSS in Uttar Pradesh.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

TO BE ANSWERED ON 29.07.2026 
 
OPTIMISATION OF TTES MANNING IN RAILWAY 
 
1721. SHRI CHAVAN RAVINDRA VASANTRAO: 
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government is considering to conduct a study to review 
manning of TTEs on trains and stationary duties at all commercial 
offices at station to eliminate overstaffing/understaffing and if so, the 
details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;  
(b) whether TTEs travel as spares as per existing arrangement in some of 
the trains of Northern Railway particularly 22401/22402 running 
between DEE (Delhi Sarai Rohilla) and MCTM (Martyr Captain Tushar 
Mahajan/Udhampur) stations and if so, the details along with the actual 
position in this regard;  
(c) whether the current practice results in an avoidable loss of man power 
and additional expenses incurred in the form of Travelling Allowance 
(TA) for the TTEs and if so, the details thereof; and  
(d) whether the Government has recently proposed an effective solution to 
optimise manpower and reducing unnecessary expenditure incurring 
due to the train manning duty assigned to the TTEs and if so, the details 
thereof along with the steps taken in this regard?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RAILWAYS, INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND 
ELECTRONICS & INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI ASHWINI VAISHNAW) 
 
(a) to (d): Indian Railways assign Travelling Ticket Examiners (TTEs) to 
train and station duties with the objective of making the best possible use 
of the available manpower.  According to the latest guidelines: 
i. One TTE is deployed for maximum of 5 AC coaches. 
ii. One TTE is deployed for maximum of 3 Chair Car or Sleeper coaches. 

Page 2 of 2 
In simple terms, the number of TTEs assigned to a train depends on its 
coach composition, ensuring efficient use of existing manpower while 
maintaining adequate ticket-checking and passenger assistance. 
Train No. 22401/22402 DEE (Delhi Sarai Rohilla) - MCTM (Martyr Captain 
Tushar Mahajan/Udhampur) Express is being manned on an end-to-end 
basis by the staff of Jammu Head Quarters being the nearest headquarter 
in the direction of the train movement. The Jammu HQ TTEs who go in 
22401 ex DEE upto MCTM come back doing checking in 12472 group upto 
Jammu and fresh batch moves in 12471 group doing checking upto MCTM 
and takes 22402 ex MCTM to DEE. Thus, to avoid idle spare movement of 
the staff, ticket checking duties have been assigned to the staff between 
Jammu and Udhampur. 
Administrative guidelines have been issued from time to time to zonal 
Railways to adopt measures to optimize manpower utilization, inter-alia 
asking the Railways to: 
i. Review the TTE links in coordination with adjacent Railways, if 
necessary. 
ii. Extend the run of TTEs beyond Divisional/Zonal jurisdiction subject to 
Hours of Employment Regulation (HOER) norms, wherever feasible, so 
as to maximise manning of coaches.  
iii. Rationalising the strength of ticket checking staff posted in the ticket 
checking squads so as to ensure increased availability of manpower 
to be deployed in the trains and at stations. 
Taking such actions is a continuous and ongoing process.

MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1722 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 29.07.2026 
 
HYDROGEN TRAIN JIND-SONIPAT CORRIDOR 
 
1722. SHRI P C MOHAN: 
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the current status of India's first indigenous hydrogen fuel 
cell train on the Jind-Sonipat corridor, the trial speed achieved the 
status of the hydrogen storage and refueling infrastructure at Jind 
including the timeline for its commercial passenger operations;  
(b) the extent to which hydrogen trains are expected to reduce carbon and 
particulate emissions as compared to diesel locomotives and the 
estimated fuel-cost savings;  
(c) the details of the other advantages of hydrogen trains over conventional 
diesel traction including noise reduction and reduced dependence on 
imported fuel; and  
(d) whether the Government proposes to extend this technology to other 
non-electrified routes as part of Indian Railways' net-zero carbon goals 
particularly in Karnataka?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RAILWAYS, INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND 
ELECTRONICS & INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI ASHWINI VAISHNAW) 
 
(a) to (d) The Hydrogen powered train was inaugurated on 17.07.2026. Till 
25.07.2026, this train has covered 1256 km of commercial run in 89 km long 
Jind-Sonipat section. The hydrogen train has been developed by Indian 
Railways on pilot basis to demonstrate the use of hydrogen powered train 
technology in Railways.  
A dedicated Hydrogen Plant has been setup at Jind for providing hydrogen 
in this Trainset. The hydrogen storage facility has been set up in 
accordance with the guidelines of the Petroleum and Explosives Safety 

Page 2 of 2 
Organization (PESO), ensuring adherence to prescribed safety standards 
and protocols. 
The Hydrogen Trainset operation ensures zero CO2 emissions with water 
vapour being the only emission. The Trainset works on fuel cell technology 
that does not have any moving part and conventional engine for traction 
power generation therefore the operation is much quieter thereby reducing 
noise pollution. This project establishes Indian Railways in hydrogen 
technology. 
As the Hydrogen Trainset and its infrastructure have been developed on a 
pilot basis, direct comparison of the cost of hydrogen-fuelled trains with 
established traction systems at this stage would not present a fair cost 
comparison. 
Prominent features and advantages of this technology include: 
 Indigenously designed and developed in India demonstrating IR’s 
commitment to Atmanirbhar Bharat. 
 Presently, it is the world’s longest (10 coaches) and most powerful 
(2400 kW) Hydrogen Trainset on Broad Gauge platform. 
 The Trainset comprises of two Driving Power Cars (DPCs) of 1200 kW 
each, totalling 2400 kW along with eight passenger cars. 
 It represents a major step in development of next generation fuel 
technology in Railways, inherently optimizing noise reduction and 
curtailing reliance on imported fossil fuels. 
At present, IR has taken up the running of hydrogen-powered train 
technology on a pilot basis on the Jind-Sonipat circuit. Decision to run 
hydrogen trains on other routes depends on availability of resources, 
operational and other requirements.

entries.t: Semiconductor Fabrication and OSAT Potential in Andhra Pradesh
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1723 
TO BE ANSWERED ON: 29.07.2026 
 
SEMICONDUCTOR FABRICATION AND OSAT POTENTIAL IN ANDHRA 
PRADESH 
 
1723. SHRI P V MIDHUN REDDY: 
 
Will the Minister of ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether the Government have assessed the potential for semiconductor fabrication, 
packaging and Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) facilities in Andhra 
Pradesh; 
(b) if so, the details thereof particularly with regard to Visakhapatnam and existing 
Electronics System Design and Manufacturing clusters in the State; and 
(c) the details of steps taken by the Government to attract semiconductor investments to 
Andhra Pradesh? 
  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (c): Inspired by the Hon’ble Prime Minister’s vision of AtmaNirbhar Bharat and making 
India a global electronics manufacturing hub, Government adopted structured and targeted 
policy initiatives for the development of electronics manufacturing across  the entire value 
chain including semiconductors. 
 
The semiconductor industry is a foundational industry. All sectors of the economy such as 
industrial, consumer, defence, telecommunication and automotive etc depend on 
semiconductors. This sector offers transformative advantages by driving technological 
innovation, economic growth, and strategic self-reliance. 
 
Semicon India Programme: 
Recognising the importance of Semiconductors, the Government launched Semicon India 
Programme in January 2022 for setting up of semiconductor fabs, display fabs semiconductor 
packaging and also for promotion of Indian designed chips.  
 
Under Semicon India Programme, Government has approved 12 manufacturing projects with 
total investment commitments of about Rs. 1.64 lakh crore. This includes the proposal of 
Advanced System in Package (ASIP) Technologies Private Limited for setting up Ass embly 
Testing Marking and Packaging (ATMP) facility in district Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, 
with an investment of ₹468 crores. The facility will be set up in technology partnership with 
APACT Co. Ltd, South Korea. The production capacity of the facility  would be around 96 
million units/annum and the unit is expected to generate more than 500 employment 
opportunities, depending on the factory automation. 
 

Further, under Semicon India Programme, Twenty -four (24) semiconductor design projects 
have also been approved for financial support. Additionally, 105 start-ups/MSMEs have been 
granted access to industry -standard Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools. So far, the 
usage of these chip design tools has exceeded 87 lakh hours. 
 
Chip to Start-up Programme: 
Additionally, Government launched Chips to Startup (C2S) programme to provide industry 
ready manpower in chip design. Under this programme, access to cutting -edge chip design 
tools has been provided at no cost. The access to these tools is provided to 320 organizations. 
So far, the usage of these chip design tools has exceeded 240 lakh hours. The list of 
organizations supported under C2S programme in the State of Andhra Pradesh is at Annex-
I. 
Semicon 2.0: 
To address the Semiconductor needs of the country and the world, the Union Cabinet has 
approved Semicon2.0 on 15.07.2026 with an outlay of ₹1.275 lakh crore, providing ample 
opportunity for the States to attract semiconductor investment. 
 
Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMC): 
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji has encouraged setting up manufacturing clusters in 
various sectors like electronics, textiles, defence, chemicals, etc.  His vision was translated 
through the Electronics Manufacturing Cluster (EMC) scheme in electronics sector. 
 
Government has supported the following EMCs in the state of Andhra Pradesh: 
    i.    EMC at Cherivi, Chittoor District – Spread over an area of 94 acres, with a 
project cost of ₹ 56.75 crore. 
     ii.  EMC at Vikruthamala, Chittoor District – Spread over an area of 501.4 acres, 
with     a project cost of ₹ 248.9 crore. 
iii.  EMC at Renigunta and Yerpadu, Chittoor District - Spread over an area of 
113.27 acres, with a project cost of ₹ 74.27 crore. 
    iv.   EMC at Kopparthy, YSR District -Spread over an area of 540 acres, with a 
project cost of ₹ 748.76 crore.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF MINES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No.1724 
ANSWERED ON 29.07.2026 
  
MINERAL EXPLORATION BY GEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA 
  
1724. SHRI ROBERT BRUCE C: 
  
Will the Minister of MINES be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Geological Survey of India has conducted mineral exploration in 
Tirunelveli district and if so, the details thereof along with the findings including the 
funds sanctioned or released and the physical progress achieved during each of the 
last three years and if not, the reasons therefor; and  
(b) the details of the steps proposed to be taken by the Union Government in this 
regard for Tirunelveli district and the time-frame fixed therefor? 
  
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR COAL AND MINES 
(SHRI SATISH CHANDRA DUBEY) 
  
(a) and (b): The Geological Survey of India (GSI) has not conducted mineral 
exploration in Tirunelveli district during the last three years.  
  
GSI had carried out mineral exploration programmes for various commodities 
such as Mica, Graphite, Limestone, etc. in Tirunelveli district till field season 2005 -
2006. These exploration projects did not yield significant outcome for any mineral 
commodity and hence, mineral exploration was not taken up further in this district by 
GSI.

entries.t: Age Based Restrictions for Access to Social Media Platforms
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1725 
TO BE ANSWERED ON: 29.07.2026 
 
AGE BASED RESTRICTIONS FOR ACCESS TO SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORMS 
 
1725. SHRI BASTIPATI NAGARAJU: 
 
Will the Minister of ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased 
to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of concerns relating to social media addiction, 
cyberbullying, exposure to harmful content, online grooming, privacy violations and mental 
health risks among children and adolescents and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government is considering prescribing a minimum age or introducing age 
based restrictions for access to social media platforms and if so, the details and timeline 
thereof; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to mandate age -verification mechanisms, parental 
consent, child safety settings and enhanced safeguards for the protection of children's personal 
data on social media platforms and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether the Government has constituted or proposes to constitute an expert committee or 
undertake stakeholder consultations for framing a regulatory framework for the protection of 
minors on social media platforms and if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (d): The policies of the Government are aimed at ensuring an Open, Safe and Trusted 
and Accountable Internet for its users, including children. With the expansion of the Internet 
and more and more citizens including children, accessing the internet services, the risk of 
exposure to inappropriate content and the harmful effects of these activities have also 
increased. The Government is cognizant of the immense opportunities offered by these 
technologies and the harms they may cause. In order to protec t the children and adolescents 
from exposure to inappropriate content and the harmful effects of social media, Government 
has adopted a series of measures for preventing the flow of such information. 
 
Legal structure 
The Information Technology Act, 2000 (“IT Act”) and the Information Technology 
(Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 (“IT Rules”), together, 
have established a framework to promote digital well-being, user safeguards and responsible 
digital participation. 
 
Information Technology Act , 2000 (“IT Act”) 
The IT Act provides punishment for various cyber offences such as identity theft (section 
66C), impersonation (section 66D), privacy violations (section 66E), publishing or 
transmitting obscene or sexually explicit content (sections 67, 67A, 67B). It also empowers 
Police to investigate offences (Section 78 and 80). 

 
Obligations of intermediaries under IT Act and IT Rules 
The Government after extensive public consultations with relevant stakeholders has notified 
the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code Rule, 
2021 (“IT Rules”) on 25.02.2021 which were subsequently amended from time -to-time to 
address emerging harms from misuse of technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI). 
The IT Rules require that the intermediaries shall observe due diligence while discharging 
their duties and shall inform the users of computer resources not to host, display, upload, 
modify, publish, transmit, update or share any information that is harmfu l to children or 
violates any law for the time being in force. 
Intermediaries, in cases where the violation involves the commission of an offence under any 
law currently in force —such as the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 read with the Bharatiya 
Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, or the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 
2012, which mandates reporting must report such offence to the appropriate authority in 
accordance with the provisions of the applicable law. 
 
Recent amendments 
The Government regularly engages with relevant stakeholders to examine the legal, policy 
and institutional framework relating to emerging issues in the cyberspace, in light of 
technological developments and public interest. Any legislative or regulatory me asures, if 
considered necessary, are processed in accordance with the extant policy and established 
legislative procedures of the Government. 
On 10th February, 2026, the Government strengthened the regulatory framework by amending 
the IT Rules, 2021 to address harms arising from synthetically generated information (SGI), 
including deepfakes and AI-generated content. 
 
Key points related to the amendment are as follows:- 
● Intermediaries are required to ensure clear labelling and traceable metadata for 
permissible AI -generated content, so that users can easily identify synthetic cally 
generated material and prevent deception or misuse.

QUESTION 
Progress under NESIDS-OTRI 
 
1726. Shri Pratap Chandra Sarangi: 
          Dr. Vinod Kumar Bind: 
          Shri Dilip Saikia: 
 
Will the Minister of DEVELOPMENT OF NORTH EASTERN REGION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of projects sanctioned under North East Special Infrastructure Development 
Scheme - Other Than Roads (NESIDS-OTRI) during each of the last five years and the 
current year, State and sector-wise; 
(b) the details of projects completed and under implementation, indicating the amount 
sanctioned, expenditure incurred and percentage of physical progress thereof; 
(c) the details of infrastructure created under the said Scheme in sectors such as health, 
education, water supply and social infrastructure; and  
(d) the expected impact of these projects on improving socio-economic indicators in the North 
Eastern Region? 
 
ANSWER 
The Minister of State of the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region  
[Dr. Sukanta Majumdar] 
 
(a) to (c) The North East Special Infrastructure Development Scheme (NESIDS) under the 
Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER) was approved as a new Central 
Sector Scheme in 2017-18 and restructured into two components viz. NESIDS (Roads) and 

NESIDS (Other Than Roads Infrastructure) in 2022-23. During the last five financial years 
and current year, i.e, from FY 2021-22 to FY 2026-27 (as on 30.06.2026), a total of 104 
projects costing ₹3,779.49 crore have been sanctioned under NESIDS (OTRI). The state 
wise and sector wise details of the projects sanctioned during the last five financial years and 
current financial year (till 30.06.2026), the amount sanctioned, expenditure incurred and 
physical progress under NESIDS (OTRI), is at Annexure-I. 
(d) The Third Party Evaluation of the NESIDS (OTRI) scheme was carried out by IIM 
Shillong in 2025. The evaluation report states that the NESIDS (OTRI) scheme has brought 
significant and tangible improvements in the lives of intended beneficiaries across the North 
Eastern Region. The Scheme has enabled critical infrastructure development in underserved 
and remote areas, directly addressing long-standing gaps in healthcare, education, water 
supply, power, and digital access. The key areas of impact include improved healthcare 
access, enhanced educational outcomes, reliable access to clean water and electricity, youth 
empowerment through the development of sports infrastructure and enhanced economic 
benefits via increased local employment during construction, better market connectivity, and 
new opportunities in tourism and service sectors.

NATIONAL NUCLEAR MEDICINE EXPANSION PROGRAMME 
1727.   SHRI DHARAMBIR SINGH 
 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:- 
 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any initiative to strengthen the availability of 
nuclear medicine and radioisotope -based diagnostic and therapeutic facilities in 
Government hospitals across the country and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether any roadmap has been prepared for increasing domestic production and timely 
supply of medical radioisotopes and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the steps taken to strengthen training and capacity -building of healthcare professionals 
in nuclear medicine and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether any Government medical institution in the Bhiwani –Mahendragarh Lok Sabha 
Constituency is proposed to be covered under the said initiative and if so, the details 
thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES & PENSIONS 
AND PRIME MINISTER’S OFFICE (DR. JITENDRA SINGH) 
 
(a)  Bhabha Atomic Research Centre ( BARC), a Research & Development  (R&D) unit of 
Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)  is contributing in the field of nuclear medicine 
through its clinical patient services units at Radiation Medicine Centre (RMC), Mumbai 
and Radiation Medicine Research Centre (RMRC), Kolkata for diagnostic and 
therapeutic services for cancer treatment. 
 At Variable Energy Cyclotron Centre ( VECC), a R&D Unit of DAE, the 30 MeV 
medical cyclotron is operated for commercial production of radioisotopes/ 
radiopharmaceuticals for cancer diagnostics. The radioisotopes / radiopharmaceuticals, 
produced at the Medical Cyclotron Facility of VECC, are being delivered on regular 
basis to various hospitals/ Nuclear Medicine Centres.  
Tata Memorial Centre (TMC), an Aided Institute under the administrative control of the 
DAE has established following diagnostic and therapeutic services by utilizing nuclear 
techniques in the fight against cancer: 

 
 
1. Gamma Camera and its associated radiopharmacy lab: 
This Unit is equipped to perform multiple types of functional imaging helping 
with cancer staging with scans such as 99mTc PSMA  (Prostate-specific 
Membrane Antigen) etc. other imaging services help with assessing the function 
such as Multigated Acquisition (MUGA) imaging to assess cardiac function etc. 
 
2. Positron Emission Tomography -Computed Tomography  (PETCT) and its 
radiopharmacy lab: 
This Unit primarily works for cancer staging, most commonly used radioactive 
pharmaceutical is 18F FDG (Fluorodeoxyglucose) which is used in majority of 
cancers for staging such as for evaluation of carcinoma lung, carcinoma 
oesophagus, breast cancer, lymphoma, etc. 
Radioactive Pharmaceuticals such as Ga68 DOTANOC, Ga68 FAPI  - Fibroblast 
Activation Protein Inhibitor  (all prepared and quality checked in house ) are 
utilized for evaluation of various cancers [such as prostate cancer, 
Neuroendocrine Tumors, Mucinous and Signet Gastro intestinal (GI) cancers etc.] 
 
3. High dose Radionuclide therapy ward and its radiopharmacy lab: 
6 bedded high dose therapy ward has been designed as per Atomic Energy 
Regulatory Board ( AERB) guidelines with appropriate layout and provision of a 
delay tank to contain radioactive sewage for proper disposal of contaminated 
patient sewage. 
Iodine-131 (I-131) is utilized for treatment of thyroid cancer, Lutetium-177 (Lu-
177) PSMA and Lu -177 DOTANOC for management of prostate cancer, 
neuroendocrine cancer and other Somatostatin Receptor (SSTR) expressing 
malignancies. 
TMC also works on project conception, development of product for known 
medical and healthcare uses. After development by the laboratory, testing and 
solutions for errors and noncompliance are addressed till the first version is built. 
It is put to field use and tested and subsequent versions are developed. 
 
Example: 
• Development of medical devices like 90Y Bhabhspheres for Trans arterial 
radio embolization: conceived, developed and tested and upgraded by 
Bhabha Atomic Research Centre/Board of Radiation & Isotope 
Technology (BARC/BRIT) & TMC. 
• Development of Blood Irradiator. 

 
 
• Development of Bhabhatron. 
• Development of Radio protectors by BARC, and testing and Drugs 
Controller General of India (DCGI) approval done by TMC. 
 
(b) Currently radioisotopes are produced through research reactors and cyclotrons. 
Radioisotopes like Ruthenium -106, Caesium -137, and Strontium -90 milked into 
Yttrium-90 are recovered through reprocessing of High-Level Liquid Waste (HLLW).  
A dedicated Isotope Production Reactor (IPR) is being constructed for enhancing

†1728. SHRI ARUN KUMAR SAGAR: 
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken or proposes to take steps for the 
renovation, beautification and provision of drinking water and water 
coolers at the platforms of Katra Railway Station and Tilhar Railway 
Station which are in a dilapidated condition under the Shahjahanpur Lok 
Sabha Constituency of Uttar Pradesh and if so, the details thereof;  
(b) whether the Government has received any requests from public 
representatives in this regard and if so, the details thereof; and  
(c) the details of the progress made so far in this regard?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RAILWAYS, INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND 
ELECTRONICS & INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI ASHWINI VAISHNAW) 
 
 
(a) to (c) At  Miranpur Katra station  of Shahjahanpur Lok Sabha 
Constituency, located in Uttar Prade sh, facilities like platform shelter, 
waiting hall, drinking water arrangement, urinal, lavatory, seating 
arrangement, foot over bridge etc. are available. The works of improvement 
of platform, new station building and 3 m wide foot over bridge have been 
recently completed. The work for amenities for Divyangjan has been taken 
up. 
 
At Tilhar station of Shahjahanpur Lok Sabha Constituency, located in Uttar 
Pradesh, facilities like platform shelter, waiting hall, drinking water 

Page 2 of 8 
arrangement, urinal, lavatory, s eating arrangement, foot over bridge etc. 
are available. The work for amenities for Divyangjan has been taken up. 
 
Shahjahanpur station of Shahjahanpur Lok Sabha Constituency, located in 
Uttar Pradesh, has been identified for development under the Amrit Bh arat 
Station Scheme. 
 
At Shahjahanpur station, the works of improvement of platform surface at 
platform no. 1 & 2/3, platform shelter and improvement of station building 
at main entry have been completed. The finishing work of second entry 
station building, improvement of circulating area and foot over bridge have 
been taken up. 
 
Ministry of Railways has launched Amrit Bharat Station Scheme for 
redevelopment of stations with a long-term approach. 
 
This scheme involves preparation of master plans and their implementation 
in phases to improve the stations of Indian Railways. The master planning, 
keeping in view the necessity of each station, includes: 
 
● Improvement of access to station and circulating areas 
● Integration of station with both sides of city 
● Improvement of station building 
● Improvement of waiting halls, toilets, sitting arrangement, water 
booths  
● Provision of wider foot over bridge/subway to commensurate with 
passenger traffic 
● Provision of lifts/escalators/ramps 
● Improvement of platform surface/ provision of platform shelter 

Page 3 of 8 
● Provision of kiosks for local products through schemes like ‘One 
Station One Product’ 
● Parking development 
● Amenities for Divyangjans 
● Better passenger information systems 
● Provision of air concourse, executive lounges, Multimodal inte gration, 
landscaping, etc. 
 
The scheme also envisages sustainable and environment friendly solutions 
etc. as per necessity, phasing and feasibility and creation of city centre at 
the station in the long term. 
 
So far, 1,340 stations have been identified fo r development under this 
scheme, out of which 157 stations,  including Shahjahanpur station of 
Shahjahanpur Lok Sabha Constituency, are located in Uttar Pradesh.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1729 
TO BE ANSWERED ON: 29.07.2026 
 
AI-ENABLED CYBER THREATS 
  
1729. SHRI G M HARISH BALAYOGI: 
  
Will the Minister of ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) the details of Artificial Intelligence (AI) enabled cyber threats including AI-driven malware, 
ransomware and autonomous cyber attack tools identified by the Government; 
(b) whether the Government has assessed risks posed by AI-driven malware, ransomware and 
autonomous attack tools to critical information infrastructure, financial systems and 
Government networks and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the details of existing mechanisms for detection, prevention and response to AI -enabled 
cyber threats; 
(d) the details of capacity -building and cybersecurity preparedness measures undertaken for 
Government agencies and critical sectors to address such threats; 
(e) the details of research, development and deployment of AI -based cybersecurity solutions 
for detection and mitigation of emerging cyber threats; and 
(f) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by the Government to strengthen India's 
preparedness, cyber resilience and incident response capabilities against AI -enabled cyber 
attacks? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (f):   The Government is cognizant of the evolving cyber security threats and challenges, 
including those arising from Artificial Intelligence (AI) enabled cyber threats. AI technologies 
may increase systemic cyber risks by enabling automated reconnaissance, rapi d vulnerability 
exploitation, credential compromise and highly convincing multilingual social engineering 
campaigns. These capabilities lower attack costs, accelerate weaponization, and make phishing 
and impersonation attacks more scalable and difficult to detect. 
 
Government is committed to ensuring an open, safe, trusted and accountable cyberspace. 
Several legal, technical and administrative policy measures have been implemented to address 
the risks posed by AI-enabled cyber threats, enhance cyber resilience, and strengthen incident 
response capabilities, which inter alia include: 
 
1.  AI-driven situational awareness systems are deployed by the Indian Computer 
Emergency Response Team (CERT -In) to detect malicious domains and phishing 
activities for necessary mitigation. 
 

2.   CERT-In has extended AI -enabled vulnerability assessment for public -facing digital 
assets in a sandbox environment to detect and mitigate vulnerabilities. 
 
3.   CERT-In operates an automated cyber threat intelligence exchange platform for sharing 
tailored alerts with organisations across sectors for proactive threat mitigation actions. 
 
4.  CERT -In has conducted 10 tailored cyber security exercises and drills on the theme 
"Building Resilience against Frontier AI-driven Cyber Threats" during June–July 2026. 
These exercises involved 1,470 participants from 345 Government and private 
organisations across sectors such as Power, Telecom, Banking, Financial Services and 
Insurance (BFSI), Transport, Education, Health and Space. 
 
5.  The Certified Security Professional in Artificial Intelligence (CSPAI) program was 
launched by CERT-In and SISA in September 2024. This American National Standards 
Institute (ANSI) National Accreditation Board (ANAB) approved program aims to 
equip cybersec urity professionals with the skills to secure AI systems, proactively 
address AI -related threats, and ensure trustworthy AI deployment in business 
environments. 
 
6.   CERT-In conducts cyber security training programs in collaboration with Industry 
partners to upskill the cyber security workforce in Government, public and private 
sectors. 
 
7.  CERT-In is one of the international partners to co-sign the joint high-level risk analysis 
report on Artificial Intelligence (AI) entitled “Building trust in AI through a cyber-risk-
based approach,” published by the National Cybersecurity Agency for France (ANSSI) 
in February 2025. 
 
8.    Advisories and Guidelines: 
i. CERT-In issues alerts and advisories regarding the latest cyber threats, 
vulnerabilities, and countermeasures to protect computers, networks, and data on 
an ongoing basis. 
ii. CERT-In has issued guidelines in June 2026 requiring all Original Equipment 
Manufacturers (OEMs) and technology providers to implement AI -accelerated 
vulnerability protection, requiring AI -assisted security testing, continuous 
monitoring, patch management,  and incident response frameworks to defend 
against AI-driven cyber threats. 
iii. CERT-In has issued a “Blueprint for Reducing Exposure and Defending against 
AI-Assisted Vulnerabilities Exploitation in Digital Infrastructure” in May 2026, 
aimed at protecting digital infrastructure against rapidly evolving AI-driven cyber 
threats.

and overhead water storage tank have been taken up.

the time frame for such optimization cannot be indicated at this stage.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1734
TO BE ANSWERED ON 29Trl JULY, 2026
RATIONALISATION OF PDS QUOTA
1734 SHRI VIJAYAKUMAR ALIAS VIJAY VASANTH:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether rising food subsidy burden has led to rationalisation of PDS quotas and if so, the details
thereof;
(b) whether fiscal considerations are overriding food security commitments and if so, the details
thereof;
(c) whether the State Governments have sought additional allocation of foodgrains and essential
commodities and if so, the details of requests received, approved and rejected during the last three
years
(d) whether the Government has data on State-wise reduction in PDS allocation of rice and wheat
from the year 2023 to 2026 and if so, the details thereof and reasons for disparities among the
States
(e) whether shortages in pulses, sugar and edible oil under PDS are due to lack of central
procurement policies and if so, the details of the measures taken by the Government to include
these commodities under strengthened distribution framework; and
(f) whether the Government has assessed impact of reduced PDS supply on poor households and
nutritional security and if so, the findings and steps taken by the Government to ensure
uninterrupted supply of essential commodities?
ANSWER
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
(SHRIMATI NIMUBEN JAYANTIBHAI BAMBHANIYA)
(a) to (b): Government is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana
(PMGKAY) which provides food and nutritional security in human life cycle approach, by
ensuring access to adequate quantity of quality food free of cost to people to live a life with dignity.
The PMGKAY is being implemented in all the States/UTs aims to supplement the food
requirements of upto 75% of the rural and upto 50% of the urban population, which at Census 2011
comes to 81.35 crore persons. While Antyodaya Anna Yojana (A AY) households, which constitute
poorest of the poor are entitled to 35 kg of foodgrains, per household per month, Priority
Households (PHH) are entitled to 5 kg of foodgrains per person per month free of cost. The


Coverage under the Act is substantially high to ensure that all the vulnerable and needy sections of
the society get its benefit.
(c) to (d): Allocation of foodgrains to States/Union Territories (UTs) under the PMGKAY is made
on the basis of identification of beneficiaries reported by the States/UTs within the coverage
determined for that State/UT and the foodgrains entitlement of beneficiaries prescribed under the
National Food Security Act, 2013. The Act further provides that if on the above basis, annual
foodgrains allocation to any State/UT is lower than the average annual offtake during 2010-11 to
2012- 13 under erstwhile normal Targeted Public Distribution System, the same shall be protected.
As and when requests are received from States/UTs for revision of foodgrains allocation
under the Act on account of addition of new beneficiaries, within the ceiling of beneficiaries
determined for that State, the same are examined and revised allocation orders are issued as per the
extant policy.
(e): The Public Distribution System is now governed as per the provisions of the National Food
Security Act, 2013. Under the Act, the term “foodgrains” is defined as rice, wheat or coarse grains
or any combination thereof conforming to such quality norms as may be determined, by order, by
the Central Government from time to time.
At present, no proposal for inclusion of more commodities under the scheme is under
consideration of the Government.
(f): in order to improve the level of nutrition, an advisory has been issued to all the States/UTs
to procure millets and distribute them to beneficiaries as per local consumption preferences and as
per guidelines issued by the Central Government from time to time.
Further, in order to improve the nutritional standards in targeted beneficiaries, the
Government has revised the nutritional norms specified in Schedule-11 of the Act, vide notification
dated 25.0 1.2023

UNSTARRED QUESTIQN NO. 1736

SUSPENSION OF FORTIFIED RICE DISTRIBUTION
1736 DR. RAJ KUMAR CHABBEWAL:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the Government has temporarily discontinued the universal distribution of fortified rice
under welfare schemes and if so, the details thereof;
(b) the reasons for the said decision including technical, financial and administrative considerations
for the same;
(c) whether any scientific or expert committee has been constituted to examine alternative methods
of addressing m icronutrient deficiencies and if so, the details thereof;
(d) the details of the quantity of fortified rice presently lying in Government godowns and the
action proposed for its utilisation or disposal; and
(e) whether the Government proposes to review the policy on fortified rice distribution and if so,
the details thereof along with the timeline therefor?
ANSWER
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
(SHRIMATI NIMUBEN JAYANTIBHAI BAMBHANIYA)
(a) to (b): The Government has decided to temporarily discontinue the universal supply of fortified
rice under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojna (Pl\4GKAY) and Other Welfare Scheme
(OWS) of the Government of India, until a more effective mechanism for delivery of nutrients to
beneficiaries is identified.
This decision was necessitated by several factors, including concerns regarding the stability
and shelf life of fortified rice under actual storage conditions. In 2023, a study was commissioned
to the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur to assess the shelf life of Fortified Rice (FR.)
and Fortified Rice Kernels (FRK). The study concluded that parameters such as moisture content,
storage conditions, temperature, relative humidity, and packaging material significantly influence
the stability and shelf life of both FR and FRK.


The findings indicate that fortified rice is susceptible to micronutrient degradation and
reduced shelf life during prolonged storage and routine handling. This degradation shortens the
effective shelf life beyond initial expectations, thereby limiting the intended nutritional benefits.
Given current procurement volumes and annual offtake patterns, rice stocks often remain in buffer
storage for over two years, exacerbating these challenges.
(c): The Department of Food & Public Distribution has not constituted a scientific or expert
committee to examine alternative methods of addressing m icronutrient deficiencies.
However, the Government of India is emphasising enhancing the food basket by providing options
such as Shree Anna or Millets through PDS, as millets are known to have very high nutrient
contents.
(d) and (e): The quantity of fortified rice lying with central pool stock as on 01.07.2026 is 321.11
LMT. Pending receipts, if any, from KIVIS 2024-25 and receivables from KMS 2025-26 will also
form part of the central pool
The policy of distribution of fortified rice under PVIGKY and OWS continues until existing stocks
are exhausted

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF MINES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1738 
ANSWERED ON 29.07.2026 
  
INCENTIVE SCHEME FOR PROMOTION OF CRITICAL MINERAL RECYCLING 
  
1738. SHRI SAUMITRA KHAN: 
SHRI ANURAG SHARMA: 
SMT. D K ARUNA: 
DR. PRASHANT YADAORAO PADOLE: 
  
Will the Minister of MINES be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the details of features, objectives, financial outlay and present status of the 
Incentive Scheme for Promotion of Critical Mineral Recycling under the National 
Critical Mineral Mission including the incentives provided for recovery and recycling of 
critical minerals; 
(b) the details of the number of companies approved or selected under the said 
Scheme so far, indicating the details of proposed recycling capacity, estimated 
investment and employment generation, State-wise, particularly in West Bengal; 
(c) the timelines prescribed for processing applications, approval of projects and 
release of incentives along with the progress made so far in the country especially in 
West Bengal; 
(d) whether the Government has taken measures to encourage participation of Micro, 
Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), start -ups and technology providers in the 
critical mineral recycling eco-system and if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the details of the steps being  taken by the Government to strengthen domestic 
recycling capacity, reduce import dependence on critical minerals and support India's 
clean energy, electric mobility and Atmanirbhar Bharat objectives? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR COAL AND MINES 
(SHRI SATISH CHANDRA DUBEY) 
  
(a) to (c): The ₹1,500 crore Incentive Scheme for Critical Mineral Recycling was 
launched under the National Critical Mineral Mission on 02.10.2025. The Scheme 
incentivizes creation of recycling capacity for the extraction of critical minerals from 
secondary sources like e-waste, spent Lithium-ion batteries (LiBs) and other scrap to 
build supply chain resilience and reduce import dependence in critical minerals.  

The Scheme incentives include capex subsidy on plant & machinery,  equipment and 
associated utilities, as well as opex subsidy upon achievement of specified 
incremental sales threshold. The Scheme is applicable across the country, including 
the State of West Bengal. 
 
The last date for applications under the Scheme was 01 .04.2026. The processing of 
applications received has been completed and 58 recycling entities have been 
declared eligible, with pledged capacity of around 850 kilo tons per annum (KTPA) 
against 270 KTPA target capacity. Incentive under the Scheme is linke d to the 
commencement of commercial production. The State -wise number of eligible entities 
along with details of pledged recycling capacity and investment are at Annexure. 
  
(d) The Scheme encourages participation of small recyclers including Micro, Small and 
Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and start-ups by keeping low requirement of minimum 
threshold capacity and investment along with reduced application fees for them.  
 
(e) To strengthen domestic recycling capacity, the Government has introduced the 
₹1,500 crore Incentive Scheme for Critical Mineral Recycling, as detailed above.  
 
Further, with a view to reduce import dependence on critical minerals and supporting 
India’s clean energy, electric mobility and Atmanirbhar Bharat objectives, the 
Government has amen ded the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) 
(MMDR) Act, 1957 in 2023 to empower the Central Government to auction mineral 
blocks pertaining to critical and strategic minerals and 56 critical mineral blocks have 
been successfully auctioned so far.  
 
Further, the MMDR Amendment Act, 2025 widened the scope of the National Mineral 
Exploration and Development Trust (NMEDT) to facilitate exploration and 
development of minerals within India, including in offshore areas, and outside India. 
NMEDT has issued guidelines to fund Indian entities to explore critical mineral assets 
in foreign jurisdictions for securing long -term mineral supply chains and reducing 
import dependence, and also to explore in offshore areas.

REVISION OF MPLADS 
   
1744. DR. M P ABDUSSAMAD SAMADANI: 
 SHRI KODIKUNNIL SURESH: 
 SHRI SHREYAS M PATEL: 
Will the Minister of STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has received representations from Members of 
Parliament across party lines demanding a upward revision of the annual 
allocation under the Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme 
(MPLADS) from the current Rs. 5 crore per annum to Rs. 15 crore or Rs. 25 
crore per annum and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has evaluated the impact of inflation, escalating 
wholesale price indices of construction materials and the increased cost of 
creating durable community infrastructure on the purchasing power of the 
current allocation which has remained unchanged since the year 2011-12 and 
if so, the details of the assessment thereof a long with the reasons for not 
revising the allocation; 
(c) whether the Government plans to introduce a periodic, inflation -indexed 
mechanism to hike the MPLADS corpus to match local developmental 
requirements; 
(d) whether the Government proposes to revise the operational guidelines of 
MPLADS to improve implementation and utilisation of funds; and  
(e) the details of the action taken or proposed by the Government regarding 
enhancement of the MPLADS allocation and the timeline fixed therefor?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF 
STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION, MINISTER OF STATE 
(INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING AND MINISTER OF 
STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CULTURE [RAO INDERJIT SINGH] 
(a) Yes, Sir. Sugges tions for revision of annual entitlement of MPLADS fund 
were received from Members of Parliament. 

(b) to (e) The primary objective of the Members of Parliament Local Area 
Development Scheme (MPLADS) is to enable each Member of Parliament to 
recommend devel opmental works based on the locally felt needs of the 
people, with emphasis on the creation of durable community assets for the 
larger public good. 
The works permissible under the Scheme span a wide range of sectors, 
including public and community infrastr ucture, public conveniences, safety 
and security, education, public health, drinking water, and sanitation. While 
various Central and State Government Ministries and Departments implement 
sector-specific schemes in these areas, the MPLADS is intended to 
complement such initiatives by addressing locally identified development 
needs, providing last-mile connectivity, and bridging viability gaps, rather than 
replacing or duplicating existing schemes. 
Further, to enhance the coverage and impact of works under t he Scheme in 
line with emerging development needs, the Union Cabinet, while approving the 
continuation of the MPLADS, also approved convergence of MPLADS with more 
number of Central and State Government schemes as well as projects of local 
bodies. This is aimed at facilitating the execution of larger and more impactful 
projects through pooled funding, thereby enhancing the overall effectiveness 
of the Scheme and enabling Members of Parliament to recommend works of 
greater scale and wider public benefit without duplication. 
In order to align the MPLADS Guidelines with the evolving development needs 
of the community and to incorporate the measures approved by the Union 
Cabinet for the continuation of the Scheme from FY 2026 –27 to FY 2030 –31, 
the Ministry is un dertaking a revision of the extant MPLADS Guidelines. The 
revised Guidelines are proposed to incorporate feasible suggestions received 
from various stakeholders, including Hon'ble Members of Parliament, 
wherever these are found to be consistent with the ob jectives of the MPLAD 
Scheme. 
At present, there is no proposal under consideration to introduce a periodic, 
inflation-indexed mechanism to hike the MPLADS funds or enhance the 
MPLADS annual allocation. However, the Ministry receives and examines, on 
a cont inuous basis, the new suggestions from stakeholders, including 
suggestions for revision of entitlement of funds under MPLAD Scheme, 
following due process.
