DELAY IN APPROVAL OF JJM 2.0 
 
1845. SHRI KUNDURU RAGHUVEER: 
Will the Minister of Jal Shakti be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the proposal for Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 has been finalized, if so, the details thereof and 
if not, the reasons for the delay in approving the Mission; 
(b) whether the delay in approving JJM 2.0 allocating funds to States has affected the provision of 
Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTCs) to newly formed households, newly identified habitations 
and uncovered rural families across the country and if so, the details thereof, State-wise; 
(c) whether the Government has conducted any assessment of the number of eligible households awaiting 
coverage due to the non-release of funds and if so, the details thereof, State-wise; 
(d) whether any interim financial a ssistance or special allocation is proposed to ensure that ongoing rural 
drinking water projects are not stalled due to pending approval of JJM 2.0 and if so, the details thereof, and 
(e) the expected timeline for Cabinet approval, release of State -wise allocations and commencement of 
financial assistance under JJM 2.0? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA) 
(a) to (e) Drinking water being a State subject, it is the States, who plan, design, approve and implement 
drinking water supply schemes. Government of India supplements the efforts of the States by providing 
technical and financial assistance. 
In August, 2019, Government of India approved Jal Jeevan Mission to be implemented in partnership with 
States for a period of five years for making provision of tap water supply to every rural household. Recently, 
in March, 2026, Union Cabinet has approved extension of the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) period up to 
December 2028, with an enhanced outlay and a restructured implementation framework focusing on 
structural reforms in the rural drinking water supply sector under JJM 2.0.  
The total outlay of the mission has been increased from Rs 3.60 Lakh crore to Rs. 8.69 lakh crore with 
enhancement of total central assistance from Rs 2.08 lakh crore to Rs 3.59 lakh crore.  
At the time of announcement of the JJM, only 3.23 crore (17%) rural households were reported to have tap 
water connections in the country. So far, as reported by States/ UTs as on 18.07.2026, around 12.66 crore 
additional rural households have been provided with tap water connections. Thus, as on 18.07.2026, out of 
19.36 crore rural households in the country, around 15.89 crore (82.09%) households are reported to have 
tap water connections in their homes.  
Subsequent to the approval of JJM 2.0, state-wise allocations and releases of Central Grants-in-aid under 
JJM 2.0 were initiated in March, 2026 itself.

NO. 1847   MS SAYANI GHOSH: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the recurring floods and 
urban waterlogging in major metropolitan cities during the 
monsoon and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has issued any advisories, guidelines or 
Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to the State Governments 
and Municipal Corporations for urban flood management and if so, 
the details thereof; 
(c) the details of the financial assistance provided by the Government 
for urban flood mitigation, storm -water drainage, flood- resilient

the last five years, city-wise; 
(d) whether the Government has assessed the preparedness and

Governments to strengthen the capacity of Municipal Corporations 
through technical support, funding, training,  early warning 
systems and climate-resilient urban planning?

entries.t: Flight Service between Thiruvananthapuram and Saudi Arabia
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 1849 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  30th July 2026 )  
FLIGHT SERVICE BETWEEN THIRUVANANTHAPURAM AND 
SAUDI ARABIA  
1849.    ADV. ADOOR PRAKASH                       
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has received any proposal or request from the General Authority 
of Civil Aviation (GACA), Kingdom of Saudi Arabia or Saudi Arabian Airlines (SAUDIA) 
for the designation of Thiruvan anthapuram International Airport (TRV) as a Point of Call 
(POC) under the existing India-Saudi Arabia Air Services Agreement; 
 
(b) if so, the details and the present status thereof along with the reasons for the delay in 
granting approval and the expected timeline fixed for its finalisation; 
 
(c) whether granting Thiruvananthapuram as an additional Point of Call would require any 
amendment to the existing bilateral seat entitlement and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d) whether the Government would consid er restoration of direct air services by SAUDIA or 
any eligible Indian carrier between Thiruvananthapuram and Riyadh in view of the 
difficulties faced by expatriates in Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the  Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar 
Mohol) 
(a) to (d) The government has received request for the designation of Thiruvananthapuram 
International Airport (TRV) as a Point of Call (POC) from the General Authority of Civil 
Aviation (GACA), Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. 
 
Presently, the Government of India promotes more international operations from non -metro 
points, including Thiruvananthapuram, by Indian carriers either directly or through their own 
domestic operations. Accordingly, non -metro points, are not being granted as new Point of 
Call in the Air Services Agreements (ASAs) to any foreign carrier including Saudi Carriers. 
 
The international operations of airlines are governed by the bilateral ASA between India and 
the respective country. In accor dance with the ASA, Indian designated carriers are free to 
mount operations to/from any point in India including Thiruvananthapuram to foreign 
destinations such as Riyadh as per mutually agreed capacity limits.  
 

The Government has provided an enabling env ironment for the growth of the civil aviation 
sector but it does not interfere in the operational plans of the airlines. The start of direct 
international flights from any point in India is purely a commercial decision of scheduled 
airlines on the basis of passenger demand, availability of slots, economic viability of the route 
and other associated factors. 
******

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1850 
ANSWERED ON 30TH JULY, 2026

1850. SHRI BHARTRUHARI MAHTAB: 
SHRI BHOJRAJ NAG: 
SHRI JASHUBHAI BHILUBHAI RATHVA: 
SMT. KAMLESH JANGDE: 
SHRI VISHWESHWAR HEGDE KAGERI: 
SHRI ASHISH DUBEY: 
SHRI BALABHADRA MAJHI: 
SHRI DILIP SAIKIA: 
SMT. MALVIKA DEVI: 
SHRI KHAGEN MURMU: 
 
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a)  the progress achieved in enhancing value addition and expanding processing capacity 
in the food processing sector and the status of such initiatives in the country including 
Nabarangpur Lok Sabha Constituency; 
(b)  the details of investments facilitated through various initiatives of the Ministry for the 
establishment, expansion and modernization of food processing units including projects 
undertaken in the country including in Nabarangpur Lok Sabha Constituency of Odisha 
and Chhattisgarh State; 
(c)  the details of the measures taken by the Ministry to promote value-added food products 
including millet-based products and other priority product categories along with the 
initiatives undertaken in the country including Nabarangpur Lok Sabha Constituency 
in this regard; and 
(d)  the details of employment generated along with support extended to Micro, Small and 
Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) under these initiatives including the number of 
beneficiaries and enterprises supported in the country including Nabarangpur Lok 
Sabha Constituency? 
  
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES  
(SHRI CHIRAG PASWAN) 
  
(a) & (b): In order to promote and ensure overall development of Food Processing Industries, 
Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) has been incentivizing setting up/ expansion 
of related infrastructure, through its two Central Sector Schemes viz. Pradhan Mantri Kisan 
SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY), Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing 
Industry (PLISFPI), and a Centrally Sponsored Scheme PM Formalization of Micro Food 

Processing Enterprises (PMFME). These schemes are demand driven and implemented across 
the country including Nabarangpur Lok Sabha Constituency of Odisha and in Chhattisgarh 
State.  
Under PMKSY, financial assistance is provided to entrepreneurs for setting up of food 
processing industries. As on 30.06.2026, 1735 projects have been approved across the country 
with approved grants in aid of Rs 9258.60 crore and private investment of about Rs 23904.74 
crore, out of which 12 projects are located in Chhattisgarh state with approved grants in aid of 
Rs 101.61 crore and private investment of about Rs 222.69 crore. 1256 projects are completed 
/ operational under component schemes of PMKSY which have resulted in creation of about 
241.55 Lakh Metric Tonnes (LMT) of processing capacity per annum across the country, out 
of which 6 projects are in Chhattisgarh state with processing capacity of 1.51 LMT per annum. 
Further, 6 project are located in Nabarangpur Lok Sabha Constituency of Odisha with approved 
grants in aid of Rs 23.62 crore with private investment of about Rs 54.67 crore and all projects 
are completed creating processing capacity of 1.43 LMT per annum. 
 
PLISFPI is targeted to facilitate expansion of food processing capacity by creating 
champion brands in Food Processing Sector. As on 30.06.2026, 163 applications from 127 
companies, at 212 locations have been approved across the country with actual investment of 
Rs. 9207 crore against the target committed investment of Rs.7722 crore, out of which 1 
proposal is located in Chhattisgarh State with actual investment of Rs. 45.14 crore. No project 
under PLISFPI has been approved in Nabarangpur Lok Sabha Constituency of Odisha.  
Under PMFME scheme, financial, technical and business support is provided for setting 
up / upgradation of micro food processing enterprises. As on 30.06.2026, 200421 micro food 
enterprises are approved with credit linked subsidy of Rs 5954.57 crore and private investment 
of about Rs 14480.24 crore across the country, out of which 1941 micro food enterprises are 
approved with credit linked subsidy of Rs 84.04 crore with private investment of Rs 255.79 
crore in Chhattisgarh state. Further, 172 micro food enterprises are approved with credit linked 
subsidy of Rs 9.05 crore and private investment of Rs 31.62 crore in Nabarangpur Lok Sabha 
Constituency of Odisha.  
(c) & (d): In order to promote processing of millets and other priority products, MoFPI through 
its three schemes, extends financial support to prospective entrepreneurs for setting up of 
related industries, as per respective scheme guidelines across the country including 
Nabarangpur Lok Sabha Constituency of Odisha. 
 
A component of PLISFPI scheme is focussed on Millet-Based Products (MBP) with an 
outlay of Rs. 800 crores. The objectives of the PLI Scheme for Millet-Based Products 
(PLISMBP) is

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.1851 
ANSWERED ON 30.07.2026 
 
DESILTATION OF RESERVOIRS UNDER BBMB 
 
1851. SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB) has approved pilot project 
for desiltation of Gobind Sagar (Bhakra Dam) in Himac hal Pradesh, if so, the 
details thereof including the estimated silt removal, project cost and expected 
benefits;  
 
(b) whether project has been delayed following cancellation of tenders due to 
objections raised by State Government of Himachal Pradesh, if so, the details 
thereof;  
 
(c) whether BBMB has assessed the impact of this delay caused by State 
Government on reservoir storage capacity, hydropower generation, irrigation, 
flood moderation, dam safety and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(d) whether BBMB proposes to reissue tenders and take steps to resolve issues 
with State  Government, if so, the details thereof along with the expected 
timeline for commencement of works;  
 
(e) the details of the time -bound sediment management policy for Bhakra & 
Pong dam reservoirs prepared by BBMB; and  
 
(f) the details of coordination with Ministry of Jal Shakti as a part of whole of 
Government approach including any assistance taken by BBMB under DRIP, 
PMKSY for desiltation, reservoir management? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a): Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB) has initiated pilot de -siltation 
projects in the Gobind Sagar Reservoir of Bhakra Dam in Himachal Pradesh at 
two locations, namely Luhnoo Ground, Bilaspu r and Seer Khad. The projects 
envisage the removal of approximately 100 Million Cubic Metres (MCM) of 
sediment over a period of 10 years to improve reservoir operations. The 
projects are proposed to be implemented under a revenue -generation model 
through c ompetitive bidding process, wherein the successful bidder is 
permitted to commercially utilise the excavated material after payment of the 
applicable royalty, taxes, duties, cess and other statutory levies to the 
Government of Himachal Pradesh. 

 
 
(b) to (d)  : BBMB received a Show Cause Notice dated 03.06.2026 from the 
Government of Himachal Pradesh regarding the tenders floated for the de -
siltation work. BBMB submitted its reply on 09.06.2026. However, the project 
has not been delayed on accou nt of the objections raised by the Government 
of Himachal Pradesh. 
 
The tenders invited during March/April 2026 were cancelled due to non -
fulfillment of   prescribed eligibility criteria by bidders. Subsequently, the 
tender for Seer Khad was suitably modif ied and re -issued. The bids were 
opened on 23.07.2026, and three bidders have submitted their proposals. The 
de-siltation work is expected to commence after award of the contract and 
obtaining the requisite statutory clearances from the Government of Himachal 
Pradesh. 
 
(e) :  Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB) has not prepared a separate 
sediment management policy for the Bhakra and Pong Dam reservoirs. 
However, BBMB is undertaking de-siltation on a pilot basis in accordance with 
the National Framework for  Sediment Management (NFSM)  published by the 
Ministry of Jal Shakti. 
 
(f) :  Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB) is participating in the Dam 
Rehabilitation and Improvement Project (DRIP) Phase II & III, a flagship 
programme of the Ministry of Jal Shakti wi th World Bank assistance. In this 
connection, The Geological Survey of India (GSI) has been engaged to identify 
sediment-generation hotspots and undertake landslide susceptibility mapping 
in the catchment area of the Bhakra Dam up to Kol Dam.

TOLL COLLECTION INFRASTRUCTURE IN MAHARASHTRA 
1853. SHRI BHASKAR MURLIDHAR BHAGARE: 
SMT. SUPRIYA SULE: 
DR. AMOL RAMSING KOLHE: 
SHRI MOHITE PATIL DHAIRYASHEEL RAJSINH: 
PROF. VARSHA EKNATH GAIKWAD: 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of recurring complaints from 
commuters in Maharashtra regarding FASTag scanner failures, erroneous 
double-toll deductions and  congestion at major toll plazas on key 
corridors, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether cases of overcharging by unauthorized agents issuing 
FASTags near toll plazas  have been reported in the State, if so, the 
details thereof and the action taken thereon; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to establish a transparent 
grievance redressal  mechanism and compensation framework for 
wrongful toll deductions caused by technical  glitches, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(d) whether any measures are being taken to ensure seamless 
interoperability and integrated  passes for frequently used urban 
transport corridors and bridges in Maharashtra, if so, the details  thereof; 
and 
(e) the steps being taken to modernize toll collection infrastructure and 
reduce delays affecting  private vehicles and State transport buses 
operating across Maharashtra? 
  

2 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) The health of all critical ETC equipment across National Highway fee 
plazas including that in the State of Maharashtra, are monitored through 
Toll Monitoring and Control Centre (TMCC). Additionally, a mechanism 
has been also established for regular coordin ation between System 
Integrators, Banks and fee collecting agencies. The issues at the fee 
plazas are attended based on TMCC Reports and feedback from 
complaint redressal mechanism. 
Further, National Payment Corporation of India (NPCI), which provides 
the Central Clearing House (CCH) services of National Electronic Toll 
Collection (NETC ) Programme, has reported that  only 17.66 lakh 
transactions, where refunds were made due to incorrect User Fee (Toll) 
deductions from January -2025 to December -2025 out of a t otal of 464 
Crore FASTag transactions in the same year which represents 0.03% of 
all FASTag transactions. 
(b) No such complaint has been received in recent times. FASTags are 
issued and sold by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) regulated banks and 
fintech entiti es through Point of Sale (PoS) counters located near fee 
plazas. Additionally, FASTags are also available through online channels 
of certain issuer banks.  
(c) The Government through National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) 
has established multiple grievance redressal mechanism for addressing 
user fee-related issues on National Highways. Complaints can be lodged 
through the National Highways 24×7 Toll -Free Helpline 1033, the 
dedicated email falsededuction@ihmcl.com, the respective FASTag 
issuer bank helplines, as well as through the RajmargYatra App. These 
mechanisms are effective, transparent, and easily acce ssible to road 
users, which also provide information on the action taken.  
Further, any amount deducted erroneously is, on verification, reversed to 
the user account by the concerned Bank. 

3 
 
(d) Nationwide interoperability of FASTag across all fee plazas inc luding 
the State of Maharasthra is ensured through the National Electronic Toll 
Collection (NETC) programme operated on the platform of NPCI, whereby 
a single FASTag is usable across National Highway fee plazas as also on 
State Highways under NETC program. 
(e) To ensure smooth traffic flow and reduce congestion at user fee 
plazas on National Highways, the Government introduced the Radio 
Frequency Identification (RFID) technology through FASTag for making 
payment at fee plaza. The declaration of all lanes of  fee plazas on 
National Highways as FASTag Lane of the fee plaza  has resulted in 
seamless movement at user fee plazas, reduced waiting times, and 
alleviated congestion, thereby improving efficiency at fee plazas on 
National Highways. At present more than 98% of the user fee on National 
Highways/Expressways is collected through FASTag only.  
Apart from this, congestion on fee plaza is also monitored through a GIS -
based toll congestion monitoring solution. 
Further, the Government has decided to implement Mult i Lane Free Flow 
MLFF through Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) with AI 
analytics and RFID -based Electronic Toll Collection (FASTag) which 
facilitates barrier-less tolling, where the user fee shall be charged from 
the vehicle users without having t o stop, slow down or stay in a given 
lane. Multi -Lane Free Flow based barrier less tolling using existing 
FASTag (RFID)+ANPR/AI- Technology has been awarded on 17 fee plazas.

MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES

FUNDS FOR COLD CHAIN INFRASTRUCTURE

Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  the details of funds allocated and utilized for strengthening cold chain infrastructure to 
minimize post-harvest losses; and   
(b)  the details of new initiatives introduced to enhance the income of small and marginal 
farmers through food processing value chains?  
   
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI CHIRAG PASWAN) 
  
(a):  The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) has been implementing Integrated 
Cold Chain & Value Addition Infrastructure scheme (Cold Chain scheme) since 2008. As on 
30.06.2026, under Cold Chain scheme, 409 cold chain projects have been approved nationwide 
with total grants-in-aid of ₹3089.08 crore, of which, ₹2540.89 crore has already been released 
for implementing them, thereby assisting in minimising post-harvest losses of crops.  
  
(b):  MoFPI provides financial assistance for setting up of food processing projects by 
implementing three schemes namely (i) Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY), 
(ii) PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme and (iii) 
Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI) for 
strengthening food processing value chains. These initiatives focus on reducing post-harvest 
losses, increasing value addition, improving market access, and creating better price realization 
for farmers.

Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any asses sment of the 
implementation and impact of the Atal Bhujal Yojana  (ABY) on groundwater 
conservation and sustainable water management in th e country including 
Rajasthan and Durg Lok Sabha Constituency of Chhatt isgarh and if so, the details 
thereof; 
(b) the details of the supply-side structures creat ed or renovated for water 
conservation and groundwater recharge, State and di strict-wise, particularly for 
Maharashtra including Jalgaon Lok Sabha Constituency; 
(c) the details of the improvements observed in the  groundwater levels of the 
identified blocks in the country, particularly for Maharashtra including Jalgaon 
Lok Sabha Constituency; 
(d) the details of the measures undertaken by the G overnment to strengthen 
community participation, awareness towards water co nservation, water 
budgeting and aquifer management under ABY in the c ountry including 
Maharashtra; 
(e) whether Akola district has benefited from groun dwater recharge and water 
conservation initiatives under ABY or any other Cen tral programme and if so, the 
details thereof; 
(f) whether the Government proposes to expand the c overage of ABY to 
additional waterstressed/drought-prone areas includ ing Jalgaon Lok Sabha 
Constituency and Akola district and if so, the details thereof; and 
(g) the details of the progress made under ABY in M adhya Pradesh during the last 
two years? 

3 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 
(a)   Atal Bhujal Yojana, a community-led participatory g roundwater 
management scheme, was implemented on  pilot basis across 8,203 water-
stressed Gram Panchayats in 229 blocks of 80 distri cts in seven States viz. 
Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Mahara shtra, Rajasthan and Uttar 
Pradesh, during the period from 01.04.2020 to 15.10 .2025. The scheme was not 
implemented in the State of Chhattisgarh. 
Overall Impact Assessment Study of Atal Bhujal Yoja na has been conducted 
by Quality Council of India (QCI). On the basis of detailed field surveys in the 
scheme implementation areas and interactions with l ocal communities, the study 
has recognized important changes brought about by t he scheme, like enhanced 
community awareness on ground water issues through capacity building and IEC 
activities, women's participation in leadership and  decision making in 
groundwater management, social inclusivity and over all knowledge enhancement 
and willingness of the community to partake in grou ndwater conservation and 
water management. A copy of this Report is availabl e on the website of 
Department of Water Resources, River Development an d Ganga Rejuvenation at 
web-link:  
https://www.jalshakti-
dowr.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/07/597fd8727a8d10641bd33d7d22ce0459.pdf

conservation and groundwater recharge under the Ata l Bhujal Yojana, State-wise 
and district-wise, are provided at Annexure-I. In M aharashtra, total 11,622 
number of supply side structures created or renovat ed under Atal Bhujal Yojana, 
out of which 589 number of supply side structures are in Jalgaon district. 
  

4 
 
(c)   As per the assessment conducted during 2023 to 2025 , out of 229 Blocks 
covered under the Atal Bhujal Yojana, 180 Blocks ha ve shown improvement in 
ground water levels, list of which is provided at A nnexure II. In Maharashtra, out 
of 43 blocks covered under the Scheme, 39 blocks ha ve shown improvement in 
ground water levels during such assessment. Further , all four blocks, namely, 
Amalner, Parola, Raver and Yawal of Jalgaon Distric t, Maharashtra covered under 
the Scheme have shown improvement in ground water l evels during such 
assessment. 
  
(d)   Community participation forms the cornerstone of th e Government's water 
conservation initiatives. Under Atal Bhujal Yojana,  participatory Water Budgets 
and Water Security Plans have been prepared and upd ated annually by all Gram 
Panchayats, supported by more than 1.28 lakh Gram P anchayat-le

entries.head:
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 1859 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 30th July, 2026 
 
EXPANSION OF CNG AND PNG SERVICES IN UTTAR PRADESH 
 
†1859. SHRI UJJWAL RAMAN SINGH: 
 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũी 
 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has any plan to promote and strengthen Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) 
and Piped Natural Gas (PNG) services in the rural and backward regions of the country, particularly 
in Uttar Pradesh, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the total number of CNG stations and PNG connections proposed to be set up in the rural areas of 
Uttar Pradesh; and 
(c) the steps being taken by the Government to improve the coverage of natural gas infrastructure 
across the country, particularly in Uttar Pradesh? 
ANSWER 
 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũालय मŐ राǛ मंũी 
(ŵी सुरेश गोपी) 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS  
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) to (c): Providing Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connections and establishment of Compressed Natural 
Gas (CNG) stations is part of the development of City Gas Distribution (CGD) Network, which inter 
alia include creation of pipeline infrastructure and other facilities for the supply of PNG to domestic, 
commercial and industrial units and CNG to transport sector is being carried out by the entities 
authorized by Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB). After completion of 12/12A 
CGD bidding round, PNGRB has authorized entities for the development of CGD network in 309 
Geographical Areas (GAs) covering the entire mainland area of the country including rural and 
backward regions. 
PNGRB has authorized 43 GAs (including 1 GA spread over Madhya Pradesh & Uttar Pradesh, 1 
GA spread over Uttarakhand & Uttar Pradesh, 1 GA spread over Bihar & Uttar Pradesh and 1 GA 
spread over Rajasthan & Uttar Pradesh) covering the entire state of Uttar Pradesh (including rural and 
backward areas) for development of CGD network. CGD infrastructure rollout is undertaken by the 
authorized entities in accordance with the authorization granted by PNGRB and the approved project 
plan. As on 31.05.2026, the authorised CGD entities have provided 23,06,333 PNG domestic 
connections and established 1,375 CNG stations in the state of Uttar Pradesh. 

PNGRB, in collaboration with CGD entities, launched the National PNG Drive 2.0 from 1st January 
2026 to 30th June 2026. PNGRB has informed that the initiative aims to ensure optimal utilization of 
existing infrastructure, promote new connections and activate non-billed customers, with an overall 
objective to increase the usage of natural gas across the diverse user categories. Under the initiative, 
various measures have been implemented by the Government and authorized CGD entities, 
including: 
i. Expansion of PNG connectivity to households, commercial establishments and industries; 
ii. Conversion of connected households into active billed consumers; 
iii. Awareness campaigns and consumer outreach programmes; 
iv. Coordination with State Governments and local authorities for expeditious statutory 
permissions; and 
v. Implementation of consumer-friendly measures, including digital registration, simplified 
connection processes and promotional schemes offered by CGD entities. 
The Government has notified a comprehensive control order dated 24.03.2026 under the Essential 
Commodities Act, 1955 to facilitate time-bound expansion of pipeline infrastructure across the 
country, especially CGD. The Order provides a uniform framework for grant of right of way (RoW) 
and permissions by mandating strict timelines, enabling deemed approvals in case of delays, and 
prohibiting imposition of unauthorized charges by public authorities. It also addresses access issues 
in residential and private areas by ensuring non-discriminatory and time-bound permissions, thereby 
removing key bottlenecks in pipeline laying.  
The progress of CGD networks is monitored regularly through reports submitted by CGD entities. In 
cases of delay or shortfall, entities are advised to take corrective measures. This includes convening 
progress review meetings or statutory hearings, as provided under applicable regulations, to discuss 
challenges and review the latest status of Minimum Work Programme (MWP) targets in their 
authorized GAs. Additionally, the Government holds regular interactions and meetings with State 
Governments to support the development of CGD networks in their respective states and to address 
related challenges.

and

created under Phase -I and Phase -II of BharatNet and to create incremental network for new GPs,

applied AI skill development for both students and educators.

Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION

exorbitant airfares on the Sri Vijaya Puram–mainland sectors and if so, the details thereof;

be regulated by the Government.; 
; 
Airlines have the a utonomy to establish airfare based on their operational & economic 
viability on a particular route while adhering to Rule 135 of the Aircraft Rules, 1937.; 
; 
The pricing of airfares is subject to dynamic fluctuations influenced by the fundamental 
economic forces of supply and demand. Various determinants such as current seat occupancy, 
fuel costs, aircraft capacity, seasonal fluctuations and other relevant factors significantly 
impact airline ticket pricing.;

competitiveness, however, it retains vigilant oversight role, intervening in exceptional 

circumstances by redistributing capacity across various sectors and imposing temporary fare 
caps, such as during the Covid Pande mic, festivals like Maha kumb or other extraordinary 
instances like Pahalgam incident & the Indigo flight disruptions.; 
;

free to select whatever markets and netw ork they wish to service & operate with the 
compliance of Route Dispersal Guidelines (RDGs) issued by Government, slot allocation by 
the concerned airport operators and further approval by Directorate General of Civil Aviation

entries.head:
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1862 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 30th JULY, 2026 
 
DOMESTIC OIL AND NATURAL GAS PRODUCTION 
 
1862 THIRU DR. S JAGATHRATCHAKAN:  
 
पेटŌोिलयम एवं Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũी 
 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the implications of crude oil production declining 
for the eleventh consecutive year and natural gas output falling for the second consecutive 
year on the country's energy security, import dependence, energy affordability and 
vulnerability to fluctuations in international energy markets;  
(b) if so, the details of the measures undertaken by the Government to boost domestic 
exploration and production activities, accelerate extraction from discovered reserves, 
encourage investment in upstream projects, improve technological capabilities and reduce 
reliance on imported crude oil and natural gas; and 
(c) the initiatives proposed to be taken by the Government to strengthen long-term energy 
self-reliance, diversify energy sources, enhance domestic production capacity and reduce 
exposure to global supply disruptions, geopolitical uncertainities and price shocks while 
ensuring reliable and affordable energy availability across the country? 
 
ANSWER 
 
पेटŌोिलयम एवं Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũालय मŐ राǛ मंũी 
(ŵी सुर ेश गोपी) 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROELUM & NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
(a) to (c): The Government continuously monitors domestic production of crude oil and 
natural gas and assesses the gap between domestic production and consumption/requirement 
and reviews the supply-demand position.  
 
Domestic oil production over the decade has shown a slight decline in trend primarily owing 
to natural decline in mature and ageing oil and gas fields. However, during this period, 
National Oil Companies (NOCs)—namely Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) Limited 
and Oil India Limited (OIL)—have sustained their production levels. ONGC has maintained 
an average oil production of approximately 19.6 Million Metric Tonnes (MMT), while OIL 
has registered an increase in production from 2.94 MMT to 3.44 MMT. It is pertinent to note 
that the NOCs have been able to contain the annual decline rate to 2% since 2014-15, which 

is superior to the global average decline rate of 6% for mature fields (as per International 
Energy Agency). 
 
Domestic production of Natural Gas has turned around from 2021-22 onwards, largely due to 
new production coming in from deepwater blocks in the Krishna-Godavari (KG) Basin. 
However, natural gas production has declined for two consecutive years, falling to 34.776 
Billion Cubic Metres (BCM) in 2025-26 from a production of 36.438 BCM in 2023-24. 
 
The Government has undertaken a series of comprehensive policy, regulatory and fiscal 
measures to boost domestic crude oil and natural gas production and reduce dependency on 
imports with the objective of strengthening the country’s energy security and reducing 
foreign exchange expenditure through participation by both public and private sector 
companies, which, inter-alia, include reforms include legislative changes through the 
Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment Act, removal of No-Go restrictions in 
the country’s offshore areas, transition from Production Sharing Contracts (PSCs) to Revenue 
Sharing Contracts (RSCs), massive investment in acquisition and processing of seismic data, 
increase in number of exploratory wells drilled etc. During the last decade over 3.5 lakh Sq 
Km of exploration acreages have been awarded.A list of such initiatives is placed at 
Annexure I. 
 
To strengthen energy security and minimise supply risks, India has significantly diversified 
its crude oil sourcing portfolio from 27 countries to 41 countries. Similarly, LNG and LPG 
sourcing has expanded to 15 countries. This diversification has reduced dependence on any 
particular country, region or transit route and enhanced India's ability to manage supply 
disruptions and market volatility. Government, in consultation with Public Sector Oil and Gas 
Companies and other stakeholders, continuously assesses global supply conditions and acts 
appropriately to ensure uninterrupted availability of crude oil, LNG and petroleum products.  
 
Government, through a Special Purpose Vehicle called Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserve 
Limited (ISPRL), have also established Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPR) facilities to act 
as buffer for short-term supply shocks. Under Phase-I, SPRs have been established at 3 
locations in Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka with a total capacity of 5.33 MMT of crude oil. 
As part of Phase II of the SPR program, the Government has approved the establishment of 
two additional commercial-cum-strategic petroleum reserve facilities, with a combined 
storage capacity of 6.5 MMT in Odisha and Karnataka.

TRAINING FOR ARTISANS IN DIGITAL TRANSACTIONS 
 
1864.   MS IQRA CHOUDHARY: 
SHRI BABU SINGH KUSHWAHA: 
SHRI LALJI VERMA: 
SHRI NEERAJ MAURYA: 
MRS RUCHI VIRA: 
 
Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has created any permanent infrastructure scheme for marketing and 
brand promotion of the products made by  the artisans in the industrial and urban areas of Uttar 
Pradesh and if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether any independent social audit has been conducted to assess the actual increase in  
income of the beneficiaries under the said scheme instead of mere ly completing the registration  
figures and if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether any special education or training has been arranged at the local level to make young 
educated artisans proficient in digital transactions and modern business techniques and  if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(d)  whether any social security or pension benefit is proposed to be linked with the above scheme 
to protect the said traditional workers of the unorganized sector from financial insecurity in their old 
age and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a):   PM Vishwakarma  scheme was launched on 17.09.2023 to provide end -to-end holistic 
support to artisans and craftspeople of 18 traditional trades who work with their hands and tool. The 
scheme covers 18 trades, namely: Carpenter, Boat Maker, Armourer, Metal Artisan, Tool Kit Maker, 
Locksmith, Goldsmith, Potter, Sculptor/Stone Worker, Cobbler/Footwear Artisan, Mason, 
Basket/Mat/Broom Maker, Toy Maker (Traditional), Barber, Garland Maker, Washerman, Tailor 
and Fishing Net Maker. Under the scheme, PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries are being provided with

through various e-commerce platforms to promote sale of their products in the domestic as well as 
international markets.  
 
(b): As per the findings of concurrent evaluation of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme conducted by 
IIM Mumbai covering 11,591 beneficiaries across all States and Union Territories and incorporated 
feedback from stakeholders  viz. bank officials, Common Service Centres (CSCs), India Post 
personnel and training centres, 93% reported moderate to significant increase in income following 
training, indicating that acquired skills translated into tangible economic benefits.  
 
 
 

: 2 :

avail of all benefits of the Scheme including Skill upgradation, credit support, modern toolkits,

The beneficiaries are also on -boarded on Udyam Assist Platform to be eligible for availing of

MICRO FOOD PROCESSING ENTERPRISES ASSISTED UNDER PMFME SCHEME 
  
1866. SHRI BHARAT SINGH KUSHWAH: 
  
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of micro food processing enterprises assisted under the Pradhan Mantri 
Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) scheme during the last 
three years and the amount of funds allocated/released, across the country, year-wise and 
States/UT- wise; 
(b) the main objectives, priorities of the said scheme along with the details of loan-based 
financial assistance provided under the scheme, including credit-linked subsidy, seed 
capital, branding, marketing, training and capacity-building support to beneficiaries, 
employment generation, enterprise formalization, value addition in the food processing 
sector and support for common infrastructure; 
(c) the categories of beneficiaries to which benefit is provided such as individual micro food 
processing units, self-help groups, farmer producer organizations and cooperative 
committees along with their eligibility therefor; and 
(d) the number of beneficiaries who have availed the benefits of the scheme so far along with 
the details of the sanctioned loan, subsidy and other financial assistance across the country, 
State/UT-wise? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI CHIRAG PASWAN) 
  
(a): Under the Pradhan Mantri Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) 
scheme, loans for 1,62,044 Micro food processing enterprises have been sanctioned under Credit 
Linked Subsidy and Centre Share of Rs. 3366.24 crore has been allocated/ released across the 
country during the last three years. The Year-wise and State/ UT wise details are at Annexure I.  
(b) & (c): The PMFME Scheme is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme being implemented to provide 
financial, technical and business support for setting up of new/ upgradation of micro food 
processing enterprises in the country. The objectives of the scheme are to build capacity of micro 
enterprises through increased access to credit, integration with organized supply chain by 
strengthening branding and marketing, increased access to common services, strengthening of 
institutions and research & training in the food processing sector.  
  

  The Scheme provides 35% credit-linked capital subsidy to eligible micro food processing 
enterprises, Seed Capital support to Self Help Group (SHG) members, Capacity Building 
through Entrepreneurship Development Programmes (EDP) and product-specific training, 
assistance for Branding & Marketing and support for Common Infrastructure such as 
processing, storage, packaging, testing and incubation facilities. The details of financial 
assistance available under various components of the Scheme, including the eligible entities, 
are at Annexure-II. 
  
The Scheme further promotes value addition of agricultural produce by strengthening 
district-specific food processing value chains, facilitating technology adoption, improving 
market access through linkages with retail, e-commerce and institutional buyers and creating 
shared infrastructure for aggregation and processing. These interventions contribute to 
enterprise formalisation, entrepreneurship development and generation of direct and indirect 
employment opportunities.

Linked Subsidy along with subsidy approved and Seed capital assistance is at Annexure III.

be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has received complaints regarding 
technical issues in the Parivahan Checkpost Portal affecting the 
payment of inter -State border taxes by commercial vehicle 
operators and if so, the details thereof; 
  
(b) whether the Government has undertaken any review of the 
functioning, uptime and grievance redressal mechanism of the 
Portal and if so, the details and outcome thereof; 
  
(c) whether the Government proposes to provide any relief including 
waiver of penalties or other remedial measures in cases where 
delayed tax payment occurred due to technical issues in the Portal

operators?  
  
  
  

ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
 
(a) to (d)     National Informatics Centre(NIC), in its capacity as a 
service provider to State/UT Governments, is facilitating the 
collection of motor vehicle tax through the Parivahan Checkpost 
portal to facilitate inter -State movement of commercial vehicl es. 
The owners of eligible commercial vehicles may access the portal 
and deposit their due motor vehicle taxes to the concerned 
State/UT Government account through net banking facility. The 
portal provides facility of digital payments to the users. 
  To check the authenticity of receipt, the transport departments 
may cross -check the payment details by logging on to the portal. 
They can also view / print various reports which will be generated 
for officials of the transport department. Online payment se rvices 
have been availed by users from 17 States through the Checkpost 
Portal.    
   The State/UT Governments onboarded on the portal through NIC 
periodically monitor and review the functioning of the Parivahan 
Checkpost Portal to ensure its efficient, rel iable and seamless 
operation. The review includes monitoring of system availability and 
performance, analysis of transaction success rates, assessment of 
user feedback and evaluation of technical and operational aspects. 
Based on such reviews, necessary co rrective and preventive 
measures are undertaken from time to time, including infrastructure 
augmentation, software enhancements, optimization of system 
performance, strengthening of security measures and improvement 
of the user support and grievance redressal mechanism. 
 NIC has informed that various measures to strengthen the 
reliability, accessibility and seamless functioning of the Portal for 
commercial vehicle operators are being taken, including : 
 Periodic upgradation of hardware and software infrastru cture 
to enhance system stability and performance.  

 Implementation of robust security measures, including regular 
security audits and vulnerability assessments.  
 Establishment of a  E-Transport helpdesk and grievance 
redressal mechanism to provide timely assistance to users.  
 Continuous monitoring and optimization of system capacity to 
handle peak transaction volumes.

SHRI G M HARISH BALAYOGI: 
SHRI MAHENDRA SINGH SOLANKY: 
SHRI SATISH KUMAR GAUTAM:

DR. SANJAY JAISWAL: 
SHRI DAMODAR AGRAWAL: 
SHRI P P CHAUDHARY: 
 
Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has taken any measures including constituency-focused initiatives 
to promote the livelihood, entrepreneurship and sustainable development of artisans, traditional 
craftsmen, women, youth, self-help groups, tribal handicraft and entrepreneurs across the country and 
if so, the details thereof, State/UT-wise; 
(b) the details of achievements, the number of beneficiaries covered and the amount sanctioned 
under the Pradhan Mantri Vishwakarma Scheme (PMVS), Prime Minister’s Employment Generation 
Programme (PMEGP), Scheme of Fund for Reg eneration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI) and 
other Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) schemes in the country, State/UT and district-
wise; 
(c)  the details of skill upgradation, entrepreneurship training, design intervention, technology 
support and capacity -building programmes conducted/implemented for artisans and craftspeople 
during the last three years across the country, State/UT and district-wise; 
(d)  the financial assistance, credit support, subsidies and market -linkage facilities provide d to 
them for livelihood generation during the last three years across the country, year, scheme, State/UT 
and district-wise; 
(e)  the details of the measures taken by the Government for the digital enablement including 
digital payments, e -commerce onboard ing/integration, branding, GeM registration, UPI -enabled 
transactions and online marketing of local products of the beneficiaries, State/UT-wise; and 
(f)  the details of the beneficiary coverage achieved under such schemes and incentive 
programmes across the country during the last three years, year, scheme, State/UT and district-wise? 
 
 
 
 

 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a):  Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) has launched a Central Sector 
scheme named PM Vishwakarma scheme on 17.09.2023. The scheme provides end-to-end holistic 
support to artisans and craftspeople across India, including women, youth and tribal areas to promote 
empowerment, livelihood, entrepreneurship and sustainable development. The scheme covers 18 
trades, namely: Carpenter, Boat Maker, Armourer, Metal Caster, Tool Kit Maker, Locksmith, 
Goldsmith, Potter, Sculptor/Stone Worker, Cobbler/Foo twear Artisan, Mason, Basket/Mat/Broom 
Maker, Toy Maker (Traditional), Barber, Garland Maker, Washerman, Tailor and Fishing Net Maker.  
(b):  The details of achievements and the number of beneficiaries covered under PM Vishwakarma, 
Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), Scheme of Fund for Regeneration 
of Traditional Industries (SFURTI) are at Annexure-I, II and III respectively. 
 
(c) to (f):   Details of Successfully Registered Artisans, Basic Skill Training, Loans Sanctioned, 
Toolkit Delivered and beneficiaries received Digital Incentive, under the PM Vishwakarma scheme 
since its inception is at Annexure-I. 
 
Under PM Vishwakarma scheme, various measures have been initiated by Ministry of MSME 
to onboard registered beneficiaries under the digital ecosystem. MoUs have been signed with Digital 
Payment Aggregators (DPAs); India Post Payment Bank, Paytm, Paynearby, BharatPe and PhonePe 
for generating QR codes to enable beneficia ries for receiving Digital Payment Incentives.  Also, 
online marketing support is being provided to PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries through various e -
commerce platforms to promote sale of their products in the domestic as well as international markets. 
Over 30,000 Vishwakarma beneficiaries have been successfully onboarded on the Government e -
Marketplace (GeM), enhancing their access to institutional buyers.

NO. 1869 DR. BHOLA SINGH: 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of beneficiaries assisted under the PM Street Vendor's 
AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM -SVANidhi) Scheme during the last three 
years, State/UT-wise; 
(b) the number of loans sanctioned and disbursed and beneficiaries 
receiving digital transaction incentives under the PM -SVANidhi 
Scheme, State/UT-wise; 
(c) the number of beneficiaries covered under the PM-SVANidhi Scheme 
in Uttar Pradesh, including Bulandshahr district, Urban Local Body -
wise; 
(d) whether the Government has assessed the impact of the PM -
SVANidhi Scheme on access to institutional credit and livelihoods 
of street vendors; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof along with the steps taken to expand 
coverage among eligible but uncovered street vendors? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
 MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a): PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) scheme was 
launched on 1st June 2020.  Under the scheme, till 12th July 2026, 76.95 
lakhs street vendor have availed 1.15 crore loans amounting to 
₹18475.06 Crore.  State/UT wise number of beneficiaries under the 
scheme during last 3 years is provided in Annexure. 
 
(b): As on 12th July, 2026, total 1,17,64,812 loans have been sanctioned, 
1,15,15,856 loans have been disbursed and 56,18,024 beneficiaries are 
digitally active under the PM SVANidhi Scheme.  State-wise details are 
available on PM SVANidhi portal https://pmsvanidhi.mohua.gov.in 
…2/- 

-2- 
(c): As on 12 th July 2026, 15,63,460 street vendor  beneficiaries have 
availed loans under the scheme in the state of Uttar Pradesh. 
As on 12 th July 2026, 26,383 street vendor  beneficiaries have availed 
loans in Bulandshahr district under the scheme. Urban Local Body wise 
details are available on PM SVANidhi portal 
https://pmsvanidhi.mohua.gov.in 
(d) & (e): Yes. Impact assessment studies of the PM SVANidhi scheme 
was undertaken by Indian School of Business (ISB), Hyderabad in 2023 
& 2025. The 2023 study was conducted in 100 Urban Local Bodies 
(ULBs) across the country covering more than 5,000 beneficiaries and 
it found that PM SVANidhi was the first loan from a bank for 95% of the 
beneficiaries. The 2025 study was conducted in 99 Urban Local Bodies 
(ULBs) across the country covering more than 5,000 beneficiaries (with 
around 60% of the respondents being part of the 2023 study sample) 
and it found that the average annualized business income among 
SVANidhi borrowers grew by around 20 percent, between 2023 and 
2025.  
Around 30 percent of borrowers across all cycles reported holding loans 
other than PM SVANidhi loans which underscores the scheme’s role in 
building credit histories for vendors who previously had little or no 
access to formal credit. 
The study also found the scheme’s impact extends well beyond 
business recovery. By easing credit constraints and stabilizing 
household cash flows, the scheme has enabled vendor families to 
improve living conditions, strengthen food security, enhance access to 
health-care, and support children’s education. 
The PM SVANidhi Scheme was initially implemented in statutory urban 
areas. The eligibility was also extended to street vendors from 
surrounding peri-urban areas who vend within the geographical limits 
of Urban Local Bodies (ULBs). Under the restructured PM SVANidhi 
Scheme, the coverage of the Scheme is expanded beyond statutory 
urban areas to include census towns, peri urban areas etc in a graded 
manner.

ROLLOUT OF E-25 PETROL 
 
1870. COM. SELVARAJ V: 
          SHRI SUBBARAYAN K: 
 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğी 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is considering a proposal to roll out petrol blended with twenty- 
five per cent ethanol, if so, the details thereof; and 
(b)  whether there is growing concern over the impact of E-20 petrol on vehicle mileage and 
performance, if so, the details thereof and the reaction of the Government thereto? 
 
ANSWER 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğालय मɅ राÏय मंğी 
(Įी सुरेश गोपी) 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS  
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) :  So far, no decision has been taken by the Government for increasing ethanol blending with 
petrol beyond 20%. Any future decision regarding higher ethanol blends will be taken only after 
detailed scientific and technical studies and consultations with all relevant stakeholders, including 
automobile manufacturers, Oil Marketing Companies and research institutions. 
(b): The Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme has been implemented through a phased, 
scientifically validated and consultative process involving NITI Aayog, automobile manufacturers, 
Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI), Society of 
Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), Indian Institute of Petroleum (IIP) and other technical 
institutions. 
Extensive laboratory studies and field trials conducted by ARAI, SIAM, IOCL, IIP and automobile 
manufacturers covering parameters such as engine durability, drivability, startability, corrosion 
resistance, material compatibility, emissions and fuel efficiency have confirmed that E20 is safe for 
use under prescribed standards. 
These studies also established that legacy vehicles do not exhibit any significant variation in 
performance or abnormal wear and tear due to E20. These extensive laboratory studies, field 
validation and real-world operating experience have not established any widespread adverse impact 
on vehicle performance due to E20 fuel. 
With regard to mileage, studies by Government agencies and automobile manufacturers indicate that 
fuel efficiency is influenced by several factors, including driving conditions, driving habits and 
vehicle maintenance. Any reduction in fuel economy in certain E10-designed vehicles is generally 

limited to about 3-5%, while E20 offers a higher-octane rating, superior anti-knock characteristics, 
cleaner combustion and smoother engine performance. 
According to SIAM and ARAI, E20 improves acceleration and ride quality while reducing carbon 
emissions. Ethanol's higher-octane number supports modern high-compression engines and its 
higher heat of vaporisation improves combustion efficiency. 
Public awareness initiatives are also undertaken to educate consumers about the technical 
compatibility of E20 fuel with all petrol vehicles without any performance issue and the 
environmental and energy security benefits of ethanol blending. Consumer feedback received 
through the grievance redressal mechanisms is regularly monitored by the OMCs, and appropriate 
corrective measures are taken wherever required to ensure consumer confidence while advancing the 
Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme.

1871.   SHRI ANUP SANJAY DHOTRE: 
  
Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the details of beneficiaries under the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme 
(PMEGP), Credit Guarantee Scheme (CGS), Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) 
Champions and Raising and  Accelerating MSME Performance (RAMP) during the last three years, 
scheme-wise and State-wise particularly district-wise in Maharashtra; 
 
(b) the details of collateral -free loans sanctioned under the Credit Guarantee Scheme to  Micro, 
Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Maharashtra, including Akola district,  indicating the 
number of beneficiary enterprises and the total amount disbursed during the said period; 
 
(c) the present status of implementation of initiatives such as enhanced Mudra loan limits, Trade 
Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) onboarding, Small Industries Development Bank of India 
(SIDBI) support, Food Irradiation and Quality Testing Units and e -Commerce Export Hubs in

(d) the details of measures taken to promote procurement, exports and market access for MSMEs 
in Maharashtra, including the benefits extended to MSMEs in Akola district during the last three

MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDMUM ENTERPRISES 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a): Ministry of MSME implements the Credit Guarantee Scheme (CGS) for Micro and Small 
Enterprises through the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE), 
the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEG P) through the Khadi and Village 
Industries Commission (KVIC), the MSME Champions Scheme, and the Raising and Accelerating 
MSME Performance (RAMP) Programme, across the country, including in the State of Maharashtra. 
The details of beneficiaries State-wise and also district-wise in Maharashtra is given in Annexure-I. 
  
(b): The district -wise details of collateral -free credit guarantees extended under CGS -MSE in 
Maharashtra during the last three years are given at Annexure-I. 
  
(c):  The status of Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) , in the state of Maharashtra including 
Akola district is given in Annexure-II.  
  
 
 
 

: 2 : 
 
 
The Government vide notification dated 07.11.2024 has directed Central Public Sector 
Enterprises (CPSEs) and all companies with the turnover of Rs. 250 Crore or more to on -board the 
Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS), an electronic platform for f acilitating the 
discounting of trade receivables of MSMEs through multiple financiers. Ministry of Micro, Small 
and Medium Enterprises (MSME) has issued a notification on June 30, 2026, mandating all the 
CPSEs to on board on any one of the TReDs platforms.  
 
As part of supporting the growth of lending to MSMEs by SIDBI, the Union Cabinet 
approved an equity infusion of ₹5,000 crore into SIDBI in three tranches. The first tranche of ₹3,000 
crore was released to SIDBI in March 2026, strengthening its capital b ase and enabling it to sustain 
credit growth while complying with regulatory capital requirements. 
 
As regards Food Irradition Unit, at present, no project has been approved in Akola,

ii.  The Ministry has established 65 Export Facilitation Centers (EFCs) in its field offices

mentoring and handholding support to MSMEs in exporting their products and services. 
Details of EFCs in Maharashtra and their functions is given at Annexure-III.  
 
iii.  Procurement and Marketing Support (PMS) Scheme provides financial assistance to MSEs

Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

section of National Highway (NH) -69 (old NH -206), including the total

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1873 
ANSWERED ON 30TH JULY, 2026 
  
DEVELOPMENT OF FOUR-LANE HIGHWAY 
  
1873. SHRI KULDEEP INDORA: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री  
be pleased to state:  
  
(a)  whether the Government has assessed the necessity and 
feasibility of declaring the Sirsa -Rania-Tibbi-Hanumangarh route as 
a National Highway and developing it into a four -lane highway and if 
so, the details thereof; 
 
(b)  whether the Government has evaluated that developing the 
said route into a National  Highway is likely to provide direct and 
improved road connectivity from Sri Ganganagar and  Hanumangarh 
to Delhi thereby benefitting national security, border  area 
connectivity, farmers,  traders and industries while also reducing 
freight transportation costs and boosting regional  economic 
development, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c)  whether the Government is contemplating upon declaring this 
route as a Nation al Highway  and developing it into a four -lane 
highway, if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d)  if not, whether there is any proposal to conduct a survey or a 
feasibility study in this regard  in the near future, if so, the details 
thereof? 
 
  

ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
 
(a) to (d)  State roads, including State Highways (SHs), are 
declared as National Highways (NHs) from time to time on the basis 
of well-established broad principles. Government receives proposals 
from various State Governments/Union Territories (UTs) from time to 
time, for declaration / upgradation of State roads, including SHs, as 
new NHs. Decisions are taken based on the broad principles of 
declaration of NHs, requir ement of connectivity, traffic density and 
synergy with PM GatiShakti National Master Plan (NMP). 
No proposal for declaration of Sirsa-Rania-Tibbi-Hanumangarh 
route as a National Highway or assessment of its feasibility is under 
consideration.

†1874. SHRI BABU SINGH KUSHWAHA: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware that despite laying of pipelines under Jal Jeevan Mission 
(JJM), regular drinking water supply has not been started in several villages of Jaunpur Lok 
Sabha Constituency in Uttar Pradesh and i f so, the details thereof along with the details of 
villages selected and progress made under the first, second and third phases of JJM; 
(b) the number of villages where works have been completed under the first phase and the 
number of villages where regular drinking water supply is being provided to every household 
through Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTCs); 
(c) the list of villages having hundred per cent FHTCs and regular water supply; 
(d) whether the roads damaged due to pipeline laying works have been repaired in a timely

and financial assistance. The Union Cabinet has approved extension of the Jal Jeevan Mission 
(JJM), with an enhanced outlay and a restructured implementation framework focusing on 
structural reforms in the rural drinking water supply sector under JJM 2.0. 
State of Uttar Pradesh has informed that in Jaunpur Lok Sabha Constituency, 690 number of 
Water supply schemes covering 1,723 villages are implemented under Jal Jeevan Mission. 
Further details regarding  Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTCs) are  available in 
public domain at https://ejalshakti.gov.in/jjmreport/JJMState.aspx.

Sabha Constituency, where regular water is supplied through these schemes. 
(c) The details of villages having hundred per cent FHTCs and regular water supply i. e. Har 
Ghar Jal Reported, are available  in public domain  at

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1876 
ANSWERED ON 30TH JULY, 2026 
 
FARM-TO-MARKET VALUE CHAIN INTEGRATION 
1876. SHRI BAIJAYANT PANDA: 
    
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether any assessment has been undertaken to identify gaps in farm-to-market 
value chain integration and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether priority commodities have been identified and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether new policy instruments are proposed to strengthen value chains; and  
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI CHIRAG PASWAN) 
(a): Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) has conducted various studies to 
estimate the processing level for selected commodities to determine the post-harvest losses and 
to evaluate implementation and impact of its ongoing schemes. However, so far, MoFPI has 
not undertaken any assessment specifically to identify the gaps in value chain integration.   
(b): Under the Central Sector umbrella scheme of MoFPI- Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada 
Yojana (PMKSY), the Operation Greens Scheme was launched in 2018-19 with an outlay of 
₹500 crore for the value chain development of Tomatoes, Onions and Potatoes (TOP) to 
promote FPOs, agri-logistics, processing facilities and professional management. In 2021-22, 
its scope was expanded to cover 22 perishable crops.  
Under the Scheme's long-term interventions, a financial assistance in the form of 35% 
of the eligible project cost in General Areas and 50% in Difficult Areas and for SC/ST 
promoters, FPOs and SHGs is provided for value chain development projects, subject to a 
maximum grant of ₹15 crore per project. The Scheme is demand-driven in nature with projects 
selected through Expressions of Interest (EOI) from time to time. So far, Ministry has approved 
36 projects in the country with total project cost of Rs. 1466.74 Crore, approved grant-in-aid 
of Rs. 376.81 Crore. The 22 perishables crops selected under the schemes are as below: 
  
i. Fruits: Mango, Banana, Apple, Pineapple, Orange, Grapes, 
Aonla/Amla, Pomegranate, Guava, Litchi; 
ii. Vegetables: Tomato, Onion, Potato, Green Peas, Carrot, Cauliflower, 
Beans, Gourd Family [Bottle Gourd (Loki), Bitter Gourd (Karela), 

Ridge/Sponge Gourd (Torai), Pointed Gourd (Parwal) and Ash Gourd 
(Petha)], Okra, Garlic, Ginger; 
iii. Marine: Shrimp 
 
(c) & (d):  MoFPI through implementation of various initiatives and schemes viz. Pradhan 
Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY), Prime Minister Formalization of Micro Food 
Processing Enterprises (PMFME) and Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food 
Processing Industries (PLISFPI) strengthen food processing value chains across the country 
through the creation of modern processing and preservation infrastructure, cold chain and 
logistics facilities, value addition, market linkages, formalisation of micro enterprises and 
promotion of innovation and investment in the food processing sector. As on date, no specific 
new policy instrument is proposed to strengthen the value chains. However, the Government 
continuously reviews the existing policy framework to introduce suitable interventions from 
time to time for the overall development of food processing sector across the country. 
*****

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 1877 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  30th July 2026 )  
DEVELOPMENT OF MAHARAJA AGRASEN AIRPORT  
1877.    SHRI DEEPENDER SINGH HOODA      
          
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) the present status of Phase -l and Phase-Il development of Maharaja Agrasen 
Airport, Hisar including the details of the Detailed Project Report (DPR), 
project cost, funds sanctioned, released and utilised and the timeline fixed for 
completion of the project; 
(b) whether the Government proposes to develop the airport as an international 
passenger, cargo and Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) hub; 
(c) if so, the details thereof along with the timeline fixed in this regard  and if 
not, the reasons therefor; and 
(d) the number of routes approved and operational under the UDAN Scheme 
from Hisar Airport along with the passenger traffic handled since the 
commencement of operations and the details of employment generated and 
investments attracted in the surrounding region? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (c): Phase -I of the development of Hisar Airport was executed and 
completed by the Public Works Department (PWD), Government of Haryana.  
 
Phase-II of the project has been undertaken by the Airports Authority of India 
(AAI) as a deposit work under a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with 
the Government of Haryana. The project involves the development of an 
Integrated A viation Hub at Hisar, including the construction of a Passenger 
Terminal Building, ATC Tower -cum-Technical Block, Cargo Building and 
other associated infrastructure, at an estimated cost of Rs. 560.00 crore 
(excluding GST). A total of Rs. 262.00 crore has been released, out of which 
Rs. 98.82 crore has been utilized. The Projected Date of Completion (PDC) of 
the project is December 2027. However, the timeline for completion of the 
airport projects depends upon many factors such as land acquisition, availability 
of mandatory clearances, financial closure etc. 

 
(d): Hisar Airport was identified under the Regional Connectivity Scheme 
(RCS)-UDAN during the second round of bidding. Under the scheme, RCS 
routes connecting Hisar with Dehradun, Chandigarh, and Dhar amshala were 
operationalized. A new phase of the UDAN Scheme was launched on 4 July 
2026 with the objective of connecting 120 new destinations and benefiting 4 
crore passengers across the country, including those in the State of Haryana. 
 
The passenger tr affic handled since the commencement of operations in 2 025-
26 is approximately 10,000. 
 
As per an ICAO study - "Economic benefits of civil aviation: ripples of 
prosperity", the output and employment multipliers of aviation are 3.25 and 6.10 
respectively.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA

IDENTIFICATION AND RECTIFICATION OF BLACK SPOTS 
  
1878. SHRI LAVU SRI KRISHNA DEVARAYALU: 
          DR. KADIYAM KAVYA: 
          SHRI MURARI LAL MEENA: 
          DR. M K VISHNU PRASAD: 
 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the details of accident-causing black spots identified on National 
Highways (NHs) in the country, State/UT -wise including the NHs 
passing through Warangal in Telangana and Palnadu in Andhra 
Pradesh indicating the location, NH number and the present status 
of each black spot thereof; 
(b) the corrective measures sanctioned and undertaken including 
the project -wise details of the number of flyovers, underpasses, 
interchanges or other road safety works sanctioned so far for the 
rectification of the said black s pots including the number of works 
for which tenders have been issued, the number of works currently 
under construction and the number of works already completed for 
the rectification of such black spots in the said areas; 
  
(c) the estimated cost, sanctio ned amount, executing agency, 
physical and financial progress achieved and the stipulated timeline 
for completion of construction work for each sanctioned 
project/remaining works in the country, State -wise including said 
areas and the reduction in accident  rates after completion of 
rectification works; and 
  

(d) whether the Government proposes to sanction additional 
projects for the time-bound elimination of the remaining black spots 
and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) Certain continuous stretches on National Highways (NHs) have 
been identified qualifying the criteria of black spots i.e. locations 
with occurrence of certain number of accidents involving fatalities 
and grievous injuries. These stretches have been iden tified on real -
time basis through AI based tools developed by Indian Institute of 
Technology (IIT), Kanpur. Based on the available accident data from 
Electronic Detailed Accident Report (e -DAR) for the period 2023 –
2025, 6,358 Black spot corridors have been  identified. The State -
wise details are placed at Annexure -I. Further, the list of the black 
corridors passing through Warangal in Telangana and Palnadu in 
Andhra Pradesh are placed at Annexure-II. 
  
(b) to (d) Rectification of black spots is a continuous process. Short-
term measures for immediate rectification of black corridors include 
road markings, signages, crash barriers, road studs, delineators, 
closure of unauthorized median openings, traffic calming measures, 
highway lighting etc. Long -term measures for rectification of black 
corridors like improvement of road geometrics, junction 
improvements, spot widening of carriageway, construction of 
underpasses/overpasses, etc. are also taken as permanent 
rectification measures as per site requirement. Long t erm 
rectification works involve pre -construction activities such as land 
acquisition, forest clearance & utility shifting which takes 
significant time. 

No separate allocation of funds is made for rectification works on 
road accident black spots which are e xecuted either as part of on -
going NH development works or on standalone basis. However, 
State/UT- wise details of funds allocated and expenditure incurred 
towards development and maintenance of NHs during each of the 
last five years and the current year are placed at Annexure-III.

PROGRESS UNDER PM-JANMAN 
  
1879. DR. VINOD KUMAR BIND: 
          SHRI PRATAP CHANDRA SARANGI: 
          SHRI HASMUKHBHAI SOMABHAI PATEL: 
          SHRI DHAVAL LAXMANBHAI PATEL: 
Will the Minister of Tribal Affairs be pleased to state:  
(a) the progress made under the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha 
Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) for the development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal 
Groups (PVTGs) across the country, State/UT-wise; 
 (b) the details of interventions undertaken under the Mission in the areas of housing, 
health, education, drinking water, road connectivity and sustainable livelihoods for 
PVTG habitations in the country, State/UT-wise particularly the tribal regions of 
South Gujarat; 
(c) whether the Government has identified any additional PVTG habitations for 
coverage under PM-JANMAN in the country including Gujarat and if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(d) the progress made since the launch of PM-JANMAN Scheme in implementation 
of infrastructure and basic service delivery projects under the Mission and the impact 
thereof on the socio-economic development of PVTGs including the number of 
beneficiaries covered, State/UT wise?  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI DURGADAS UIKEY) 
  
(a)  to (d): Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN) 
was launched by the Hon'ble Prime Minister on 15th November, 2023 for the socio-

economic development of the 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) 
communities residing in 18 States including Gujarat and one Union Territory. 
  
The mission aims to provide basic facilities to improve their socio-economic 
conditions such as safe housing, clean drinking water and improved access to 
education, health and nutrition, road and telecom connectivity, electrification of 
unelectrified households and sustainable livelihood opportunities. These objectives 
are being met through 11 interventions implemented by 9-line Ministries. The details 
of the benefits given under PM JANMAN, as on 30.06.2026, Ministry-wise & State-
wise and District-wise in Gujarat, are given at Annexure I. The progress so made 
under the abhiyan has contributed to the socio-economic development of PVTGs 
through improvement in basic amenities and livelihood opportunities.  
  
  
Ministry of Tribal Affairs through the State Governments/UT 
Administration/departments has undertaken habitation level data collection exercise 
through PM Gati Shakti mobile application to estimate PVTG population figures and 
infrastructure gaps in order to cover PVTG population residing in villages & 
habitations covered under PM JANMAN. Based on the data captured, State/UT- 
wise, PVTG villages, habitations and population is tabulated at Annexure II. The 
actual number beneficiaries to be covered under the abhiyan is subjected to 
eligibility criteria of specific guidelines of concerned interventions as per norms 
approved.
